### REG-3794 - NOTHING EVER RE-ASKED A FINISHED BACKFILL ITEM: NO MONTHLY REFRESH (v3899 #151)
His 11-08 ruling: a ~2-year backfill, then a monthly refresh. Once every queued item was done the runner said "every queued
item is done" forever. d2jsp_backfill.queue_monthly_refresh (runner: --refresh) re-opens only an item whose backfill finished
and whose price file read it over 30 days ago (or never), pages it back only to the day before that read ("caught up"), and
the pace is run_once's own lastAskAt - 1 search a minute. A fresh item and a mid-backfill item are left alone.
Law: test_the_monthly_d2jsp_refresh_asks_only_stale_items. Seen RED x2.

### REG-3793 - THE BACKFILL STORED 1,829 OF 1,832 ROWS WITH NO SELLER (v3899 #151)
MEASURED 11-11 on the running backfill: every log line said authors=-. The parser takes a seller only from a line that neither
names the item nor carries a price (v3894 - so a body mention is never the seller), and a results row names both.
d2jsp_backfill.topic_authors reads the page's own rows: a topic belongs to the smallest <tr> linking to it, and that row names
its seller only with exactly one topic and one user.php name. Two names, two topics, none, or two rows that disagree: unknown.
The runner fills only posts the parser left without a seller (--check-authors counts it over the kept pages/, asking nothing).
UNKNOWN until a kept signed-in page is read: the rule is the page's structure, not yet seen on a real page.
Law: test_the_backfill_reads_the_seller_off_the_results_page. Seen RED x3.

### REG-3792 - A DUPLICATE ENIGMA TOPIC WEIGHED 1.5 VOTES: THE VOTE WAS SPLIT PER PAGE, NOT PER SELLER (v3899 #151 / #180)
MEASURED 11-11 16:07 on his console DB (GrokBot 6798004838): Enigma perfect weighed 110566436 at w 0.5 beside its duplicate
110552180 at w 1.0. d2jspOneVotePerPost shares a vote only between rows on ONE page; the DB keeps one row per link, so the
stored 0.5 was half a vote whose other half had folded onto the same key, and a seller's two topics on two pages were two
votes. d2jsp_price_db.vote_shares groups every stored row of a tier at price time: rows sharing a seller (author), a topic
(t=), or a declared same listing (mark_same_listing -> sameAs) never weigh more than ONE vote together (stored w scaled to 1 in
proportion); a group under one keeps its w (a shop post's 1/28 row is not raised); a w 0 outlier stays 0; unknown sellers in
different topics stay a group each. MEASURED on the 11-11 snapshot: 171 priced tiers, 0 prices moved. The runner's
reweight_sellers (rewrote w on every fold) is gone. Tiers carry "votes", explain rows "vote" and "author". His Enigma reads as
one vote once its seller is read (REG-3793) or the pair is marked. Law: test_a_duplicate_d2jsp_topic_counts_once. Seen RED x3.

### REG-3791 - THE PRICE DB STORED inf, nan AND True AS POSTS (v3899 #151)
His rule: a post without a price is not a post. ingest kept any float(fg) > 0: "inf", "nan" (nan <= 0 is False) and True
(float(True) == 1.0) were stored and counted as new posts, though counts() never priced them. ingest and counts share
price_of (a finite fg > 0, never a bool). Law: test_a_post_without_a_price_is_not_a_post. Seen RED x2.

Dean's console's last report: "the shelf driver beat 1.0h ago, but 2 dark: chronicle dark (51 owed), deleter dark (131 owed)"; the same beacon's readers block: "Claude is signed out on this PC" (OAuth session expired), and its fault rows: "791 item name(s) were READ from 18 reel(s) and NONE are banked". ### REG-3756 - A PC WHOSE SEALED READS FOUND NO CHRONICLE PAGE READ "BLOCKED AT SIGHTING" (v3901, #44, Dean 11-11)
Dean's console's last report: the river "blocked at 'sighting'" - 0 sightings against 7 sealed reels, a DRY joint, a broken pipe on his row. river.j_sighting waited on EVERY sealed reel (chronicle_swept.json's count), but each seal records what its read found - `pages: 0` when the reel held no Chronicle page - and such a read legitimately leaves no sighting behind. Now j_read also counts sealedWithPages (seals whose read found a page, or that do not say - an older row is never assumed empty) and j_sighting waits only on those, naming how many of the sealed reels found a page. A seal that found a page and left no sighting still reads DRY. Law: test_a_seal_that_found_no_page_owes_no_sighting (BASELINE the real gap stays DRY; a seal that does not say still owes; the read joint is unchanged). The river law (22 cases) stays green. SEEN RED: heart2 --prove 2 of 2 PROVEN.

### REG-3755 - THE GAME'S OWN DOOR WAS WORKED OUT FOR EVERY REEL AND NEVER SHOWN (v3901, #188, his ruling 11-11)
His ruling 11-11: on every route the session STARTS at the game's own door - the first D2 logo, witnessed by the title or Connecting to Battle.net, then character select. The chronicle lane works that door out for every reel it walks (d2r_screens.chain over the reel's door marks, kept in its ledger as `chain`), and NOTHING read it: chronicle_line.game_door() had no caller outside the laws, so a reel that opened on a cloud launcher, Boosteroid's queue or the Battle.net launcher said only when the REEL opened - the launcher minutes counted as the game. Now control_app._session_doors() hands each walked reel's door (startTs, logoTs, titleTs, connectingTs, charTs) to /api/sessions, attached AFTER the row cache like v3898's game link (the lane walks a reel after its row is built, and a sealed reel's directory never changes again), and the Shelf card draws "game began 9:04 PM at the D2 logo · 12 min in" on its own line, the full chain in its tooltip. No door -> nothing is said; an unreadable ledger draws no door (None, never an empty map). The render sandbox now seeds three synthetic doors so `shelf-cards` photographs the line. Law: test_a_card_says_when_the_game_began (_session_doors over a fixture ledger; the after-cache attach by its own source; shDoorPart in node: the logo, no door, a title start with no lag, an unknown reel start). SEEN RED: heart2 --prove 3 of 3 PROVEN.

### REG-3753 - A REEL FILMED NOTHING FOR 34 MINUTES AND NOTHING SAID WHY (v3901, #188, Dean 11-08)
MEASURED 11-12 on Dean's frozen copy (off the repo): reel 11-08 17:09 opened after an update ("Diablo is on screen"), its AI reads ran the whole time (Catacombs Level 2 at 17:22) and its first footage frame landed at 17:43 - a painted in-game frame, seconds after "[reap] hist over its 8.0GB cap ... read-eviction took 112 picture(s)"; a second reel that evening started 31 minutes late. Ruled out from his own logs: the warm-up gate (no "held back" line at either seal) and the game-window gate (the reads ran, so _GAME_OK held). The disk floor is unlikely too: the shedding lines came 10-20 min apart, which is the reaper's cadence only while free space sits ABOVE the floor (under it, it runs on every read). That leaves a stale capture file (the Windows feed archives eye.jpg / live.bmp only while it is under 5 s old, and the agent said "D2R pin found but grab black and not focused" in that hour) - UNKNOWN, because the footage writer kept its reason only in _FOOTAGE_WHY, in memory, overwritten every second, so nothing could say. Now every refused footage frame is counted by reason (source-missing, source-stale on the Windows feed, no-game, warming-up, disk-floor with the free GB, write-failed), the start of a pause and its end are each said once in the agent log, and the reel's index carries footageRefused when it seals. Law: test_the_reel_says_why_its_footage_stopped (the real _archive_footage_copy under a raised then lowered floor; BASELINE a frame lands with room). SEEN RED: heart2 --prove 3 of 3 PROVEN.

### REG-3751 - THE RECORDER'S REAPER DELETED FIRST AND RECORDED SECOND: A STOPPED DELETE LEFT NO RECORD (v3901, #217, the second eye on v3899)
The Grok CLI's look on v3899 (Mac ledger, finding 2): "_reap_record ... a crash after write() ... can still drop the reap line". Reproduced in part: the line is safe once written (the with-block closes the file before True, so a process crash after it loses nothing), but the ORDER was the hole - the disk-floor reel reaper ran rmtree / os.remove FIRST and wrote its reap-log line SECOND, so a recorder stopped between the two (an update's relaunch, a kill, a crash, an 11,000-frame rmtree) left a reel gone with no line at all: the #217 shape. Now an INTENT line goes down before each delete (removed null, intent true) and the outcome line still follows; river_stamp._deleter_records credits an intent whose outcome never landed (in words that say the recorder stopped mid-delete; an outcome that says the delete FAILED is never credited) and reel_custody names it. The same look's other findings, measured: (3) set_gap vs shard_sizes - REFUTED, both refuse a bool n and an unreadable manifest is refused by proof_shard.check_shards; (4) the note's command lists every name while its prose cuts at six - by design since v3898 (a follow-up that asks for the whole set). Law: test_a_reap_writes_its_intent_before_the_delete (the real _reap_record, _deleter_records and custody; the reaper's order by its own source, one anchor each). Law: test_a_half_applied_update_heals_itself (BASELINE: his own bytes still stop it). Seen RED: heart2 --prove PROVEN; the landed-update and stale-lock laws stay green.

### REG-3625 - A LAW IS KEYED ON THE FUNCTIONS IT RAN, NEVER ON ONES IT NEVER CALLED (#92)
**PULLED FROM v3894 (his call, 2026-11-10 ~20:25 IST) - NOT SHIPPED.** Its new key format ("heart2 P3 key v4") missed every
one of the 9,804 carried proofs, so v3894's round owed all 10,187 and its 21 shards were cut at their deadline with ~9,000
still owed (one chunk alone modelled 6,755 s, over a shard's ~57 min). The two commits (5389bc3d4, 632899cfc) are reverted;
#92 returns as its own version with a planned full re-prove (seed the v4 keys first, or migrate v3 entries whose inputs
did not change). The text below describes the change as written, not what is live.
His 11-06 ask: a one-law fix must not re-prove half of 9,446 proofs. REG-3393 traced past children that cannot read the tree, so a complete trace can drop files the run never opened. A file the run DID open (heart2, the law itself) still put every byte in the key, so a wording change in an uncalled helper discarded every proof (v3875 round 3 reused 0 of 9,446). Step 2 (the card's REG-3394, landed here): when sys.monitoring said hello, a traced .py that was not opened as data is hashed on its module-level lines plus the functions that started (PY_START). An uncalled function is not in the key. A source/data read keeps every byte, so a narrow key cannot serve a stale proof over bytes the law read. CRLF and LF of the same source are one function key. A run without monitoring, or a file that will not parse, falls back to the whole-file hash. Law test_a_law_is_keyed_on_the_functions_it_ran.

### REG-3626 - A LAW'S OWN TEMP REPO KEEPS THE CASE'S LINE ENDINGS, NOT THE PC'S AUTOCRLF (#107)
REG-3364 gave every checkout LF and left this batch: a law that git-inits its own temp repo still inherited the runner's global core.autocrlf. Git for Windows (and GitHub's windows-latest) installs with that set to true, so a fixture written as LF was rewritten as CR LF the next time Git touched it, and a byte assertion went red only on Windows. tv/git_quiet.pin_lf and init_repo pin core.autocrlf=false on the throwaway repo after init, and win over a Windows-default global. A census holds every test function that git-inits a throwaway repo to a pin. Law test_a_temp_repo_keeps_the_cases_line_endings.

During the CI wait the engine now watches per-job status: the moment one shard goes red it pulls the log, classifies (real / cut-off / timeout / infra), auto-reruns only that shard when it is a flake or cut-off (or queues the rerun until GitHub will accept it), and reports a real failure immediately so the fix can start while other shards are still running. Law: test_a_failed_shard_is_rehearsed_before_the_ci_push.

The Grok CLI's backlog look at v3861 (#231 comment 6671668579, finding 1). because it costs 44 s there, over the 20 s cap.

### REG-3304 - test_control PINNED THE OLD LETTER OF THE BEACON'S WRITE GATE, SO A BOUNDED WRITE READ AS AN UNBOUNDED ONE (v3875, GitHub's round)
GitHub, agent suite (3) and every proof shard's clean run: test_control 1 failure of 2274 -
TestV2283TheRosterMustNotSpendItselfToDeath.test_the_durable_row_is_BOUNDED_not_unconditional asserted the literal
`if (material || ageS >= REFRESH_S) {`, and v3873's daily material cap (REG-3277) named that condition `writeNow`
(`(material && !wOver) || ageS >= REFRESH_S`). The law held - more tightly - and the guard read its rename as the v2283
quota death. It now pins the new condition and the `if (writeNow)` that gates the lastseen write (2 sites carry it, the
lastseen one matches once, as before). Reproduced here by running that class alone (source reads only, no browser); green
after. (Corrected in v3876: an earlier line here said the shard never named the case. It did - REG-1877's
"its red case(s), named" line, one below the UNPROVABLE row; my filter for UNPROVABLE dropped it.)

### REG-3299 - THE PRE-FLIGHT SAID GREEN OVER 36 REGISTERED LAWS IT NEVER RAN: ITS POPULATION WAS THE COST TABLE, WHICH LAGS THE REGISTRY (v3875, GitHub's round)
v3875's first GitHub round came back red on one law, test_every_picture_the_console_asks_for_is_shipped, which fails on this
PC in 4 s - and the pre-flight had said "GREEN - 1477 law(s) ran clean" ten minutes earlier. tv/preflight.py chose its laws
from tv/gate_costs.json, and a law is added to that table only after CI has timed it: measured, 36 registered gates were in
run_gates and not in the table, every law written since the table was last refreshed. None of them ran here, and nothing
said so. Now `preflight.uncosted()` adds every registered python gate the table has not measured: it runs here, bounded by
LAW_TIMEOUT_S, unless its script drives a browser (GitHub's, his rule). The pre-flight says how many. Measured on the fix:
32 run here (all 32 green with REG-3298 in, 21 s), 4 drive a browser. The registry is read from the tree being
pre-flighted (a tree without run_gates.py has none). Law: test_a_version_is_preflighted_before_github_grades_it
(+ test_a_registered_law_the_cost_table_never_measured_runs_here), red-proof PROVEN.

### REG-3298 - v3874'S QUICK WINS TILES COMPOSED THREE ART PATHS THE PICTURE LAW HAD NEVER MET, SO IT ANSWERED UNKNOWN (v3875, GitHub's round)
GitHub, agent suite, v3875: test_every_picture_the_console_asks_for_is_shipped FAILED - "unknown art door bible.html:70266
art/tz_' + slug + '.jpg" and two at 70280. v3874's `_qwZoneArt` composes `art/tz_<slug>.jpg` from tzArtFor, and `_qwTile`
composes `art/<BOSS_PORTRAIT>` and `art/<_QW_SU_ART>`; tv/art_names.py knew none of the three, so it could not say whether
the pictures they ask for ship. Every name they ask for WAS in art/ (measured: 1271 names, 0 missing). Now the three are
doors: the zone art expands through the tz-info feed, the boss through boss-portraits, and the superunique sprites through a
new feed, qw-su-sprites (the 10 values of _QW_SU_ART, floor 10), so a renamed or missing .gif fails the law instead of
showing an empty tile. Law: test_every_picture_the_console_asks_for_is_shipped, red-proofs PROVEN (3 new).
### REG-3518 - NOTHING SAID WHETHER A ROUND GOT FASTER; EVERY ROUND IS NOW MEASURED AGAINST THE ONES BEFORE IT (v3890, #194)
His words 11-09: "make sure it keeps getting faster self improve it". tv/ci_speed.py is the ledger that says whether the rounds
get faster: when GitHub vouches, the ship measures every workflow on the commit from GitHub's own job records - the queue
(created -> started), the slowest job (started -> completed), the wall (first created -> last completed), the jobs - appends one
row per workflow to a machine-wide ledger (git's common dir) and says each against its earlier rounds. Run once on v3889's
real round: Publish waited up to 15.0 min, Routine I's slowest job 19.8-20.0, the proof shards' 43.3, the Windows set's 54.0
in a 99.6-min wall. And the measurement that sent the repo back: on Konyo-Labs (an Enterprise org on its trial) a round ran
at most 10 jobs at once (counted three times over a minute: 10 running, 20 queued) against ~40 on KonyoDigital's Pro - his
call, 11-09 18:50: "stop it.. and move it back to the pro one". `python3 tv/ci_speed.py --show` prints the ledger. A
measuring fault is said and never refuses a ship; only the real ship (main()) is measured.
GUARD: test_every_round_records_how_fast_it_ran (4 red-proofs).
### REG-3579 - A HUNG PROOF COULD RUN 30 MINUTES AND STARVE THE RUNNER SILENT (v3894)
MEASURED on v3890 run 42712427277 attempt 1, shard 10 (sha d22085c7b): the hosted runner lost communication at 54 minutes while "Prove this shard" was still in_progress. No logs were kept and the cache was never uploaded. GitHub: the runner was starved for CPU/memory or its network was blocked. Attempt 2 of the same shard finished the same 475 proofs in 26.9 minutes (prove_seconds=1554) on another runner. Shard 10 held 79 gates including every one of test_v3765_records_arm_live's 43 proofs; 279 proofs ran fresh and 196 were served by key. It is not systematically the longest shard (recent slowest were 3, 12, 17, 20, 21; a healthy v3890 shard ran 56.9 minutes), so a shorter job-level cut would falsely TIMEOUT work that finishes. The hole is one proof: two lanes double every law's timeout (LANE_DEADLINE_SCALE=2), so test_control's registered 900 s becomes 1,800 s - long enough for a hang to starve the runner agent before HARD_STOP (deadline + 480 s = job minute 63). Now `_inflight_limit` of a CI run (one with a deadline) also caps one proof at PROOF_CAP_S (900 s, the longest registered law timeout). A cut proof is TIMEOUT, owed, named. His Mac and a PC's census (no deadline) are unchanged.
GUARD: test_a_shard_cuts_before_the_runner_goes_silent (5 cases, 2 red-proofs).### REG-3578 - A PLANNER COMPARE FILLED IN NUMBERS THE PLANNER DID NOT CITE (v3894, #28)
A character-window row that disagrees with a cited planner value is a conflict; a planner key without frames, or a window row without frames, is unknown. Nothing is invented. Buff calibration stays later. Law: test_a_planner_compare_does_not_invent_missing_numbers.
### REG-3577 - FILM SIZE WAS READ FROM THE WINDOW'S CLIENT SIZE (v3894, #155/#255)
film_size_of returns (filmW, filmH) or None. A reel that only recorded the window client size does not pretend those pixels are the jpeg. Law: test_film_size_is_never_read_from_the_window_size.
### REG-3576 - AN UNRESOLVED FAILING CLASS CLOSED EVERY LOCK (v3894, #103)
_net_case_guards treated `src is None` as close-all, so a giant law whose failing class could not be resolved shut every lock the file guards. An unresolvable class is skipped; only a class that guards the lock closes it. Focused laws stay fail-closed. Law: test_an_unresolved_failing_class_does_not_close_every_lock.
### REG-3575 - A NAMELESS RED OF A GIANT LAW CLOSED EVERY LOCK (v3894, #103)
_net_case_guards returned True when a find named no case, so one red of test_control closed every lock. A giant law (NET_NARROW_MIN_LOCKS or more) now stays open on a nameless red; focused laws still close by the whole file. _net_heart does not let one cross-lock law's single red close every lock. Law: test_a_giant_laws_nameless_red_does_not_close_every_lock.
### REG-3574 - THE CHARACTER WINDOW WAS NOT HELD TO CITED PLANNER BREAKPOINTS (v3894, #28)
compare_window_to_planner reports agree when a sheet row's frames match a cited planner reference. The only numbers used are the published maxroll Patch 2.4 breakpoint tables (fetched 2026-10-04) already in test_the_breakpoint_row_is_the_next_step.py — the same tables d2planner uses. No itemized d2planner export was invented; buff calibration stays later. Law: test_the_character_window_agrees_with_cited_planner_breakpoints.
### REG-3573 - ADD MOD SEARCH MISSED AN AFFIX'S OWN STAT KEY (v3894, #95)
The searchable Add Mod list matched printed text and the affix name, but not the stat key the affix already carries (fcr on a Faster Cast Rate roll). _cbAfKeys reads those keys from the affix's own roll lines. No abbreviation table was invented. Law: test_add_mod_search_matches_an_affix_stat_key.
### REG-3572 - STAT AND SKILL AREAS IN THE CHARACTER WINDOW DID NOT OPEN (v3894, #234/#146)
Strength through IAS and the skill tree each have a data-cell (stat: / skill:) that opens a detail sentence. A number is shown only when the character already carries it. Law: test_the_character_window_stat_and_skill_areas_open.
### REG-3571 - BELT CELLS IN THE CHARACTER WINDOW DID NOT OPEN (v3894, #234/#146)
The window draws a 4x4 belt grid. A named item opens its card; an unseen cell only speaks its sentence. Law: test_the_character_window_belt_cells_open.
### REG-3570 - STASH CELLS IN THE CHARACTER WINDOW DID NOT OPEN (v3894, #234/#146)
The window draws a 10x10 stash grid. A named item opens its card; an unseen cell only speaks its sentence. Law: test_the_character_window_stash_cells_open.
### REG-3569 - INVENTORY CELLS IN THE CHARACTER WINDOW DID NOT OPEN (v3894, #234/#146)
The window draws a 10x4 inventory grid of chx-grid-cell buttons (not a third doll). A named item opens its card; an unseen cell only speaks its sentence. Law: test_the_character_window_inventory_cells_open.
### REG-3568 - A RESISTANCE ROW HID THE PARTS THE ENGINE ALREADY SUMMED (v3894, #153)
Hell's penalty and Anya's scrolls come from row.parts (difficultylevels.txt ResistPenalty and "Anya's resistance scrolls", +10 per completed difficulty). The visible line is those parts; -100 / +30 are not hardcoded. Law: test_a_resistance_row_names_its_hell_anya_and_gear_parts.
### REG-3567 - A SPEED ROW DID NOT NAME ITS CURRENT TIER (v3894, #153)
_cbBpHtml prepends "tier k/T · " from _cbBpTiers onto eng.bp.say, so the stats column shows the current tier and still says how much more reaches the next step. Law: test_the_stats_row_names_the_breakpoint_tier.
### REG-3566 - A NEW REEL DID NOT STAMP THE FILMED JPEG'S PIXELS (v3894, #155/#255)
The seal measures the first listed frame with film_size_from_jpeg and writes filmW/filmH onto capture. It does not copy the window client size into those keys. Law: test_a_new_reel_stamps_the_filmed_jpeg_size.
### REG-3565 - FILM SIZE WAS NOT RECORDED APART FROM THE WINDOW (v3894, #155/#255)
from_measured copies filmW/filmH only when both were measured under those names. Window w/h never become film size. from_index reads them back as None when absent. Law: test_the_capture_stamp_records_film_size_apart_from_the_window.
### REG-3564 - THE CARD'S BEST PLACE WAS THE FIRST BOSS, NOT SILOSPEN'S ALL #1 (v3894, #85 / gh#254)
Bane Ash's All #1 is Coldcrow / Cave Level 1, not Andariel. A qw-best-place banner names silospen's All #1 above the lists. The first boss row keeps "1st · best run" and qw-best only when it IS All #1; otherwise it reads "1st · best boss". Law: test_quick_wins_marks_silospens_all_first_as_the_best_place.
### REG-3563 - A SESSION HAD NO SOFT UNDERSTANDING OF GAMES, RUNS AND BOSSES (v3893)
His ruling: also count games, runs and per-boss farm counts as a soft layer on top of existing session seals; unknown when unclear. digest now carries `understanding` (ordered game names, sequential focused runs, town/field from the already-read area, per-boss lair visits). say_games and session splitting are unchanged. Law: test_the_session_carries_a_soft_understanding.
### REG-3562 - BOSS FARM COUNTS WERE NOT READ FROM THE AREA TEXT (v3893)
Per-boss farm counts (how many Andariel runs) come from the already-read area matched against the silospen set-mf lairs (Andariel -> Catacombs Level 4), once per game name via game_name_of_row. A zone the table does not name stays unknown. Law: test_boss_farm_counts_come_from_the_area_text.
### REG-3561 - CORNER TEXT WAS NOT CHECKED AGAINST THE TOWN (v3893)
The overlay already writes the zone name. That string is checked against the five act towns (and the 'The …' spelling). A known town names its act; any other written area is the field; empty is unknown. No pixel town template was invented (this tree still has no act-1–5 town frames). Law: test_corner_text_is_checked_against_the_town.
### REG-3560 - SEQUENTIAL GAME NAMES WERE NOT LINKED AS ONE FOCUSED RUN (v3893)
Consecutive numbered names that count up (Morph1 -> Morph2 -> Morph3), read via game_name_of_row, are one focused run. A gap, a name without a number, or a single numbered name is unknown. say_games and game_runs are not rewritten. Law: test_sequential_game_names_are_one_focused_run.
### REG-3559 - AVATAR CLASS WAS NOT CHECKED AGAINST CHARACTER SELECT (v3893)
The in-game avatar class vs the class from character select is a soft cross-check (agree / conflict / unknown). attribute_character is unchanged. The digest carries it as classCheck. Law: test_avatar_class_is_checked_against_character_select.

readSocketFillers names what is IN the sockets; d2jspParseSearch now peels those names (and a slash-roll written next to them) so "shako 15/15 Rainbow Facet" is not a 15/15 Shako and "shako 141 Ber'd" keeps the 141. The leftover _qwAlso once-path called effChance without the item, so a set piece used the unique curve. It now passes x.n; regular rows ask setMfChance then fall back to adjustChance (no extra /players). Law: test_quick_wins_also_rows_use_the_set_curve.
### REG-3556 - A PRESS ON THE CHARACTER-WINDOW BACKDROP LEFT IT OPEN (v3893, #191)
#chx-win is a full-screen host; the card is .chx-win-box. A press on the backdrop now peels it via _chxClose. Law: test_a_press_outside_the_character_window_closes_it.
### REG-3555 - A TAB SWITCH LEFT THE CHARACTER WINDOW OPEN (v3893, #191)
navClean, switchTab and the console header already closed the builder and the unique/drop/boss cards, but not #chx-win. All three now ask _chxClose. Law: test_a_tab_switch_closes_the_character_window.
### REG-3554 - THE SAME D2JSP SELLER COUNTED AS TWO POSTS (v3893, #180)
The same seller is one post and one price: when a signed-out readable user.php name (or a stored author) proves two topics are the same seller, their votes share a weight of 1. An unknown author stays one vote per link. Topics are never hard-deleted or merged by id. Law: test_the_same_seller_is_one_d2jsp_vote.
### REG-3553 - THE GUEST BOARD BADGE READ THE BAKED D2R_BUILD, NOT THE LIVE API (v3893, #193)
The guest #v687-build-badge painted window.D2R_BUILD from a cached bible.html (v3888) while /api/status and the Fleet said v3889. It now takes st.ver when the live API answers. A failed fetch never claims a live version. Law: test_the_guest_badge_reads_the_live_version.
### REG-3552 - THE SCENARIO WALK TREATED THE LOBBY AS IN-GAME (v3893, #187/#185)
His ordered templates: login → CONNECTING → character select (name + class) → lobby (game name typed or seen, then chosen) → game-entry portal → town (act 1–5). Lobby and the portal are still before a town, so they never reach the stash reader; character select does not flip the walk into play. Battle.net login, CONNECTING... and the game-entry portal have no real frames on this tree (not invented). Law: test_the_scenario_templates_follow_his_order.
### REG-3551 - A SESSION THAT STARTED AT THE LOGO WAS TAGGED AS THE PREVIOUS CHARACTER (v3893)
Recording starts before character select, so who_at(session t0) only saw earlier characters and could name the reel as the previous player. The highlighted name was already read (char_select.selected_of, logins, session_characters). digest now consults that login for the reel's sessionId. A session with no login of its own still inherits who_at(t0). Law: test_the_session_is_tagged_from_the_character_select_name.
### REG-3550 - THE STASH READER RAN ON LAUNCHER AND CHARACTER-SELECT FRAMES (v3893, #187/#185)
His ruling: the stash reader is joined to the same launch-chain templates the recorder uses, and to the shadow recorder's window. It runs only while a reel is recording, and only once the chain (second logo → CONNECTING... → character select → in-game) or mid-session hud/lobby has put the film in play — not as a separate standalone filter. Pre-game screens (logo, title, character select) never reach classify_stash_grid; an unlabelled launcher/idle frame does not either until the chain has entered. This tree has no real Battle.net-login or CONNECTING... frames to invent templates from. Law: test_the_stash_reader_runs_only_in_play.
### REG-3549 - THE FLEET'S MIDDLE EYE GLOWED CALM-GREEN WHILE WAITING FOR A REEL (v3893, #189)
His ruling 2026-11-09: the Fleet's middle shadow-reader eye must be DARK unless a reel is actually recording (`sh.recording`). Law: test_the_fleet_shadow_eye_is_dark_unless_recording (the older fleet-eye law no longer pins the waiting-green).

### REG-3533 - UNIQUES AND SETS ONLY COUNTED THE CAPPED finds[:16] TEASER (v3891, #184)
Elad's rule: every unique/set seen on the floor counts once (identified or not); charms and other
non-unique non-set items count only in STASH, not in those two boxes. MEASURED: `_theatre_sessions`
capped `finds` at 16 for the 12s poll (that cap stays) and then called `_chron_tally(_finds)`, so the

### REG-3523 - THE AGENT SUITE RAN A HAND-SET 5; IT NOW CHOOSES ITS SLICE COUNT FROM MEASURED GATE COSTS AND REFRESHES THEM EVERY ROUND (v3891, #194)
MEASURED on v3889's agent tests: 5 fixed slices, the slowest job 20.1 min (~13.6 of gates + setup). Now the plan job

hands that ONE table to every shard as GATE_COSTS, so all cut the same slices from fresher costs. The verdict measures
every gate this round ran from the shards' own logs (--base: a gate not run keeps its last cost) and saves the table.

saves the table (actions/cache); the next round's stamp check restores it, chooses the fewest fast shards whose heaviest

### REG-3506 - A SET ITEM'S ODDS MOVED WITH MF BY THE UNIQUE CURVE: PAST MF 300 A SET AT A HIGH-LEVEL BOSS GETS RARER, AND THE PAGE SAID CHEAPER (v3890, #43)
MEASURED 11-09 on silospen's calculator (D2R_ROW_3_0, the source of every stored 1:N): Sander's Paragon from Hell Mephisto
is 1:9,382 at MF 300 and 1:10,007 at MF 1000; the page printed 1:7,381 - it moved every 1:N off its MF-300 base by the
unique curve (adjustChance, effective MF x 250 / (MF + 250)). The game rolls UNIQUE first and set only on a failed unique
roll: P(set) = P(set roll) x (1 - P(unique roll)), each in C integers - (ratio - (ilvl - qlvl)/divisor) x 128, x 100 / (100 +
effective MF), floored at the row's min, less chance x bonus / 1024 - with ItemRatio's normal row (unique 400/1/6400, set
160/2/5600; exceptional and elite bases the same) or a class base's row (240/3/6400, 120/3/5600), the set roll's effective
MF x 500 / (MF + 500). At a high-level monster the set roll sits on its 5600 floor while the unique roll climbs, so the set
gets rarer; at Normal it still gets cheaper (Normal Mephisto 1:5,160 -> 1:4,614). Hand-checked on 5 act bosses x 3
difficulties x 4 MFs (bonus 983, base level 1): 0.02% worst. Now tv/silospen_set_mf.py pulls 8 sample set items (normal,
exceptional, elite and class bases, base level 1-85) at MF 0/300/700/1000, fits each farm's monster level and quality bonus
to them (FITS), and writes the page's SET_MF block; effChance takes the item (the registry's sources carry it, 22 call
sites pass it) and a set at a fitted farm rolls setMfChance. NOT modelled yet, named: terror-zone columns (the monster
level follows his character level), the Cows, the Pit, Diablo Clone, Quick wins' own places - they keep the unique curve.
GUARD: test_a_set_items_odds_follow_the_unique_first_roll (Python and the page's own JS against silospen's checkpoints;
every set on the boss tables has its base; every farm measured or named; the item reaches effChance; 5 red-proofs).

suite never runs on his Mac); the measurement above is the before/after.

### REG-3364 - EVERY WINDOWS CHECKOUT WAS CR LF, SO EVERY RAW-BYTE LAW WAS RED THERE (v3880, board #107)
#107's probe (a one-off GitHub Windows job, branch ci/win107-probe, run 42367869017) ran the 62 laws GitHub's Windows prover
found red untampered and kept why. One class: a law reading a file's raw bytes on a "\n" anchor - test_one_hunt_clock
("CUT START MISSING"), test_every_windows_console_starts_itself_at_sign_in ("substring not found" in start_tvd_win.ps1 read
"rb"), and others. MEASURED 11-07 on the work ALT: core.autocrlf = true, and `git ls-files --eol` reads w/crlf for
bible.html, control_app.py and start_tvd_win.ps1. That is Git for Windows' default; GitHub's runner does the same. So
GitHub's Windows set was never whole for those laws, and on the ALTs they were owed for ever.
FIX: .gitattributes `* text=auto eol=lf`. The index already holds LF only (2765 LF, 0 CRLF or mixed; a real renormalize of a
clone changed 0 files), so no PC sees anything modified. A Windows checkout writes LF from now on. A CRLF file already on a
PC stays until a version touches it, and bible.html and control_app.py change every version. Binaries are detected and left
alone. SIMULATED before shipping: a CRLF checkout pulling the commit fast-forwards cleanly with status clean. The repo
carries no .bat/.cmd/.vbs, and PowerShell runs LF scripts.
NOT CHANGED: laws that build their OWN temp repo get the runner's global autocrlf and need their own fix (#107's next batch).
GUARD: tv/test_every_checkout_gets_lf.py - the rule, a clone made with autocrlf=true gets LF (and a binary's bytes), no
committed CRLF. 1 red-proof, RED; without eol=lf the same clone measured CR LF.

### REG-3363 - NO PC COULD SAY WHETHER D2JSP ACTUALLY ANSWERS THERE (v3880, board #56, his 11-05 worry)
His words 11-05: "d2jsp works on Dean's PC? the MacBook never did". The D2JSP lamp says whether a sign-in exists, and
REG-3344 made a shadow's lamp UNKNOWN. Only a real search proves d2jsp answers, and no PC recorded one where another PC could
see it.
FIX: v3878's refresh lane (d2jsp_refresh.run_once) already asks the forum for one stale item a pass on every PC. Now:
- every read it makes is recorded on that PC (.d2jsp_check.json, gitignored: when, which item, what came back);
- a day with nothing due asks CHECK_ITEM (Shako) once, so a PC whose database is all fresh still proves its sign-in reads;
- the record rides the PC's beacon ("d2jsp"), shaped by functions/api/console.js (ok true/false/null, time clamped, words
  capped). A flip of its outcome is news; a newer read with the same outcome is not.
- Every Fleet row's box draws it: "d2jsp reads · 3 h ago", "signed out", "did not read (unread)", or UNKNOWN (never asked,

### REG-3360 - AN IMPORT OUTLIVED THE CONSOLE THAT ASKED FOR IT: THREE RAN AT ONCE ON THE OLD ALT, ONE FOR 32 HOURS (v3879, board #103)
MEASURED 11-07 ~12:45 IST over SSH, after GrokBot's #230 6705733326 saw the OLD ALT's river time out. Three `heart2
--import-shards` were running at once. Two were orphans of consoles that had already exited (parent GONE): one started
11-06 02:59 and had keyed v3876's bundle for 32 hours, one from 03:43. The live console's own import was the third. The
PC had 457 MB of 7.9 GB free, and GET /api/river timed out at 60 s. The work ALT, with one import, answered its river in
2 s. Killing the two orphans by PID freed 575 MB.
CAUSE: proof_release runs heart2 with subprocess.run. Its timeout (5400 s) lives in the console, so it dies with the
console when an update or a restart replaces it. Nothing bounded the child.
FIX: the console passes its pid (--import-parent). heart2's _watch_import_parent asks every 10 s whether that pid is
alive, and ends the import (exit 3, saying why) once it is gone. This is the console's own _orphan_exit_loop rule: only
a child that was TOLD its parent watches, so a hand-run import never ends. Stopping between writes is safe: each write is
atomic, under an OS lock released when the process exits, and REG-3352 keeps what was written. A probe that cannot
answer keeps the import, never a guessed death.
GUARD: tv/test_an_import_ends_with_its_console.py - REAL processes: a parent is started and killed, and the import must
exit 3 by itself. A live parent keeps it. A broken probe keeps it. The argv and main() wiring. 4 red-proofs, all RED.
NOT CHANGED: the Windows PID-reuse window (a new process with the dead console's pid keeps the import alive, as before).

### REG-3350 - TWO OF MY REG-3319 RED-PROOFS STAYED GREEN ON GITHUB'S PROOF ROUND AND RED ON THE MAC (v3877, GitHub's round 7)
GitHub, proof-keys shards, v3877 at 2fa719744: test_a_named_file_the_law_never_opened_is_keyed_by_name[2] and
test_a_gate_proven_on_these_bytes_is_carried[59] BLIND ("stayed GREEN through its own defeat"); both were RED here. Two
causes, both mine. (1) [2] broke only the Popen line's node_version_only call. On Linux with glibc 2.34+ under Python
3.13+ (GitHub's 3.14), subprocess starts a child with os.posix_spawn even with close_fds, and that event's branch asks
node_version_only AGAIN: the bare node still said U and the edit re-proved. MEASURED with the two audit events raised by
hand under the trace site: old sabotage Linux path [A, U], new sabotage [A, p]; the Mac's 3.9 raises Popen alone. NOW the
proof breaks node_version_only itself. (2) REG-3319 made heart2 arm node_trace.cjs in NODE_OPTIONS for every traced law
run, and that one hook file writes the ledger's trace and whatever HEART2_TRACE_LOG a child carries. So under the prover,
the ledger law's and the named-file law's fixtures inherited a working hook: a broken arming in gate_ledger (ledger [59]) or
in the fixture's heart2 (named [5], unrun on GitHub because the gate stopped at [2]) stayed green. MEASURED with
NODE_OPTIONS carrying the hook: the old laws [5] and [59] GREEN, the same [59] RED without it. NOW both fixtures take any
node_trace.cjs --require out of the NODE_OPTIONS they inherit, and every one of the 20 + 15 red-proofs goes RED under the
outer hook. Lesson: a red-proof proven by hand outside the prover is not proven on the prover's environment - when a change
arms something for every law run, re-prove the laws that test the same arming under it.

the SAME try as the read, after _river_remember(_lanes) has kept this very read; a reader that timed out on the busy PC and

answer is written, and a BrokenPipe / ConnectionAborted / ConnectionReset after that is no river failure: nothing is filed

(+1 case, on the source - the handler runs inside the live server); red-proof PROVEN (1). Dean's river NOT draining (ROUTED

### REG-3263 - ON WINDOWS A FAILED NODE FETCH WAS THE PROCESS'S ANSWER FOREVER, SO THE REPAIR BOOK'S HOURLY RETRY NEVER FETCHED (v3873, #11, the Grok CLI on REG-3158, #231 6681759774)
node_runtime._background keeps one answer per process so a fetch is never repeated in a loop. The repair book's node door asks it once an hour, so on a Windows PC whose first fetch failed (the network down at boot) every later ask got that cached failure, and node stayed missing until a relaunch. A failed answer now expires after RETRY_FAILED_S, which is the book's own one-hour cooldown. A success is still never fetched again, and a failure is retried at most hourly. A partial best-flavor import is owed again after PARTIAL_REASK_S (45 min), at most PARTIAL_MAX_TRIES (4) times per commit, and a re-ask that misses keeps the set already in. The look's other two points: the import not asking runtime_refusal is by design (that rule is for PC-to-PC carried exports, REG-3045; GitHub's runners are pinned, and each imported law still owes one clean run on the PC, his 11-05 ruling). The shared cancel group across commits is named, not changed: a newer commit's run supersedes the older one's make-up, which no PC still on the older commit needs once it updates.

### REG-3255 - THE ENGINE FRAME'S RE-POINT CANCELED THE CONSOLE'S OWN IMAGES, SO A SLOW CONSOLE SHOWED BROKEN ICONS (v3872, #73)
GrokBot counted broken images for days: Mac 8, then 4; ALT 6, then 16. My own probes found 0 on the Mac. Measured on the work ALT, headless at 1920 through an SSH tunnel with GETs only, across several runs: 2 to 9 broken per load, every time some of /art/ui_tab_forge.png, ui_tab_session.png, ui_tab_funi.png, ui_tab_tvd.png, ui_tab_tools.png, logo_gold.png, diablo_hell_graphic.png (#hero), hd_ber_rune.png and hd_lem_rune.png. Each file is a valid PNG and is served 200 with the right type; a fresh request decodes it. Each broken element fails decode() with EncodingError and is still in the DOM, although its onerror removes it: no error event fired, so its load was aborted. Logged per request: every /art/ request the engine iframe starts ends net::ERR_ABORTED (29 to 100 per load). They come from its v=boot document, which the first status poll re-points to the version (control_ui.html, the v1251 cache-bust), and then from the versioned document. Blink shares one in-flight image load between documents, so the console's own images, asked for at that moment, inherit the cancel. On a fast console the loads finish first, which is why the Mac rarely shows it. Not the instrument: with art requests left un-intercepted the broken images still appear (7, then 2). Fix: after each engine-frame load and the page load, each image that ended broken is asked again once (?reask=1, which the art route ignores). An image still loading, a lazy one not yet asked, a loaded one and a data:/blob: one are left alone. Measured on the ALT's own page with the same logic injected: 9, 7 and 5 broken went to 0. Law test_a_canceled_image_is_asked_again (3 cases in node on the shipped block; 4 red-proofs PROVEN by heart2's prover).

### REG-3253 - THE MAC READ d2jsp THROUGH A COPY OF HIS CHROME'S SIGN-IN THAT d2jsp TURNS AWAY (v3872, #87, his call 2026-11-06)

### REG-3252 - A TRIM BEFORE THE ONE THAT KEPT A FRAME COULD STILL DATE ITS PRUNE (v3872, the Grok CLI on REG-3239, #231 6680105032)

### REG-3251 - A LANDED DIAGNOSIS WHOSE SAVE FAILED WAS ASKED AGAIN, AND A KILL MID-ASK RE-OPENED THE DAY (v3872, the Grok CLI on REG-3237, #231 6680104597)
The look at v3869's tip found the hole in REG-3237's fix. The day's spend was counted only after the answer came back and was kept in memory as a number. So a landed answer whose save failed was on disk nowhere: not under seen and not under did-not-land. The next pass asked it again: one landed ask, cap 2, asked on both passes. A kill before os.replace took the count with the process, and the next process spent the allowance over the old file. Now each ask is RESERVED on disk before it is made: the count moves and the fault is marked "cut off" first. A record that will not write asks nothing and says so. A kill mid-ask leaves its ask counted, the fault waits for tomorrow, and the hover says the ask was cut off before its answer was saved. A landed answer whose save fails is kept in the process and laid back over the file on the next pass. "Not asked" (no claude) gives its reservation back. ### REG-3239 - A PRUNED FRAME COULD BE DATED ON A TRIM BEFORE IT WAS FILMED, OR ON ANOTHER REEL'S TRIM (v3868, the Grok CLI on REG-3207)
The Grok CLI's look at read_pictures.py (#231 6675925066), each confirmed in judge(). Now a frame with no capture time, on a reel trimmed more than once, is "released with its reel - which of its trims took it cannot be told"; one trim alone is the only deleter that could have taken it and keeps its date (the pre-flight caught the first cut undating that case), and a reap that NAMES the frame dates it. (5) When the tombstone path could not be asked, the memo keyed a fallback path the loader might not read; it no longer memoizes then. (6) A refusal carried its stamp and no time; it carries both. (2) is narrower than stated: loose frames (`<n>_<ms>.jpg`) are never in a reel's tombstones, so the reel-only rule is right for them. (2) On Windows, holders() dropped a process that would not answer and returned the set of whatever answered - an empty set when none did - which the pass took as a finished read; a process of THIS user (or of an owner that cannot be read) that will not answer is UNKNOWN now, nothing pruned. (3) On POSIX, lsof's exit status was ignored once any process line came back, so a listing that failed part-way read as complete; measured on his Mac a full listing exits 0, so any other exit is UNKNOWN. (4) The re-ask before each prune compared holders with the worktree's folder only, but `git worktree remove` also deletes its gitdir under the main .git; a process holding only that index is a hold now. Law test_what_keeps_growing_is_salvaged_then_pruned (+4 cases, 4 red-proofs PROVEN).

### REG-3231 - THE ROUTE'S FULL VAULT SWEEP RE-RAN A REEL THE HANG BOOK HELD, AND TWO UNASKED CHECKS READ AS "NO LANE" (v3867, the Grok CLI on REG-3200/3201)

### REG-3217 - THE TASK BOARD WAS THE ONE MAP STILL TYPED BY HAND (v3866, his words 2026-11-05)
His words: "make sure its derived always console and you and the taskboard synced.. so we are always with our finger on the trigger and know whats still being worked on and not shipped". Fix: tv/task_truth.py gives every card a DERIVED phase. Its keys are the REG ids its subject names (lists and ranges expanded), else a version leading the subject, else a branch, else the same from its description (`basis` says which). Each key is resolved against git in the console's own checkout: no-evidence, building (local only), graded (a ci/ branch), shipped vN (origin/main), live vN (the SITE serves N, read from the newest successful Publish run, never origin/main's stamp again), looked (GrokBot's visual seat on #230, after the ship), third-eyed (a SECOND-EYE row on #231). A tree that would not answer is UNKNOWN, never no-evidence; an unread lane is UNKNOWN, never "not looked". The board lane publishes the phase on every card, and /d2r/tasks.html draws it with when it was reached and which comment made it.

The first cut (claude/fx-board) was reviewed against his real board before it shipped, and the review held it (verdict fix). Measured: 13 "ready to close" flags, 0 of them real. Every one rested on a Grok CLI status note on #230 ("This seat has not read the v3863 range"), on GrokBot's CODER seat posting a plan, on a REG id recapped from the changelog lower down a look, or on a look that said the work FAILS. "live" was origin/main's stamp, so the hour a Publish runs read live. "REG-2980, 2986, 3109" keyed REG-2980 alone and "REG-2914/.../3086-3089/3098" dropped three ids. The doctor row's message named the surface id foot-tasks, so a regenerated HEART.md would have counted a surface the row does not watch. Repaired: a look is only what its HEADING names, the newest look about a key decides and a failing one refutes it, GrokBot counts only on #230 from its visual seat, the third eye only on #231, `live` reads the Publish run (`site_view`, one page through handoff._gh's new paginate=False), and the chip carries `w` (which moment its age is) and the look ids. Law `test_the_task_board_is_derived_from_the_evidence` (46 red-proofs PROVEN).

### REG-3191 - GITHUB'S PROOFS WERE IMPORTED AND STILL NEVER OPENED A LOCK, AND HALF OF THEM KEYED DIFFERENTLY ON HIS MAC (v3865, his ruling 2026-11-05 item 3)
His ruling: "Each PC imports the proofs for byte-identical files at update ... Locks open on (imported proofs + local self-check)". Measured the evening of 2026-11-05: heart2's `_owes_here(run, name)` was True whenever `run.direct` was None (every run outside a push), so after every ship each changed law re-ran locally before the census went current. His Mac imported 2,928 proofs and still owed 162 at 40 a slice, with every river lock shut. And the import banked only 2,928 of GitHub's 8,577 v3864 entries. `heart2._inert` decides whether a stamp line is masked out of a proof's key (REG-2602). It asked `stamp_leak.leak_problem`, whose last check refuses free text naming THIS machine's home path or user name. On a runner (home /home/runner) a ship row naming GitHub's runners was a leak and stayed raw; on his Mac it was masked. One set of bytes, two keys. Keyed on his Mac with HOME=/home/runner, frame.release's eight guards (209 proofs) matched the runner on 78, exactly the unmasked ones.

Fix: `_inert` asks `leak_problem(t, machine=False)`: 209/209 and a 121-gate sample of 655/655 now key the same on both, a Windows home too, and no key his Mac gave before moves. The bump and the gate ledger keep the machine check. `heart2.trust_pass` writes into the census, before a slice proves anything, every owed gate whose every proof the bank serves over this checkout's own bytes, at the age it was measured, and counts them as `trusted`. Not on the import's word: a gate any proof of which declares `needs`, one in the declared ENV_SELF_CHECK, a gate with any proof the bank cannot serve, and a gate the census holds BLIND. The trust pass runs right after the update import (`proof_release`: `heart2.py --trust --import-shards`, only when the import landed) and as the self-prove lane's light start when a slice is held only by busy / cooldown / backoff / memory / takes-only. It runs once per bank signature, never beside his game, never in an environment re-prove. Census writes hold one lock, and the trust pass re-reads the census under it, so a BLIND filed meanwhile is never overwritten. The push path is unchanged. Laws `test_an_imported_proof_opens_the_locks` (27 red-proofs) and `test_a_proofs_key_is_the_same_on_every_machine` (4).

### REG-3192 - NOTHING KEPT PROVING WHAT THE LOCKS TOOK ON ANOTHER MACHINE'S WORD (v3865, his ruling 2026-11-05 item 4)
His ruling: "the background full proof keeps running at idle as a SAFETY NET but no longer holds the river shut - a red/blind it finds goes to the fleet + BUGS and closes only the lock its law guards." Once REG-3191 lets imported proofs open the locks, a law that is red on THIS PC only (environment, not code) would stay trusted with nothing checking it.

Fix: over a current census the self-prove lane runs the trusted gates here at idle (`--net`, every stand-aside rule, never a small slice). PROVEN ends the trust. A RED clean run, a BLIND or an INVALID is recorded per gate in `netFinds` with a BUGS-ready line, never in blind, gateShas or the fingerprint, and closes only the locks whose guard set holds that law (`self_arming._net_heart`, the #156 rule). The census stays current. A find, and a trusted gate the net could not judge yet (`netUnjudged`), is judged again after NET_RETRY_S, and each run counts once. Finds ride the beacon (`net_for_wire`), the fleet worker (`functions/api/console.js`) and the Fleet row ("safety net: <law> RED - its locks shut"), and this PC's doctor row warns and names the law. Laws `test_a_safety_net_red_closes_only_its_own_lock` (25 red-proofs) and `test_a_safety_net_find_reaches_the_fleet` (7, three need node).

### REG-3193 - THE PROOF IMPORT KEYED ON ONE CORE WHILE EVERY LOCK WAITED (v3865)
Measured 2026-11-05: `heart2 --import-shards` ran on one core: 1,278 s for v3863 and 1,635 s for v3864, with every lock shut the whole time. Fix: heart2 computes each law's keys (v1 and the variants the target records) in a spawn pool before `select()`, in jobs of at most 12 proofs, and `key_for` computes here whatever a worker did not answer. Workers = cores - 2, at most 8, and no more than free memory above child_guard's floor holds. Unknown memory means one at a time. pythonw on Windows, no git in a worker, gone with its parent; a failed pool is said and the rest keyed here. Measured on the real v3864 bundle at one commit: one core 1,782.6 s, 3 workers 728.5 s, 8 workers 419.8 s, a worker peaking at 262 MB, and 0 of 8,577 keys different from one core. Law `test_an_import_keys_on_spare_cores_exactly_as_one_core_would`.

### REG-3215 - THE HEART SAID OPEN OVER A LOCK THAT MAY NOT ACT, AND THE FLEET CARD SAID SHUT (v3865, GrokBot #230 2026-11-05)
GrokBot on glass at 21:08: "Fleet 'locks shut' while frame.release is OPEN - glass trusts stale proof census". Measured at 21:23: the heart's frame.release row carried state "OPEN" ("35 of 35 DISTINCT ATTACKS refused ... wilson 0.901 >= 0.722") and permitted false ("the heart2 PROOF census is STALE ..."), heldBy stale. The top counted open 7, total 9, permitted 4, and may('frame.release') was False. So the Fleet card was right. "OPEN" answered "is it proven strong enough", but his question is "may it act now".

The same word sat on every lock surface: the list cell read "OPEN · MAY NOT ACT", the valves header "7 of 9 open", the organ row "7 of 9 locks open", the Vault chip hover "OPEN: ... — but it may NOT act now", and the fan hover "OPEN — it proved itself" or "HELD — ...". The fan caption said "held" where the Fleet said "shut".

Fix: self_arming writes both answers on every row. `act` is "may act" or "shut"; `actSay` is "shut - the prover is behind"; `provenSay` names the strength, e.g. "proven 0.90 >= 0.72", "not proven 0.44 < 0.51" or "by design - nothing to sabotage". A row with no verdict reads shut. `lock_counts()` is the one valve tally, "4 of 9 may act now (7 proven)", and a missing verdict makes the count UNKNOWN, never 0. The trim (the seventh field it would have swallowed), the heart route, the selfArming organ row, the chips, the heart's list and header, and the fan's hover and shut caption all print those words. `state` and `permitted` stay for older readers. Law `test_a_lock_says_may_act_or_shut_first` (17 red-proofs PROVEN). Moved anchors: `test_health_engine` (the HARDENED red-proof now targets the one tally) and `test_a_held_lock_shows_its_catch_up` (held -> shut).

### REG-3216 - THE HEART FLOOR NEVER TIGHTENED WHEN COVERAGE ROSE (v3865, GrokBot #230 2026-11-05)
HEART.md said the console watches 8 of 406 painted surfaces and the board 4 of 602. tv/heart_floor.json still held 7 of 366 (its names omit `bug`) and 1 of 513 (`vault-moved-note` alone). The floor rose only on a hand `--bless`, and `--check` compared counts. So `bug` could stop being watched and the console fall back to 7, or the board to 1, with the gate green. The ratchet only held as far back as the last bless.

Fix: a regeneration now raises a page's floor to the map whenever the map still watches every name the floor holds. A lost name leaves that page's floor alone, so the loss cannot be blessed away by a regeneration. `--check` refuses a floor that lags the map and names what it is missing. It also refuses a lost name even when the count held, because one gained surface can hide one lost. A bless that lowers the floor needs `--why`, which is recorded as `_lowered`. HEART.md and the floor are built first, then written whole. Before, `io.open(OUT,"w").write(render())` emptied HEART.md when render raised. The committed floor is raised to the measured map: 8/406 with `bug`, and the board at 4/602. Law `test_the_heart_floor_rises_with_the_map` (8 red-proofs PROVEN).

### REG-3210 - PUBLISH RE-PROVED A COMMIT ITS ci/ ROUND HAD ALREADY PROVED, AND THE FIX FIRST BROKE THE RE-RUN THAT RESCUES A STUCK SHARD (v3865, his words: "2hr and 50 min are you kidding me?")
That figure was a UTC-vs-Israel-time misreading, not a measurement. What GitHub recorded:
On 2026-11-05 the ci/proof-keys-v3864 run banked proofs-9d9485ea6…tgz at 18:17 UTC. Publish (run 42084305066) began nine
minutes later on the same commit. Its shards restored only "the proofs the last MAIN run banked" (REG-2961: v3863's) and
served 1-2 proofs each. Shard 6 proved 380 of its 388 again, for 49.5 min, and the whole Publish took 55.7 min on a commit
already proved. Every PC imports that bundle; GitHub did not. Now proof-keys-shards.yml's `seed` job builds one seed per
run: the REG-2961 restore plus the proof-bank bundle for exactly $GITHUB_SHA. tv/proof_seed.py fetches it through the PCs'
own proof_release.download and safe_extract, and merge_shards keeps only servable PROVENs. served.json names what this
commit already proved. Every shard downloads the seed and checks its sha256; on a mismatch it exits 3. heart2 still
serves a seed entry only under this checkout's own key. A seed that cannot be built is a cold run, said and never red.
Second eye: moving the restore into the seed job broke the rescue that got v3864 out. Shard 10 of run 42061540765 held 656
of 8,829 proofs and ran 87 min until it was cancelled at 17:40 UTC. "Re-run failed jobs" restored the cache attempt 1's
fan-in saved (heart2-proofs-<sha>-42061540765-1); the shard served 47 gates whole and finished in 36 min. The seed job is
not re-run, so its seed predates attempt 1. Now a re-run shard restores heart2-proofs-<sha>-<run_id>- into
heart2-seed/rerun, and `proof_seed.py --widen` merges it after the digest check. The plan stays the seed job's
served.json, so the re-run shard cuts the same plan as its siblings. Law: tv/test_a_proof_run_starts_from_its_exact_commits_proofs.py
(10 red-proofs, 10 PROVEN).

### REG-3211 - THE SHARD PLAN PRICED A PROOF THE CACHE WOULD SERVE LIKE ONE IT MUST RUN (v3865)
Once a run starts from its exact commit's proofs (REG-3210), most of every plan is served. The plan still priced each
served proof as a full run, so the owed rest would land wherever the gate names fell. MEASURED on v3864's Publish (run
42084305066): the slowest shard proved for 3,170 s against a mean of 2,297 s (1.38x). Shard 14 took 23.5 min for 11
proofs. Now proof_shard.plan(served=) prices a proof already PROVEN at this commit at SERVED_PROOF_S with no clean run,
and cuts and places only the owed proofs, longest first. Every proof is still assigned exactly once, and served=None
gives exactly the old plan. heart2._served_now reads the seed job's served.json, and only when its sha is this
checkout's HEAD. heart2 says each shard's modelled wall ("REG-3211 OWED-WORK PLAN"). On a fixture shaped like v3864 the
old plan's slowest shard carries 5.1x the mean owed work; the new one at most 1.25x. A cold run (no served list) plans as
before. Its pile is now bounded by REG-3212 and picked up by REG-3210's re-run. Law:
tv/test_a_proof_run_plans_by_the_work_still_owed.py (6 red-proofs, 6 PROVEN).

### REG-3212 - A PROOF RUN HAD NO BOUND HIS 75 MINUTES COULD TRUST, AND THE FIRST BOUND COULD NOT CUT A RUN ALREADY GOING (v3865, his words: "why has it been stuck for so long and not triggered at an alert somewhere at 75 minutes which was max?")
Shard 10 of ci/proof-keys-v3864 (run 42061540765) proved for 87 min of job; every other shard was done by 17:05 UTC. It
ran under a 160-minute step cap and a 180-minute job cap, so nothing fired. Now the shard job is capped at 75 min and
the prove step at 70. heart2 reads HEART2_PROVE_DEADLINE (job start + 55 min) and HEART2_GATE_CAP_S (1500). Past either
bound, a proof that would have to run is not started. It is recorded TIMEOUT: owed by name, never PROVEN, never banked.
A proof the cache serves is still served.
Second eye: the bound was asked only before a proof started. With 3 lanes the deadline scale is 2, so a 900-s gate got
1800 s per run, and a proof started at minute 54 could run past the step cap and leave no manifest. Now every law run
of a push takes the tighter of two limits: its own deadline, or the bound. The bound is the run's hard stop (its
deadline + HARD_STOP_AFTER_S 480 s: minute 63) and, for a gate's proofs, the gate's cap. A run the bound killed or would
not start is TIMEOUT. So are the PROVENs whose closing clean run the hard stop killed (they are never banked
unconfirmed). The fan-in names every TIMEOUT with its shard. The census lists TIMEOUT apart from "laws owed a fix", since
a law that only ran out of time is no defect. Publish's verdict still holds the deploy on a TIMEOUT of one of the push's
laws. With no bound set (his Mac, a PC's census) nothing is cut. Law: tv/test_a_gate_past_its_bound_is_cut_and_named.py
(17 red-proofs, 17 PROVEN).

### REG-3208 - NOTHING MEASURED OR PRUNED WHAT KEPT GROWING ON THE DISK, AND THE FIRST LANE FOR IT HAD NINE HOLES (v3865, his words 2026-11-05)
His words: "whatever keeps growing needs to have a looped system in place that prunes and extracts and saves any data informational that's needed". Measured that night: 6.9 GiB free, under his 8 GB ON AIR floor. What had grown: 94 scratch dirs in the temp root, ~3.3 GB of Grok-seat worktrees (some not merged, some not git trees), 2.2 GB of Claude's shipped worktrees, and a 2.7 GB clone holding one commit not upstream. Reel retention owns only reels and frames, grok_chat_prune only his Grok chats, and the doctor's disk headroom row only free GB.

tv/disk_growers.py is the lane. It works from a DECLARED registry (seat worktrees and scratch in /private/tmp, law fixtures in $TMPDIR, %TEMP% twins on Windows). Each pass goes measure -> salvage -> read back -> prune. It prunes only under a 16 GB watermark or past an age bound. Every entry starts in dry-run and arms itself after 3 clean passes over 24 h. The console runs it in the disk sign's pass, and the doctor row is "disk growers".

The adversarial review reproduced nine holes on temp fixtures, and each is now closed:
- lsof was asked once per pass, so a shell entering tree B after A's prune did not stop B's. It is now asked again before EACH prune (0.27 s).
- Age was mtime only, so a cp -Rp copy read 240 h old. Age is now the newer of mtime and ctime.
- One tree with no origin/main, or an untracked nested repo (IsADirectoryError), reset its whole entry's dry-run forever. A declared wait no longer fails arming.
- $TMPDIR (vault-law- 518, playwright-artifacts- 414) was undeclared. law-scratch entries now record each fixture with one manifest line.
- owed read 0 while an age was UNKNOWN, and a PC without psutil was UNKNOWN with nothing to prune. Holders are now lazy, and owed is None exactly when something was unread.
- A state reset was said nowhere. It is now said in the lane and the doctor.
- A lane that only waited for days read OK. The doctor now shows the reading's age and goes MISSING after 24 h unmeasured.
- A pass was unbounded. It now handles 200 growers and defers the rest as owed.

Law: tv/test_what_keeps_growing_is_salvaged_then_pruned.py (34 tests, 42 red-proofs, all PROVEN).

### REG-3209 - A GROWER'S INFORMATION IS SALVAGED AND READ BACK BEFORE IT IS PRUNED, AND THE SALVAGE NEVER COSTS THE DISK MORE THAN IT RELIEVES (v3865)
Claude had to salvage that 2.7 GB clone by hand (git cherry against origin/main, git format-patch, a README) before removing it.

The lane now salvages into tv/.salvage (git-ignored):
- every commit not upstream by patch-id, as a format-patch;
- the tracked dirty diff;
- untracked files under a cap (the larger ones are named);
- a clone's stashes;
- a scratch dir's summary, verdicts and log tails.

It reads every file back by sha256 and size, plus meta.json and its manifest line. A salvage that does not read back blocks the prune, and so does a tree whose upstream cannot be told.

The review found two more holes:
- git cherry skips merge commits, so a clone's conflict resolution was in no salvaged file and the clone was pruned. A tree with a merge commit not upstream is now also saved as history.bundle, and `git fetch <bundle> HEAD:refs/heads/salvaged` restores it.
- Patches, the dirty diff and stashes had no cap, and nothing checked free space: a 30 MB dirty binary became a 58 MB salvage on a disk at 2 GB free. Now:
  - every written byte counts against SALVAGE_CAP (20 MB), and past it the tree waits whole, never cut short;
  - a single diff whose touched files sum past READ_CAP (200 MB) is never read into memory;
  - nothing is written that would leave the salvage disk under 1 GB or push the salvage dir past 2 GB.

Same law as REG-3208.

### REG-3200 - THE VAULT LANE RE-RAN A HUNG REEL AFTER EVERY RELAUNCH, AND A READER BUMP THAT ANSWERS THE SAME ENDED ITS COOLDOWN (v3865)

MEASURED on his Mac 2026-11-05 (GET /api/status, /api/river, /api/fleet; his console log read only):
- The tick said *"8 owed, none startable this tick: 1 quarantined after a hang"*.
- The eagle said *"vault: 99 session(s), last did work 194.5 h ago - past the 48 h mark, so this lane has STOPPED"*.

WHAT THE 8 OWED REELS ARE:
- 7 are sealed by the current reader with 0 rows, and their one solo re-read is spent. The tick's sealed branch `continue`d without counting them, so they were passed over in silence.
- The 8th is reel 21967. It was cooling after 6 barren reads under vp3554, until 11-12.
- The 16:06 bump to vp-reg2915 is declared to answer the same as vp3554 (`VAULT_PROMPT_ANSWERS_SAME_AS`, so its seals stand). `_vault_cooling` compared versions exactly, so the bump ended the cooldown.

WHAT HAPPENED NEXT:
- The console booted at 20:27:26. The lane started 21967 at 20:28:43, the sweep hung 854 s, and the watchdog quarantined the reel in memory only.
- A relaunch hands an in-memory quarantine straight back. His log shows that loop on reel 20599: 4 quarantines on 10-17, three right after the v3759/v3760/v3761 boots. Reel 21967 has hung once.
- lane_health counted startable work for the chronicle lane only, so the vault lane could only ever read STOPPED.

⚠ **NOT A LOCK CONSEQUENCE.** vault_sweep_start never asks the self-arming lock, and the tick said "none startable", not LOCKED. Opening the locks starts none of the 8.

**FIX:**
- A hang is a persisted attempt (`.vault_autoread.json` "hung"). The reel backs off 30 min, then 2 h.
- A retry under the same reader is wall-clock bounded. Past 1200 s it gets the #130 stop at its next banked read, enforced from the 10 s rescue tick.
- One sweep counts as one attempt.
- After 3 hangs the reel shows amber *"needs a look: <MB, frames, filmed>, <why>"*. Ways out: a new reader, or POST /api/vault_sweep {"retryReel": <reel>} for exactly one more bounded try.
- The hold is checked at the picker and the start door, and it survives a relaunch.
- A run that returns having examined the reel in full takes it off the book.
- A new reader's first attempt is never capped.
- **One reader rule, `_vault_same_reader` (the seals' rule),** for the cooldown, its barren count, the hang hold, the hang count and the retry bound.
- The tick counts and names sealed reels (*"wait on a new vault reader"*) and the held reel's next try.
- `_vault_lane_reasons` uses the tick's own picker rule. lane_health asks it through the serving console, so a waiting vault lane reads BLOCKED with its own reasons.
- Paid reads only go down.

Laws:
- `test_a_hung_reel_gets_a_bounded_retry`: 21/21 PROVEN.
- `test_an_owing_vault_lane_says_what_each_reel_waits_on`: 9/9 PROVEN.
- `test_a_barren_held_reel_cools`: its REG-2561 sabotage re-anchored, 4/4 PROVEN.

### REG-3201 - THE EAGLE CALLED A REEL ITS OWN LANE WAS HOLDING "NO AUTOMATIC LANE" (v3865)

MEASURED on his Mac 2026-11-05 (GET only):
- The eagle said *"3 of 42 reel(s) sit at a station that owes work no automatic lane delivers (PRINTER 2, STATION 1)"*.
- The fleet's PRINTER row quoted the vault lane's whole queue (*"owes 8 ... 1 quarantined after a hang"*).
- The drain said *"waiting at STATION 1 behind STATION: A LANE EXISTS AND THIS QUEUE IS NOT ITS INPUT"*.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE:
- The STATION reel is 21967, the vault lane's own reel.
- The two PRINTER reels (52736, 17617) are in no lane's queue. The vault lane owes 8 without them, and the r4 review found retro_triage has both at full=true, panels=0.

**FIX:**
- `_station_delivery` decides per reel who moves it, from each lane's own rule: the vault picker `_vault_pass_reason`, the reel sweep's `_chron_reel_owes_a_read`, and REG-1749's `_proven_empty` veto.
- The doctor's river row, the live fleet stuck row and the drain's upstream reason (`_river_drain_why` over `_reels_at_station`) all use it.
- A hold that clears by itself (a hang's backoff, a cooldown, a reel still recording) is not counted. Every other wait is named.
- A check that could not be asked is the wait 'unknown' and names the failed check, never *"no lane's queue holds it"*. The doctor keeps the station reading for it and says it is UNKNOWN.
- A fixture shelf keeps the lane's own word.

Law: `test_every_station_has_a_lane_or_says_what_it_waits_on`, 18/18 PROVEN.

**OPEN RULING:** a triage-proven panel-free PRINTER reel has no lane that writes its seal. Retention's chain skips vault-owes for it, so it looks releasable once it leaves the newest 16. That is not verified on his data.

Pre-flight caught one more before GitHub did (test_the_eagles_pass_runs_in_a_child): the doctor asked the SERVING console for each reel's lane, but "the river" runs in the eagle's child (REG-2987), where the serving console is out of reach and a fresh import holds no retired / cooling / hung reels, so a held reel would have read as delivered. Moving the check into the console was measured and refused: one reel_router.route() on his Mac is +197 MB, the spike REG-2987 moved out. The doctor now asks the imported module after it restores the vault lane's store from disk - every input of the picker rule is persisted there - and a store that will not read is UNKNOWN.

### REG-3196 - A FAILED RIVER READ NEVER SAID WHY (v3865, his Fleet 2026-11-05 21:01)
His words: "i want the river flowing and the fleet rendering it properly that it is for each and for whoever is not fix it!".
OLD PC ALT's river.why read "a newer river read failed 1043 s ago - these lanes are the last good read" and nothing more. The
reason was recorded on that PC (_RIVER_LAST['fail']['why']) and never reached the wire, and it was only the exception's
class ("the river could not be read (KeyError)"). Now the failure keeps its message, scrubbed for the wire with _wire_text.
A newer failed read sends it in river.why and as river.failWhy / failAgeS, the worker forwards both (absent stays absent),
and the row draws a muted "last river read failed" with the reason in its hover. A failing river WALK now reaches it too

### REG-3130 - CLOSING THE WINDOWS OCR WORKER COULD HANG THE CLOSER LOOP: THE CLOSE WAITED ON A WRITE ONLY THE TERMINATE COULD FREE (v3860)
`close_ocr_worker` closed the worker's stdin (raw close, v3424/#185) and terminated it second. Windows' C runtime locks a
file descriptor for the whole of a write(), and close() takes that lock, so on win32 the raw close WAITED for a writer
stuck on a full pipe - and the terminate that would have freed it was queued behind the close. MEASURED 2026-11-04 on the
new Konyo · ALT (Python 3.12): close first still blocked after 12 s; terminate first returned in 0.0 s, the writer got
BrokenPipeError. The Windows OCR worker (ocr_win.ps1) runs through this routine. Fix: terminate first, then the raw close,
then the object close, each in its own try. Law test_a_broken_pipe_must_not_skip_the_reap: a venue-free model of the fd
lock (red on every OS with the old order), the real-pipe case now uses a SIGTERM-ignoring child so the raw close stays
load-bearing on POSIX; on the ALT the old order is red on both. The fork/zombie premise case is pinned to POSIX.
### REG-3131 - THE WINDOWS CONSOLE PROCESS RAN IN THE ANSI CODEPAGE; ONLY ITS CHILDREN WERE IN UTF-8 MODE (v3860)
control_app.py has set PYTHONUTF8 in os.environ at import since v1463 (win32), which reaches every child but cannot
change the running interpreter: the console itself read node's UTF-8 and opened files in cp1255/cp1252 (reader thread
dies -> stdout None, or a middle dot mojibakes). start_tvd_win.ps1 now sets PYTHONUTF8=1 and PYTHONIOENCODING before
Start-Process, and self_prove.spawn sets PYTHONUTF8 on win32 itself, so a census does not depend on WHO spawned it.
⚠ OWN-INSTRUMENT NOTE: the new ALT's census on 11-04 was a HAND runner whose env lacked PYTHONUTF8, and it filed at least
9 laws red that the console's own lane (which inherits the import-time setting) runs green; batches 2-4 on #230 were
corrected in 6637238383. Law test_a_windows_console_runs_in_utf8_mode (2 red-proofs, both RED).

kai caption, and no count may stand in for it. No code changed. Law: test_unread_text_is_shown_as_the_ocr_read_it gains

### REG-2987 - THE EAGLE'S DOCTOR PASS PEAKED THE CONSOLE'S OWN HEAP AT +500-800 MB EVERY TICK; IT RUNS IN A SHORT-LIVED CHILD NOW (#172, his priority 1)
REG-2985's spike profile (a scratch console of his Mac, his data, Python 3.9): with the source parses gone, every RSS spike
past 450 MB sat inside the eagle's in-process console_doctor.run - corroborate's readings, the eye audit, the run census, the

On a console the pass now runs in a short-lived child (audit_child.doctor_rows, `python3 audit_child.py doctor ...`) and its
memory leaves with it; the console asks only console_doctor.IN_PROCESS itself - the 15 rows that read the process they run in
(the serving module's fleet/presence state, sys.modules, os.getpid, the boot records PILLOW_BOOT/NUMPY_BOOT, the test-venue
memo) - and merges them in roster order. The rules: a stale answer is never served (each ask carries a nonce; its result file
is read only for that nonce and removed); one pass at a time; a child that fails, times out or writes nothing leaves the pass
UNKNOWN with no rows until the next tick - never derived in the console, never an older pass. The child runs below normal
priority (nice 10 / BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS) and writes its current check where eagle_state() publishes `measuring`
(inChild). His eagle button (/api/eagle) asks through the same door. run() gained `only`/`skip`; an `only` part primes no
per-tick cache. A law, the gate, CI and a CLI are not consoles and run the whole pass in their own process, as before.
MEASURED (the same scratch console, sandbox-exec denying his console and agent ports, 1500 s, eagle every 60 s):
  BEFORE (in-process pass; RSS only - footprint re-measured in a follow-up): console ru_maxrss 919 MB, per-pass RSS
  peaks 522-856 MB over 14 passes, RSS back to 34-56 MB after 11 of them (452/437/309 after three); console CPU 386 s,
  children 299 s (max 595 MB: the audit children, git, lsof).
  AFTER (pass in a child): console ru_maxrss 652 MB, per-pass RSS peaks 316-636 MB over 11 passes; footprint (resident +
  compressed) peaks 529-640 MB, between passes 163-586 MB with no upward trend; console CPU 177 s, children 639 s (max
  872 MB: the doctor child). Every child pass answered (140 rows; 38-40 s every tick, 284 s / 204 s with the periodic
  tier); no doctor child was left running after the console exited. The console imports 471 modules, not 528.
  The cost: total CPU 816 s against 685 s (+19%), a cold pass in a fresh process every tick, run below normal priority.
Law: test_the_eagles_pass_runs_in_a_child (8 tests, 11 red-proofs RED): an AST scan holds every process-bound check to
IN_PROCESS; a part asks only its part and primes nothing; a real child (pointed at a closed port) answers the rows this process
does; a stale, missing or unreadable answer and a timeout are UNKNOWN, never served; one pass at a time; the eagle asks the
child on its own cadence, merges in roster order, goes UNKNOWN when the child does not answer, and runs whole off a console;
the eagle button asks through the same door. Re-anchored: test_a_periodic_check_is_still_watched_unattended's red-proof (the

### REG-3081 - THE STALE COVERAGE FLOORS COULD BE RE-BLESSED NOWHERE (#2, still broken in its own note)
Task #2 names ~30 stale floors in tv/render_coverage.json: the push gate measures more nodes than the floor holds, so
that many watched nodes could vanish inside a green run. `render_check.py --bless` raises them and needs a browser. His
Mac does not run one for a suite, and no workflow ran it. NEW .github/workflows/render-bless.yml runs it on CI, under the
bless's own refusal rules, unchanged:
- the FULL set or nothing: no target is named, and a subset bless refuses;
- every target clean: one red or UNKNOWN target refuses, and the record names it (REG-3082);
- a floor only rises: a lower CI count is held and listed;
- a cold tree: a fresh checkout every run, no restored sandbox (v3215).
It starts by hand (workflow_dispatch, once on main) or from a push to ci/bless/**, never on main's pushes. Its token
reads only and it never commits. TV_RENDER_SCALE is set to render_bound.CAP, since no push hook kills a slow run there and
the job's own 40-minute ceiling stands.
One artifact is uploaded even when the bless refuses: the floor, its diff, the log, the record (hidden files included)
and the shots. The job summary is `render_bless.py report`, and the job's exit code is render_check's (PIPESTATUS, not
tee's). The floors it hands back are applied with `render_bless.py apply` (REG-3083) on the machine whose push gate
enforces them.
Law test_ci_blesses_coverage_on_a_full_cold_run (the workflow text, comments dropped), 6 cases, 8 red-proofs RED,
baseline green. The workflow is named in test_a_newer_ci_push_cancels_the_older_run's WORKFLOW_FILES, so its concurrency
block is held with every other ci workflow's; that law, the slow-mirror law and the push-cache law are green.
UNMEASURED: no run of the job yet. It needs a push to ci/bless/<x> or a dispatch from main. Expected blockers, read from
the code: the heart targets draw from tv/.heart2.json, which a cold checkout lacks (REG-2451: six heart readings "shrank"
