### REG-3083 - A FLOOR BLESSED ON CI COULD OUTRUN THE PUSH GATE THAT ENFORCES IT (#2)
CI's render-bless job (REG-3081) measures from a cold sandbox on a Linux Chromium. The floor it writes is enforced by the
push gate on his Mac. A CI count above what the Mac measures would refuse his next push ("measured X, was Y") over a node
that was never gone, at ~25 minutes a push. Its diff is a measurement, and not yet a floor this tree can carry.
NEW tv/render_bless.py, no browser:
- `report <record>` is the CI job's summary: complete or why it refused, every raise, hold and add.
- `apply <record> [--verdict PATH] [--write]` raises each floor to min(CI's count, the push gate's count), only where the
  push gate measured above the floor too. The push gate's count comes from this machine's tv/.render_verdict.json; its
  coverageStale rows are the widths its last full run measured above the floor.
- Both numbers are measurements, so nothing is invented and nothing is lowered.
- Refused whole: a CI record that is not complete, and a verdict that is not a full, clean, unaborted run with a known
  floor and no coverage refusal.
- A LIVE population (COVERAGE_VOLATILE) is never raised.
- --write changes only the floors it raises; the node signatures are diagnostics and stay.
Law test_a_ci_bless_never_outruns_the_push_gate (Python, fixtures only), 8 cases, 6 red-proofs RED (CI's count goes in
whole, a width the gate never measured above its floor is raised, a live population is raised, an unclean verdict speaks
for the gate, a raise lowers a floor, an incomplete record is applied), baseline green.

### REG-3082 - A BLESS LEFT ONLY A MERGED FLOOR, AND A REFUSED ONE LEFT NOTHING (#2)
`render_check.py --bless` writes tv/render_coverage.json, a merge in which a held count (lower than its floor), a raised
one and a new width look alike afterwards. A refused bless wrote nothing, and its one line said "this run did not report
every target" even when every target reported and one was red. On the machine that ran it the scrollback covers that. For
a bless made on another venue (CI's render-bless job, REG-3081) it would leave a floor and no measurement under it, or a
red job and no reason.
The bless now writes .render_bless.json beside the floor (so a law's temporary floor keeps its record with it):
- every count it measured;
- what it raised, held and added;
- or, refused, why: "it asked for N of M targets", "it stopped early at X", "N target(s) did not render cleanly (names)",
  "N target(s) were UNKNOWN". main() hands that reason in, and the refusal prints it.
The floor rules are untouched: it only rises, and a run that is not full and clean writes no floor. The record is
gitignored, a local fact like .render_verdict.json. test_render_coverage's one case that blesses the real floor file now
restores the record too, so its fixture bless never stands as the real one.
Law test_a_bless_records_what_it_measured (the real _coverage_bless and main(), the browser and the renders stubbed,
the floor in a temp file), 3 cases, 4 red-proofs RED, baseline green. Coverage neighbours green: test_render_coverage
(re-proved, bad 0 of 5), test_the_ratchet_is_not_skipped_by_a_subset, test_a_coverage_drop_can_be_named.

### REG-3089 - A RARE'S NAME FOLLOWED BY ITS BASE HAD NO HOME: "CHAOS WHORL RING", "RAVEN CASQUE CIRCLET" (#158)
Same measurement as REG-3087: every name of his last sweep was routed through the page's router in node on claude/int.
A ground label is two lines, the rare's name over its base, and the reader handed some over as one: "Chaos Whorl Ring",
"Dread Grip Demonhide Gloves" and "Raven Casque Circlet". The grammar read only the two-word shape, so these were "nothing
on the board recognises this name".
FIX: _rolledQuality reads the first two words as the rare. It keeps the rest as the rare's base (rq.base) when two things
hold:
- the builder's base table names it;
- its type is a slot the suffix can name (_rolledBaseFits, by the game's itypes: a Circlet is a helm, Demonhide Gloves are
  gloves).

### REG-3105 - A CONTAINER'S LOOK BECOMES A FULL LOOK ONLY WHEN EVERY TAKEN CELL IS NAMED ONCE; ANYTHING LESS ASKS HIM (#158 P4)
His design calls A and B (#230 c6473846977, approved for P4). The board assembles, because it owns the item sizes and the
receiver. window._vaultFullLookFrom works like this:
- It lays the session's named reads (each with its own frame, over the floor when scored: the one rule, _vaultLookCounts)
  on the container's taken cells (REG-3104), with _itemCells' sizes.
- A read may sit anywhere inside its item's footprint.
- Two reads of one name inside one footprint are one item; two cells are two copies (his Q1).
It stamps _vaultFullLook only when exactly ONE layout explains every taken cell exactly once, with no read on an empty
cell. Then the receiver's drain counts what is absent.
Anything less is never a look. It is a QUESTION in MOVE TASKS (d2r_vaultFullLookAsks, forked per profile), stored with
its evidence (the frame, the cells, the reads):
- a shared page's number is never read (his call B): "which shared page was this?", and his answer stamps it. A task row
  may hint; it never proves.
- a stash tab the read did not name: "which tab was this?", answered by him.
- a session that names no character: "whose stash was this?".
- cells no read in that session named (with the cells).
- a read on an empty cell, or two names on one cell (a conflict, with the reads).
- an item with no fixed size on this board.
- an unread panel. That container is not-complete, never empty.
- two layouts.
A full look of the same container clears its older questions. The frame gate holds it all: AUTO INTAKE off, a held vault,
or a shadow assembles nothing and asks nothing. A shadow draws the owner's questions read only, and every door that
answers or clears refuses there (REG-3095's guard form).
Found while proving it: `null >= 0` is true in JS, so a shared look with no page passed the page test. The receiver still
refused it. The null is now asked first.
GUARD: tv/test_a_container_look_is_whole_or_a_question.py, 5 cases through vaultAccumApply with a payload of the console's
shape (fixture names). 8 red-proofs, RED. On claude/int it is red: "_vaultFullLookAsks is not a function".

### REG-3104 - THE SWEEP COUNTED EACH CONTAINER'S TAKEN CELLS AND THREW THEM AWAY, SO NO FULL LOOK COULD BE MADE (#158 P4)
The board can stamp a FULL LOOK (window._vaultFullLook, REG-2892): a frame that shows a whole container, every cell its
item or empty. Nothing produced one. The reader names items from hover tooltips only. The pixel layer counted which cells
of the panel a read looked at are taken (vault_corpus.stash_occupancy / inventory_occupancy, REG-1889), but the sweep used
that count only to cross-check names and then dropped it.
FIX: the sweep now keeps that count.
- vault_retro.container_look runs on every read frame. It records the session, the frame, the frame's own capture time
  (f_<ms>), the container (the panel that was COUNTED) and its taken cells.
- vault_retro.newest_container_looks keeps the newest look of each (session, container).
- The result is published as the proposal's `containers`, and apply_payload carries it to the board.
What the container is:
- the bag is the inventory, whatever screen it sat beside;
- a stash tab's own grid is the personal stash or a shared page, by the read's tab;
- a tab the read did not name is None (UNKNOWN);
- a shared page's number is never read, so `page` is always None, and the board asks him which page it was (his call B).
A panel whose occupancy would not read is `occupied: None` with its reason, never an empty panel.
The board assembles the look (REG-3105).
GUARD: tv/test_a_sweep_carries_each_containers_own_cells.py, 6 cases on fixture occupancies, plus the sweep's join pinned
by its own lines. 5 red-proofs, RED. On claude/int (836921abc) it is red: 6 failed, "vault_retro has no attribute
container_look".

caption's width is known before layout. _hrtSvg now collects each lock's caption stack and places it from that width
(window._hrtFanPlace: 0.62 em a character, a full em outside ASCII - an overestimate by design): every stack keeps its
node's x (pulled inside the view box at the wedge's edges), drops straight down just clear of every box already placed,

/api/saves answer (REG-2926) into that section:

reads "cannot be made in game" (two hyphens), and so does MAGIC & RARE. They are said, not renamed: renaming a core

The room and the builder offered only characters this console's reels had read on two character-select visits, in the

### REG-2926 - THE CONSOLE HAD NO DOOR FOR THIS PC'S SAVE NAMES (#251)
REG-2925's reader had no route, so neither the Characters room nor the vault could ask what this PC's save folder names.
GET /api/saves answers control_app.saves_answer(), which is d2s_read.saves() behind one door. The answer is kept while
nothing in the save folders changes: each folder's mtime, and every .d2s's size and mtime, because a .d2s is read
whole. A folder that will not stat or list is never kept, and a failed look is UNKNOWN (chars None), never an empty
roster. Law test_the_console_answers_this_pcs_save_names (fixture folders passed in; the route passes none, so the
console reads its own PC), 6 cases, 3 red-proofs RED (the kept copy never used, a changed folder answered from the
kept copy, a failure read as no characters), baseline green.

### REG-2925 - THIS PC'S SAVE FOLDER NAMES ITS CHARACTERS, AND NOTHING READ IT (#251)
Measured 2026-10-29 on his two PCs: neither holds a .d2s, because his characters are online and Battle.net keeps them.
The D2R save folder holds one key-binding file per character played on that PC, <Name><id>.ctlo and/or .keyo, so it
names this PC's characters with their exact spelling and nothing else (no class, no level). The id is an account id:
the same character carries the same id on the Mac and the ALT, and a deleted and remade name gets a new one. On a Mac,
D2R runs in a CrossOver bottle, and the bottles live where CrossOver.conf's BottlePath says; the default bottle folder
was empty on his Mac. tv/d2s_read.py now reads it, read-only (listdir only; nothing opened but a .d2s; nothing
written).
- save_dirs: the Saved Games known folder on Windows; every bottle's drive_c/users/<user>/Saved Games on a Mac.
- save_roster: names only, and for each name how many ids carry it, never the ids themselves. No file time leaves,
  because a binding file's time is when its bindings were written, not when the character was played.
- saves: "no-folder" is chars None (UNKNOWN), never an empty list. A folder that exists and will not list is counted
  ("may be short", or UNKNOWN when nothing else was found), never read as empty. With no .d2s the answer says
  "no .d2s on this PC; online characters live on Battle.net".
Law test_this_pc_names_its_characters_from_its_saves (fixtures in the run's own scratch), 7 cases, 5 red-proofs RED
(ids leave, no folder reads empty, BottlePath ignored, a digit taken into the name, an unlistable folder skipped
silently), baseline green.

### REG-2996 - A LOCKER'S NEXT MULE WAS ASKED FOR AS "UNI-ARMOR #2", A NAME THE GAME REFUSES (#144, his ruling 2026-10-29 Q1)
A locker's Mule 2+ is a character he makes in the game (REG-2875), and MOVE TASKS asked him to "Create mule UNI-ARMOR #2 in
the game": a '#', a digit and a second '-', where a D2R name is 2-15 letters with at most one '-' or '_' and no digit
(REG-2980). His ruling: overflow names go "per locker, letters only (armor-A, weapon-A), one mule per category". One helper,
_vaultLockerMuleName(m, k), names a locker's Mule k (k >= 2) by its word and a letter: UNI-ARMOR's Mule 2 is ARMOR-A, Mule 3
ARMOR-B; UNI-WEAPONS' Mule 2 is WEAPON-A. A core locker's word rides its id (ARMOR, WEAPON, SMALL, SETSTALIK, SETSREST,
RUNEWORDS, SOCKETED, MAGICRARE, CHARMS, GRAILDUPES, WIP), so renaming the locker never renames a character he made; a mule he
added uses the letters of its own name (12 at most). Mule 1 is the locker's own character and gets no derived name.
_vaultLockerMuleSay(m, k) is the one spelling, "Mule 2 · ARMOR-A", used by the make task (its words and its tick's label), the
move row ("UNI-ARMOR · Mule 2 · ARMOR-A (9,3)"), the where-is cells (filed, hand-added and the planner's), FIND's target
cell, his hand spot's chip and his tick's refusal. The mule window's header for Mule 2 reads "UNI-ARMOR · ARMOR-A" (was
"UNI-ARMOR #2"). "Mule N" still opens each spelling, so REG-2884's page buttons read it as before.
Law: test_a_lockers_next_mule_is_named_by_a_name_the_game_accepts (3 tests, 8 red-proofs RED; 41 safe sibling laws green). Re-aimed: REG-2875's law (the
card-vs-target cells, the row and the make task read the page's helper; its rows must carry a legal name that maps back to k)
and REG-2884's law (Mule 2 in the helper's spelling; its red-proof [0] follows the new _findTargetSay call); REG-2875's
red-proofs [3] and [5] follow the lines this changed (re-proved RED). The v3769 law's slice carries the two helpers. Not pinned by a law: the planner's cells (_orgPlannedCells), the hand spot's chip and the tick's
refusal - each uses the same helper. Not built: a read on a character named ARMOR-A closing its make task, as a read on WAR-A
closes the war mule's (REG-2803); his tick still closes it.

### REG-3070 - THE CHARACTER WINDOW DREW A WORN ITEM BY ITS NAME, NOT ITS SLOT: FORTITUDE AS ARMOR DREW A CRYSTAL SWORD (GrokBot 04:03, #36)
GrokBot on the character window: each worn item drew by its own NAME, #248's defect again on the one surface that has
only a name. A runeword drew the base its picture is keyed to, whatever the slot: Fortitude in the Armor slot drew
hd_crystal_sword, and Plague and Splendor drew another slot's base too. A rare's name or a plain word drew nothing at all:
Carrion Greaves, Wraith Grasp, Dragon Talon, and the bare "Shield", "Armor" and "Boots" a read sometimes leaves.
FIX: _cbSlotArtName(name, slot, base) in the builder's block, asked by _chxDollHtml. This is #248's rule, given the slot:
- A unique or set item draws its own graphic.
- A recorded base of THAT slot's type draws that base. A plain base names itself, when it is of that slot's type.
- A runeword draws a base of that slot's type it can be made in. Its own picture stays when it is one (Enigma's plate
  mail on the torso, Fortitude's crystal sword in the hand), and is dropped when it is another slot's (Fortitude's
  crystal sword on the torso). The slot's own kind comes first: in the off-hand a shield beats a second weapon, so
  Spirit draws a shield and Lawbringer, which cannot be one, a sword.
- Anything else draws a base of that slot's type: a rare's name, a bare word, or a runeword read in a slot it cannot be
  made for.
- A name the database lacks that has its own picture keeps it.
- null when the builder's database cannot be read. The doll draws that as UNKNOWN.
The slot's kinds are the builder's own rail categories (the planner's Shields, Body Armor, Helmets ...). No table was
added.
NOT CHANGED: the gear ledger records no base today (its rows carry item, sightings, tier, ts and reel). The `base`
argument is ready for a reader that records one.

### REG-3004 - A RUNE, GEM OR MATERIAL TYPED BY HAND NOW MOVES ITS TALLY UP OR DOWN THROUGH THE TOOLS TAB'S OWN DOOR (his Q5, #144)
His ask: a rune, gem or material added by hand may move its tally up or down, and the tools section already has a
tally up/down control for a misread.
WHAT EXISTED:
- The Tools tab's Rune Stash, Gem Stash and Materials cards move a count one at a time through adjustRuneStash,

- _stashTallyMove(name, delta) uses _stashTallyOf (REG-2899's one rule) to pick the tally, and moves it through that
  tally's own adjust function. It reads the count before and after and says "Ber Rune - the Rune Stash 0 -> 1". It
  refuses a -1 at zero and never touches the owned list.

  row is its +1.
- The read chip's +1 now asks the same door.

Left alone, because they are a different door: the ledger restore's merge-max apply and the photo intakes. Both SET a
count to a measured figure; neither steps it.
GUARD: tv/test_a_hand_add_moves_a_count_through_the_tools_door.py, 5 cases. It puts a spy on each door and checks:
- up and down by hand;
- never below zero;
- the add box's row and Enter;
- the read chip asks the door;
- no store is stepped by one outside its door.
5 red-proofs, all RED.

### REG-3076 - 90 SPEC PINS ON A STORE THE BOARD WRITES BACK WERE WRITTEN BETWEEN TWO LOADS (#161, after REG-3059)
REG-3059's shape on v527: a spec writes a store with page.evaluate, then reloads, over a first page that holds its
own copy of that store in memory (persist() writes 21 stores back whole). v527 failed that way on v3818 and v3839; which
writer put the store back is UNMEASURED - a node replay does not reproduce persist() as the writer (REG-3059 as corrected
in v3840). REG-3059 fixed that one spec by hand. Swept: 90 more pins in 54 specs, read with a scan that skips comments:
- 75 followed by page.reload() in 45 specs (rwMade 46, owned 35, runeStash 23, setPieces 8, unknownReads 5, copies 2,
  wishlist 2; a pin often sets several). The first count was 66: a scanner that did not skip comments read "main's" as
  a quote and lost 8. One, v637's 'L·d2r_rwMade', sits under a world prefix: agent-guide's list had it, this scan
  did not, and now reads keys under LSR's prefixes;
- 8 followed by page.goto(URL) in 7 specs, plus a goto between a pin and its reload in v631;
- 3 seeding helpers whose key is an argument (reg2410 seeds d2r_owned, v1625 rwMade and setPieces, reg2414 two vault
  stores);
- 4 that pass a named constant: v2200's and v2203's SEED, an expression string writing owned and setPieces, then
  page.goto. Found by CI, not by the first scan: v2200:53 was flaky on b26d0cbec (green on retry) and red on both
  attempts on main 014d4fc3d.
tests/_pin.ts: pinEvaluate(page, fn, arg) runs the spec's own function - or expression string, as page.evaluate takes -
records the localStorage writes it made, and replays them in a ONE-SHOT init script (a sessionStorage mark) before the
next document's own scripts; a function that returns a promise is refused, by name. reloadPinned(page) /
gotoPinned(page, url) load again and check every pin's mark, naming the pin's file:line and keys if it never reached the
boot. Known reach: the premise proves the pin reached the next boot, not that nothing in that boot rewrote it - a writer
inside the reload's own boot would still win, and the spec's own assertion would then go red. LSR.setItem skips a write
whose bytes already match, so such a key is not recorded. agent-guide's list of 52 (REG-3059, a lower bound by its own
account) reconciled against this sweep at c0f4f1e24: 42 converted here, v637 the one in-class miss (now converted),
and 9 out of this class - pins on d2r_chronicleInbox/InboxLog, ownerClaim, testGuest, foundLog and activeProfile, none
of them a store persist() writes; they stay as they are, named here.
Routine I on b26d0cbec (2,381 passed, 5 failed, 1 flaky) and 116e9b6a4 (2,380 passed, 5 failed, 2 flaky), with no pin
ever missing its boot: every converted spec green except v1630_sealed_stamp, whose 5 tests failed identically on the
base 3e0d8eac2 (REG-3056's landing; v3840's REG-3084 fixes it). v2200:53 stayed flaky with its SEED pinned - the same
"a migration overwrote his manual placement of 'Key of Hate'" - so d2r_muleAssign is rewritten in or after that boot:
a separate defect, the writer UNMEASURED, not this one. Every changed spec and the helper parse under node's type
stripper.

### REG-3059 - v527'S v536.2 SPEC PINNED ITS CHRONICLE BETWEEN TWO LOADS; NOTHING IN v3839 WIDENED IT - THE SAME SPEC FAILED ON v3818 (CI on ci/claude-v3839)
Routine I on c0f4f1e24, shard 9: tests/v527_loot_filter_card.spec.ts:97 ("owning a socket-correct base for the word
DROPS its base") expected insightHasBase true and got false, on both attempts. CI's trace: the reload's DOM already
drew the Chronicle at (99/99), and `_endgameFilterBases().names` was empty. That pair has one reading: Insight was made
again by the reload's boot. Unmade with no base, the filter would list Colossus Voulge; unmade with its base, the spec
passes.
WHAT v3839 CHANGED, measured rather than guessed: nothing that reaches this scenario.
- The same assertion failed on both attempts of ci/claude-v3818 bedb53b33 (2026-10-28), a build with none of v3839's
  code, and passed on the builds after it. It is an intermittent failure that takes both attempts of one run (2 of the
  last 200 Routine I runs), not a v3839 regression.
- Timing does not trigger it. v3839's two attempts spanned a 2.3 s and a 3.9 s navigation, and a 3 ms and a 387 ms pin,
  and both failed; v3837's green run sat between them (2.7 s, 6 ms). v3839's shard ran faster than v3837's (1100 s
  against 1294 s), so it was not a loaded runner either.
- The v3839 bible.html hunks do not touch this path. REG-3009's doors (_unconfirmedTicks, _ticksConfirm, _ticksClear)
  have no caller on the board: only the console calls them. The sunder art copy and the `_magicArtSrc` charm branch
  never read the Chronicle, and the trace holds no page error.
- A node replay of the whole sequence agrees: the first boot with the spec's stores, the pin, every queued timer,
  pagehide, beforeunload and visibilitychange, then all 43 stores carried into the reload's boot, with and without its
  #session hash. v3837's and v3839's bible.html come out identical: the pin holds (98 made), Insight is a make-now task
  on its Colossus Voulge, and the filter names nothing. Whatever puts Insight back runs only in Chrome, on a path the
  node world does not model (a resolved fetch, an observer, an image load). WHICH one is UNMEASURED.
The fragile part was the spec's pin. It wrote d2r_rwMade with page.evaluate between two loads, over a first page whose
in-memory rwMade is the seed floor (Insight included) and which persist() writes back whole. Fixed in the spec: the
pin rides a second addInitScript, with RUNEWORD_TIP's names read on the first load, so the reload's boot reads the pin
itself whatever the first page wrote last. A premise check (Insight not made after the reload) names the pin, not the
Forge. If the writer is in the reload's boot itself, that check goes red and says so; the fix is then incomplete and
the next look is in Chrome. The other v527 specs pin in their first init script or never reload. CI proves it. The
edited spec parses under node's type stripping, which refuses a planted bad file.
NOT SWEPT: 52 evaluate-then-reload pins across tests/*.spec.ts, most on stores persist() writes back. They are green
today and only CI can run them, so they are listed, not rewritten.
Corrected in v3840 (Claude, from agent-guide's measurement): the first entry said persist() put Insight back - an inference a node replay of the whole sequence does not reproduce; the writer is a Chrome-only path, UNMEASURED.

### REG-3045 - A CARRIED EXPORT IS TIED TO THE RUNTIME IT WAS PROVED UNDER, AND EVERY ENTRY IT BANKS SAYS WHO CARRIED IT (#186)
A carried export was tied to bytes, a HEAD and a platform word, but not to the interpreter: same bytes on the same OS under
another Python minor can prove differently. An export now records platform, Python major.minor and node (its major, or
"none" when no node is on PATH - measured absent; a node whose version cannot be read is unrecorded). A CARRIED import
(heart2 --import-proved --carried-by, what proof_carrier.take now runs) is refused whole unless: Python is recorded on both
sides and equal; node is recorded on both sides (unrecorded = UNKNOWN, refused) and, when both have one, the same major.
"none" on one side is an ABSENCE, not a mismatch: Dean has no node (REG-2354) and the ALT does, so refusing on it would
carry nothing, and the ALT's node proofs banked on Dean follow REG-2715's serve rule (not served where node is absent;
D2 below measured that this shuts no lock). The box/shard path into the Mac's push records the runtime and does not
enforce it, so CI's Linux shards stay importable. Each entry a carried import banks carries {by, key, head, platform, at,
importedAt}; a proof this PC already serves keeps its own. Law: as REG-3047; red-proofs RED.

### REG-3044 - A PROOF OF ANOTHER PC'S VENUE, OR OF AN OS THIS ONE IS NOT, IS NEVER BANKED FROM ANOTHER PC (#186)
A proof's key digests tracked bytes, so an imported PROVEN re-keyed on this PC's bytes is a proof of those bytes - except
where the proof measured the PC. Five capabilities are venue, not code (heart2 PROOF_NEEDS_HOST): d2r-install, live-console,
human-eyes-ledger, reel-shelf, overlap-venue; an ALT PROVEN for one re-keyed identically on Dean and was banked, then served
wherever Dean had the capability. And an OS-bound proof (macos, posix, posix-signals) was checked only by the carrier's one
platform word, never per entry, and not at all on the box path. proof_shard.carry_refusal is now the one rule, asked of
every entry of every import with THIS tree's declaration of that proof (never the file's): venue -> never carried; OS ->
only when both platforms satisfy the need (an export that does not record its platform carries none); tool needs (node,
bash, numpy, dir-link) and no need -> carried as before. Every PROOF_NEEDS_HOST name is in exactly one class (a law holds
it). D2, MEASURED for his question on a fixture census shaped like Dean's (no node; temp census, cache and red memory):
118 gates declare a node proof (628 proofs), 2-16 of each lock's guard laws among them; proved with node absent, an
all-node law files UNPROVABLE and a mixed one PROVEN, both with their gate digest banked and blind empty; on a stamped census
of that shape the global heart rule reads "census current, 0 blind" and every lock takes that answer. So an ELSEWHERE node
law shuts no lock, and REG-2715's rule (a proof needing what this PC lacks is not served) stands. Law:
tv/test_a_carried_proof_stands_only_where_it_was_earned.py (23 cases; with REG-3045..3047, 21 red-proofs, all RED).

### REG-3102 - ONE RED-PROOF GREW A PROCESS CHAIN THAT RAN A HOSTED RUNNER OUT OF MEMORY, SO THE SITE COULD NOT DEPLOY
Publish 40812615686's proof shard 7 died twice ("The runner has received a shutdown signal", exit 143, at 04:17:30 and
05:18:15), so nothing after v3836 deployed. Every gate's clean run passed both times. The one gate that never finished was
test_a_source_audit_runs_in_a_child, and both deaths came about 2 min (142 s, 125 s) after its lane printed "6 line(s)
held", i.e. during RED_PROOF[6]. That proof makes audit_child.wanted() say yes in every process, and wanted() was the only
thing stopping a child from spawning a child. The law's setUpClass spawned a lane_spans child; that child's own
_lane_spans() found no cache and spawned the next, and so on. Measured on a bounded copy (its own process group, a depth
cap, a fixture TV_HIST): a new level every ~0.19 s, each holding ~72 MB RSS, and nothing derived until audit_child's 180 s
timeout. That is about 370 MB/s on his Mac, which fills a 16 GB runner well inside the timeout. heart2's
subprocess.run(timeout=...) kills only the law, never its orphans. The same proof run on a tree without this fix (sab, a
local prove) grows the same chain on that machine.
Fixed: audit_child.run() itself refuses inside a child (TVD_AUDIT_CHILD=1), and the child derives in its own process.
Re-probed with the same tamper: zero spawns, the cache written, rc 0. Law: test_a_source_audit_runs_in_a_child gains
AChildNeverSpawnsAChild (a child asked to spawn derives itself; baseline: a console still spawns) and RED_PROOF[9] (the
refusal removed). Still open: heart2 runs a law without its own process group, so a future runaway would still outlive
its law.

Before REG-3038, _serve_hist ran sips itself and served the full frame when `r.returncode != 0 or not os.path.isfile(cached)`.
REG-3038 moved that call into shadow_sessions.make_derivative, whose _sips_thumb judged only that the output file existed
(`return os.path.isfile(dst)`) - the digest's rule, which never needed more. On a Mac, a sips that exits non-zero after
leaving a broken file would then count as a made derivative, be kept in cache160/cache1280, and be served to the Shelf scrub
and the theatre from then on - a regression REG-3038 would have shipped on his own console, caught reading its diff
before it landed in a version. _sips_thumb now returns `r.returncode == 0 and os.path.isfile(dst)`, so a failed sips makes
nothing and the next resizer (Pillow, written beside and moved over the broken file) or the full frame answers, as before.
Law: test_a_windows_theatre_serves_small_frames gains AFailedSipsIsNoDerivative (a Mac console whose sips writes junk and
exits 1 still serves a 160 px frame; 1 red-proof, RED).

### REG-3024 - A REFUSED DAILY PICK WROTE NOTHING AND SAID NOTHING, SO AN EARLIER DAY'S PICK READ AS TODAY'S (#158)
dailyCreateAi read its answer with r.json() and kept a pick only when the body carried an answer, so a refusal in any shape
(the cap, an error body, a 502 with no body, a fetch that threw) wrote no pick - correctly - and said nothing: the card went
on showing an earlier day's sentence under "Today's pick", and the day's stamp stayed, so it was not asked again until
midnight. It now reads its answer through window._intakeAnswer; a refusal still writes no pick, takes the day's stamp off (the
next load asks again) and the card says "Today's pick: not read - <the refusal rule's sentence> · the last pick it read: ..."
(window._createNowAiBanner, the one line renderCreateNow draws; window._intakeNotReadSay(null, why) is the count-less form).
The console's task-force card, which reads the stored pick on its own, is not changed. Law:
tv/test_a_refusal_is_never_a_read_at_any_door.py (TheDailyPickSaysARefusalAndWritesNoPick, every refusal shape); red-proofs RED.

### REG-3021 - ONE CAP RULE: A CAP ENDS THE BATCH AT EVERY DOOR, AND THE VAULT INTAKE STOPS FOR THE SUBSCRIPTION CAP (#158, his ruling)
Measured in node on c70a8187b, a five-shot batch where every answer was the subscription cap: the set tracker, the craft
workshop, the Chronicle and grail screenshot readers and the vault grid counter each asked the reader 5 times, and the tally
reader 15 (three voting passes a shot). The vault intake has stopped a batch at an API usage limit since v438 (_aiLimitHit),
but read at the code (it is not run in node) its test never knew the subscription cap (429 + {error:'subscription-cap'}),
and its first read counted a 429 as an error before the test could see it. His ruling: one cap rule at every door - a cap
means the rest of the batch is not read for the cap's reason, never re-asked. window._intakeIsCap(status, body) is that rule
(the subscription cap, or a 402 / the v438 usage-limit words - the vault intake's own test, moved beside the refusal rule), and
the answer reader names a cap (`cap`). Every batch door stops at the first cap: the shots after it are not sent, each is
counted "not read" with the cap's sentence (the Chronicle reader lists each such page in `refused`), and what was read before
it is kept. The tally reader stops its passes at a cap and carries it through the one `why` every tally reader hands to all
the shots of its batch. The vault intake raises its own stop on a cap, and its banner says the cap's sentence ("... - the rest
of this batch was not asked") instead of the Anthropic monthly-cap text. The refusal rule also reads the website's upstream
reason from `detail` (it said only "the reader refused (upstream)"). A refusal that is not a cap (a 502) still does not end the
batch. Not changed: the vault intake's locate and empty-read retry reads, which ignore a refused retry as before, and the item
checker's judge (one frame a call, not a batch). Law: tv/test_a_refusal_is_never_a_read_at_any_door.py (ACapEndsTheBatch -
all-capped, capped mid-batch, a usage limit, a 502 that must not stop the batch, counting the asks; the vault's _aiIsLimit and
_aiLimitMsg run in node, its first read's stop pinned at the line); red-proofs RED.

### REG-2979 - THE SET TRACKER AND THE CRAFT WORKSHOP CALLED A REFUSED SHOT "NOTHING RECOGNISED" (#158, v3834 second eye)

tv/test_a_refusal_is_never_a_read_at_any_door.py (both doors, six shapes, a part batch); red-proofs RED.

### REG-2978 - A 429 OR A 502 WITH NO JSON BODY THREW BEFORE THE REFUSAL RULE SAW ITS STATUS, AND A CAP LOST ITS SENTENCE (#158, v3834 second eye)
Reproduced in node on int-9: the Chronicle and grail screenshot readers and the Ask box called resp.json() before
_intakeRefused, so a 502 with an empty body or a 200 carrying HTML threw - the Chronicle reader filed an 'unreadable' page,
the grail reader said "no FOUND items could be read (1 image error)", the Ask box said "Unexpected end of JSON input - is the
site deployed". The item checker's upload ("read failed (server 429)"), the tally reader ("the intake answered HTTP 429",
"the intake said: upstream"), the vault grid counter (an error with no reason) and the vault intake ("AI service unreachable
· HTTP 429") asked the status first and dropped the body, so a cap never said it was a cap. One reader of the answer now
sits beside the rule: window._intakeAnswer(resp) takes the body as text, parses it when it is JSON, asks the rule of the
status and whatever came back, and calls a body that is no reading (empty, not JSON, not an object) a refusal with its own
sentence; window._intakeThrew(e) says a read that never happened. Every intake door reads through it, so the rule is asked in
one place (a law counts it). The grail import carries a part batch's unread shots to its toast and its report; the vault
grid counter returns its errWhy and the engine's vault-count receipt carries it (control_app). The tally reader's sentences
are now the rule's ("the reader answered HTTP 503", "the reader refused (overloaded)"); REG-2730's law re-aimed. Not changed:
the vault intake's v407 retry of a 200 + {error}, its locate and retry reads, and the daily pick (a refusal has no answer and
writes nothing). Law: tv/test_a_refusal_is_never_a_read_at_any_door.py; the vault intake is pinned at its line (read, not
run); red-proofs RED.

### REG-2967 - REG-2804'S ONE-TIME WAR-ROLE STAMP MADE ANOTHER TAB'S FIRST ROSTER SAVE A CONFLICT (found by agent-guide's sweep)

v3836 batch (it passed on v3834 and on CI). Bisected by reverting: REG-2804 alone. Its legacy migration set
`sh.warRoleV = 1` on the in-memory roster on EVERY board, including one that had never saved a roster, and wrote it only when
a name-made WAR mule changed - so memory differed from the store, and the cross-tab sync read that as an edit this tab made
and held the other tab's save as "stale". Now a never-saved roster is skipped (the default lockers carry no name-made WAR
mule), and on a saved roster the stamp is saved with it whether or not a mule changed, so memory equals the store. Law:

### REG-2894 - FIND NEVER SAID WHEN AN ITEM WAS LAST SEEN (intake design P2: "every record shows last seen <date>")
FIND named where each item sits and not when it was last seen, so a placement read on Oct 6 looked as current as one read
today. Each FIND row now says "last seen <date>" - the newest capture time the item's witness row records - through P1's
one helper (_vaultSeenTimes, REG-2816; cherry-picked onto this branch so there is one helper, never two). The helper now also
reads the receipt a filing row keeps (`ownedBy`), so a photo filed by his hand stays dated by when it was taken, and the
copy readout reads the same answer. No capture time says "no capture time", never today; a witness store that will not
read says UNKNOWN. Law: test_every_record_says_when_it_was_last_seen (whole page in node; 4 red-proofs RED).

### REG-2893 - AN OLD READ COULD STILL PLACE AN ITEM AFTER ITS STASH WAS SEEN WHOLE (intake design P2, his Q2)
His Q2: "A read older than the container's newest full look can't add, move or remove anything. It is kept as history."
Nothing compared a read with any look of its container. `window._vaultStaleRead` now does, at the tvVaultRegister door as
one separate call (agent-111's removal rule sits at the same door): a read whose container (the holder and location its look
names) has a full look newer than the read - or a read with no capture time once that container has one, since an undated
read cannot be shown to be newer - is refused (`refused: 'stale'`, its own reason) and files nothing; the register's ledger
row still records it with the reason, which is the history it is kept as. A newer read, a read that names no container, a
container never looked at whole, and his hand are untouched. Law: test_a_full_look_outranks_an_older_read (with REG-2892,
8 red-proofs RED).

### REG-2892 - THERE WAS NO SUCH THING AS A FULL LOOK, SO NOTHING COULD BE PROVEN GONE OR STALE (intake design P2)
His design: "A full look is a frame that shows a whole container ... the container's truth at that capture time." REG-2861
made the drain count absence only from a frame that says complete:true; nothing defined what such a frame must carry or
recorded one. `window._vaultFullLook` is the contract and its receivers: complete:true, the container (holder, location
stash / inventory / shared, a shared page's number), the capture time, the session and frame, and EVERY cell of the grid
once - its item or empty (window.MULE_GRID, from the packer's own constants). Anything less is refused in words and stamps
nothing. A full look feeds the drain (complete:true, slot_identity's cell keys, a shared page's rows stacked) and stamps
d2r_vaultFullLooks - the newest look per container, forked per profile like the records; an older look is history and
changes nothing. No producer was faked: the console's vault reader names items from hover tooltips only (tv_diablo
VAULT_READ_PROMPT: "the grid itself prints none"; vault_doctor's 220 occupied cells and zero names), so no sweep frame is a
whole container. The producers it waits for are the guided sweep (P4) and P2's full-look detection.
Law: test_a_full_look_outranks_an_older_read.

### REG-2891 - A LIVE READ'S LOOK CARRIED NO TIME, AND THE GATE AND THE FILING ROW DROPPED ONE THAT DID (intake design P2)
A read row carries two clocks: `ts`, when the read landed (the board orders reads by it), and `captureTs`, the frame's own
capture time (tv_diablo: "captureTs must be the FRAME's capture ms, not the receipt-landing time"). Measured: bible.html
read `captureTs` nowhere, `_vaultLiveWitness` built a look with no time, so the live receipt was undated; and a look that
did carry a time lost it at `_vaultWitnessCheck` (it kept id/frame/conf/holder/loc/cell) and at vaultFile's filing looks -
P1 measured 0 of 20 filing looks dated. The live look and its witness now carry `captureTs` (never `ts`; none = undated),
the gate keeps a look's `at` when it reads as a time (never invented) and the filing row keeps it. Law:
test_a_read_carries_when_it_was_captured (whole page in node; with REG-2890, 7 red-proofs RED); test_v3767_intake_identity's
two red-proofs on the gate and the filing looks re-aimed over the new line and re-proved RED.

### REG-2890 - A PHOTO WAS DATED BY WHEN IT WAS DROPPED, NOT WHEN IT WAS TAKEN (intake design P2, #230 c6473846977)
His design: "Capture time, never arrival time. A photo takes its file's capture date." Measured: vaultIntake's hand witness
stamped `at: new Date()` and a folder or TV photo carried no time, so its receipt fell back to the door's clock - an Oct 6
screenshot dropped today read as seen today. Each file's own clock (File.lastModified, the moment the game wrote it; no
EXIF reader exists in this repo and none was added) now rides on the photo's look (`at`) and its receipt (`ts`, which the
owned door marks measured), through one door each (_vaultShotTime, _vaultPhotoWitness, _vaultPhotoReceipt), and the scan
report says "taken <date> - <date> - N with capture time unknown". A file with no clock gets no time and its receipt stays
unmeasured. A hand upload's own `at` stays the moment he declared it. Law: test_a_read_carries_when_it_was_captured.

### REG-2962 - THE DEPLOY NEVER WAITED FOR A PROOF; NOW NOTHING A PUSH CHANGED PUBLISHES UNPROVEN (#161 stage 2)

publish.yml's deploy needed [smoke, suites, review]; no proof ran on main, so the laws' red-proofs were proved only by the hook on his Mac. Publish now CALLS proof-keys-shards.yml (job `proof`, gate deploy, actions: read) and the deploy needs it. In the deploy gate a shard never fails the run itself - each failure is named in its manifest (owed, REG-2591) - and the fan-in's verdict (`tv/proof_shard.py --deploy-verdict`) passes only when the proof set is whole and no law this push changed since the last commit Publish published is owed a fix; a law only the Mac can prove is left to the hook, and with no last publish or a diff git cannot take, every law is this push's. A law owed a fix that the push did not change is said and never holds the deploy (the hook never proved unchanged laws either). The last proof-keys run (10-23, ci/proof-keys-c9c6b4b08153) ended with 6 of its 16 shards failing, so a gate on every law would have stopped every deploy. Law test_the_deploy_waits_for_the_proof_of_its_laws (9 cases), 7 red-proofs RED. The workflow itself is CI's to prove on a ci/ branch.

### REG-2961 - CI PROVED EVERY LAW FROM AN EMPTY CACHE ON EVERY RUN (#161 stage 2)

Each proof-keys shard proved into an empty $RUNNER_TEMP cache (REG-2585), so CI re-proved every law each run (~41 min a shard) while the Mac reused byte-identical proofs. Each shard now restores the proofs the last main run banked (actions/cache, prefix heart2-proofs-) as a READ-ONLY seed (HEART2_SHARD_SEED, read only in a proof shard); the main run's fan-in merges the shards' PROVENs into the next seed (`tv/proof_shard.py --merge-shards`, servable only, the newer of two) and saves it from main only (main's cache scope is the one every branch may restore). Safety checked in code before relying on it: _VerdictCache._key is a sha256 over the law, the proof, the gate spec and every input's path and bytes, and peek() looks an entry up only under the key key_for() takes from the checkout's bytes now - so a seed of any commit serves a proof only over byte-identical inputs (pinned on a fixture sandbox whose subject changes). The shard's own file still starts empty and holds only what the run served or proved for its own plan, so the fan-in and the Mac's all-or-nothing import never see a stray proof. test_a_proven_verdict_is_reused_only_on_identical_bytes re-aimed to admit the seed's two lines. Law test_ci_reuses_a_proof_only_for_identical_bytes (8 cases), 7 red-proofs RED.
### REG-2915 - THE TOOLTIP CROP COULD NEVER BE CUT ON HIS REELS: DIFFERENCING FINDS THE WHOLE SCREEN (#158.7)
The crop that NAMED an item (#45, v2239) was found by differencing a hover frame against the one before it. On his reels the
D2R world animates behind the panel, so the change box covers 53-91% of the frame and the 60 KB cap rightly refuses it - the
lane cut nothing. The vision read that names the item already saw the tooltip: VAULT_READ_PROMPT now asks for its box ("tip":
[left, top, right, bottom] in the picture the reader saw), normalize_item keeps a valid one, and the sweep cuts the crop from
it (vault_retro._crop_from_box): the box is placed on the frame through the read's own picture map (the one its item points
use), padded 2% of the frame each side, kept inside the frame, and scaled to a 512 px longest side - MEASURED on the 31 crops
his Mac kept: at their own size they run to 61 KB, against the 60 KB cap; at 512 px, at most 45 KB. The byte cap stays the
backstop. A read with no box behaves as before (the frame-difference crop, or why there is none) and says "the read gave no
tooltip box (UNKNOWN)"; a box with no picture map is UNKNOWN, and one covering more of the frame than a tooltip can is
refused - never a full-frame crop. Each look says how its crop was cut (cropFrom). The crop stays evidence to look at, never a
witness. VAULT_PROMPT_VER is vp-reg2915 and lists vp3554 as asking the same question, so no sealed reel reopens: crops come
from reads made from now on. Law: test_the_tooltip_crop_comes_from_the_read_that_named_it (8 cases on a fixture reel whose
frames all differ, through vault_retro.sweep with a stubbed reader; 7 red-proofs, each RED).

(`rotates`). Read in the code, every delete call in those reaches is the console's own bookkeeping: stop_agent (PID_PATH, the
live eye frame), _stop_capture and _capture_health (CAP_PID_PATH), _force_kill_all_agents (PID_PATH), _launcher_picture (the
temporary picture it took itself) and _clear_exit_on_purpose (its own marker) - never a reel, his footage, a ledger or the
vault. Each lane now declares those functions in a `clears` clause and auto_scope.CLEARS names the exact target each one
removes. clears_report reads every delete call in the lane's reach from the syntax tree (a comment is not a call), and the
reporter permits the row only when each is a declared function removing a declared target: a new delete, a new target, a

declaration was made to match the code - and the `never` lines stop saying nothing is removed. After: all four rows
permitted. Law: test_a_lane_clears_only_what_it_declares (14 cases, a class per lane; 4 red-proofs, each widening one
lane's reach, each RED); test_auto_scope's permission case re-aimed to 'a clause that covers it' and renamed.
### REG-2984 - THE CACHE LAW AND THE FORECAST LAW PINNED "A LISTING LAW IS NEVER CACHED"; THEY NOW PIN THE TRACED KEY (REG-2944)
test_a_proven_verdict_is_reused_only_on_identical_bytes's case "a law that lists a directory itself is never cached" and
test_a_push_records_its_forecast_and_actual's "a law that lists a directory is UNKEYABLE" were the old floor, written down
- and REG-2944 retires that floor on purpose. Re-aimed, not deleted: the cache case now drives the REAL push and proves a
listing law is banked with listed=["tv"], reused over an identical tree, and re-proved when a file joins tv/ (its red-proof
re-aimed: a listing law keyed as if it did not list is served the old PROVEN); the forecast case calls a listing law FULL
(it will run until its trace keys it) and keeps "UNKEYABLE with its reason" on a law whose PROOF_NEEDS is footage.

### REG-2983 - THE PUSH RECORD SAYS HOW MANY LISTING LAWS ITS TRACE KEYED, AND WHY THE REST WERE NOT (REG-2944)
A listing law is TRACED-keyable by the static walk and banked only when its run's trace is complete and stays in the tree,
so whether it was actually banked is a fact of each push, never of a file. The RECORD carries tracedListing {banked,
refused, why} and a line: "REG-2944 listing laws: N PROVEN(s) banked under what their traced run listed, M not banked -
<reason> xK" (a browser law's Chrome child is untraced, so its refusals read there as a number).

### REG-2981 - A LISTED DIRECTORY'S GITIGNORED ENTRIES ARE NOT KEY MATERIAL, AND A RUN THAT READ ONE NEVER BANKS (REG-2944)
#242's rule - runtime data is never a key input - carried into the listing key, as a decision with its reason. THE PROVING
SANDBOX DOES CARRY GITIGNORED FILES: safe_copy copies everything outside its HEAVY dirs (measured on his tree, names only:
151 gitignored files in tv/ - 87 .json, 19 .jsonl, 12 .png, logs, a pid, a lock, mkstemp temps; none a .py). So a
gitignored newcomer in a listed directory does NOT re-key (keying runtime names would move every key between the pre-prove
and the hook, #242's measured reuse loss), and to keep runtime CONTENT out of every banked verdict, a run whose trace READ or
STAT'ed a gitignored entry of a directory it listed is never banked. What stays outside the key, named: a law whose verdict
turns on the mere PRESENCE or COUNT of a gitignored file in a directory it lists. Untracked-but-unignored files (a law not
yet added) are key material like tracked ones. THE FLOOR IS A NUMBER, NEVER A HOPE (his addition): each banked listing
entry records ignoredSeen - how many gitignored names its listed directories held when it banked - and the census law
reads every traced law's listing calls, takes the filter each applies (a glob's pattern, or the endswith / startswith
constants of the loop it feeds) and tests it against a name for every .gitignore pattern: a listing with no filter, or one
whose filter can match a gitignored name, must stand in its EXPOSED map with the reason it is safe (22 laws today: his
footage or home that no sandbox carries, its own scratch, a listing it opens entry by entry, or - named as the floor - two
censuses that count on purpose: fixtures/ by size, art/*.png). A new law that counts every entry fails there by name.

### REG-2944 - A LAW THAT LISTS A DIRECTORY IS KEYED BY WHAT ITS TRACED RUN LISTED (REG-2296, FOR PROOFS)
63 laws could never have a proof saved, most of them censuses whose denominator IS a tree folder: heart2's static walk
refused any law FILE calling os.listdir / os.walk / glob ("what it reads is decided at run time"). gate_ledger already keys
a gate's PASS by what its traced run listed (REG-2296); this is that move for a PROOF. THE TRACE: the REG-2640 sitecustomize
also logs every os.listdir / os.scandir (and glob's own event) as `L <full real path>`, skipping the import system's own
listings of sys.path (the same frame check gate_trace uses); _trace_read collects them and _trace_record unions them per
law. THE KEY: a listing law's pre-run key is PENDING ("pending-listing:<digest>") - taken again after the run, never stored.
At bank time it becomes v3: the v1/v2 material plus, for each directory any traced run of it listed, the sorted names of its
tracked or kept entries with each file's bytes (an absent directory is material too). Lookup recomputes v3 from the tree as
it is NOW for each recorded listed-set (the newest 8), so an added, removed or changed file in a listed directory is a miss
and nothing else is. Never banked: an incomplete trace, a listing outside the tree (his home, /proc, the shared temp dir),
a run that read a gitignored entry (REG-2981). The run's own fixture_tmp scratch (d2r-test-<pid>-) adds nothing. MIGRATION:
none - a law that does not list keeps its v1/v2 key byte for byte (pinned), and listing laws had no entries.
THE CLOSURE-LISTING FLOOR, A DECISION: a law that lists only through a module it imports (gate_files() and the like) keeps
its v1/v2 key and is not keyed by its listings - keying those would re-key nearly every heart law on any tv/ change and
cost the wall clock this exists to save.
WHAT IT BUYS, honestly: a tv/*.py census re-keys whenever ANY tv/*.py changes, and most pushes change one. The win is the
pushes that leave its listed directories alone and every identical-bytes rerun (the pre-prove then the hook, a retry),
which today re-prove every listing law from nothing. The RECORD's REG-2983 line counts what was banked.
Law: test_a_listing_law_is_keyed_by_what_it_listed - a pending key is never served; a complete trace banks and an
identical tree serves; a planted new file, a removed file, a changed byte and an unignored newcomer each re-key; a file
elsewhere does not; a gitignored newcomer does not and a run that read one never banks; no key matches across a listing
change; a listing outside the tree never banks and own scratch does; an incomplete trace banks nothing; a law that lists
nothing keeps its v1 key; and the REAL trace hook, in a child python, records a listdir and a glob and not an import.
9 red-proofs, each RED for its own assertion.

### REG-2943 - A SIGTERM MID-PUSH EXITED WITHOUT WRITING WHAT THE PUSH HAD ALREADY BANKED (#150)
heart2._on_fatal_signal removed the sandboxes and os._exit()ed; os._exit skips atexit, so whatever store() had banked since
the last per-gate flush (and the cache's usedAt marks) never reached the disk. It now flushes the push's verdict cache
first (_flush_on_kill): only entries already STORED - never a PROVEN still in _CLEAN.pending, which no green clean run has
bracketed - and only when the cache's lock is free, because the signal may have landed inside code that holds it and a
handler that blocks there never exits. SIGKILL cannot be caught at all, which is why REG-2942 writes at each checkpoint.
Law: test_a_killed_push_keeps_what_it_proved (a child that SIGTERMs itself leaves the banked entry on disk and not the
waiting one); its proof declares "posix-signals", so a PC that cannot send itself a signal files it ELSEWHERE.

### REG-2942 - A PUSH KILLED MID-GATE LOST EVERY PROOF THAT GATE HAD ALREADY PROVED (#150)
_prove_gate_push held every PROVEN in _CLEAN.pending until the gate's CLOSING clean run (REG-1988) and flushed per gate,
so a kill mid-gate - the hook's deadline, a Ctrl-C, a closed terminal - lost all of that gate's proofs (test_control: 27
at ~4 min each), and the next push proved them again. Banking each PROVEN the moment it returns was asked for and is NOT
sound: a gate's proofs share ONE clean run, and a proof can go red because earlier runs drifted the sandbox (state the key
does not hold) rather than because of its tamper - the case the closing run exists to catch. So the bracket moves earlier
instead of going away: once CHECKPOINT_EVERY (4) PROVENs wait and another proof is about to run, the gate's shared clean
run(s) are asked again (_checkpoint_bank). Green - every waiting PROVEN now sits between two green clean runs - banks them
through _bankable and the REG-2640 key and writes the cache to disk at once; red, unknown or raising banks nothing and
asks no further checkpoint, and the closing run judges the gate exactly as before. COST: at most one extra clean run per 4
freshly proved proofs in a gate (a gate re-proved from nothing pays up to 25% more runs; one with 4 or fewer fresh proofs
pays nothing; a proof served from the cache never counts). GAIN: a kill loses at most 4 proofs' work. CHECKPOINT_EVERY is
the one dial. THE REVIEW ADDED TWO RULES: a LATER red clean run of the same gate - a checkpoint or the closing run - takes
back every proof an earlier checkpoint of it banked (_checkpoint_revoke; the cache's new unstore() drops it from disk too,
never another run's newer proof of the same bytes), so no resume ever reuses one; and the push RECORD carries a #150 line -
checkpoints forecast and run, their cost in seconds, proofs banked early and the seconds of work a kill could no longer
lose, reds and what they took back, and SAVED: hits a killed run's checkpoint had banked (an entry keeps a `ckpt` mark
until its gate closes green, so only a gate that never closed counts as saved). A K that costs more than it saves is then
a number. Law: test_a_killed_push_keeps_what_it_proved - killed after a green checkpoint, the disk holds those 4; the
resumed push serves all 4 and runs only the 6 still owed; a red checkpoint banks nothing; a red second checkpoint takes
back what the first banked and the resume reuses none of it; a red closing run takes back both checkpoints' banks; an
unkilled gate of 10 pays exactly two checkpoints (4 clean runs) and leaves no mark; the record counts cost and saving.
10 red-proofs, each RED for its own assertion. The 21 laws that drive the push path and the other 41 runnable laws that
import heart2 pass with the change.

### REG-2941 - 28 LAWS LISTED ONLY THEIR OWN SCRATCH OR ONE FIXTURE FRAME, AND NONE OF THEIR PROOFS WAS EVER SAVED: 91 UNKEYABLE -> 63 (#173)
heart2 banks a PROVEN only under a byte key, and a law file that calls os.listdir / glob.glob / os.walk is UNKEYABLE
(what it reads is decided at run time), so every one of its proofs re-runs on every push it is in. tv/unkeyable_laws.json
listed 91 such laws holding 470 proofs. In 28 of them the listing could never read anything a byte key misses: it listed
a directory the law had just made in its own scratch, or took "the first .jpg" of one tracked fixture reel. Fixed by
the REG-2362 rule: each such listing is fixture_tmp.list_own / match_own (refuses any path outside this process's own
contained scratch, so it cannot be pointed at the tree, his footage or a shared temp dir), with contain() added where the
law lacked it; two cleanup walks over read-only fixtures became the same own-scratch walk; three laws that counted what
their subject left in the SHARED temp dir (second_eye_*, minigrid.*) now point tempfile and TMPDIR at a watch dir inside
their own scratch, so they count only what this run made (and no longer race other runs); and
test_equipped_items_are_pixel_exact_per_character names its two fixture frames, so heart2 keys their bytes.
The 28: river_drains_every_pass, backup_lane_survives_a_loss, a_plan_is_computed_once, a_stub_agent_never_films_his_screen,
a_suite_run_is_reused_only_on_identical_bytes, a_pc_proves_itself_a_slice_at_a_time, an_evidence_picture_is_never_reaped,
the_backup_prune_never_orphans_a_loss, an_abandoned_seal_is_finished_not_waited_on, a_machine_establishes_its_own_tree,
atomic_write_keeps_the_mode, version_stamps_are_written_atomically, an_unread_journal_is_not_a_night_with_no_rows,
the_prune_never_frees_a_word, reel_index_durability, reel_retention, roundtrip_sim, the_cheap_end_route_row_asks_the_store_once,
vault_retro, g5_grok_eyes, the_eye_sees_the_blocks_around_a_big_files_hunks, a_sandbox_is_removed_whatever_its_bits,
a_fixture_pack_is_not_his_footage, equipped_items_are_pixel_exact_per_character, a_scratch_dir_is_not_made_by_reading_the_module,
a_refused_frame_leaves_no_snapshot_behind, the_live_frame_cannot_be_pulled_mid_read, vault_lane (each tv/test_*.py).
Each now reads KEYABLE under heart2.law_inputs (the census's own question), passes clean, and the laws that newly contain
their scratch or pin a frame were re-sabotaged (sab bad 0); the watch-dir census in the_live_frame_cannot_be_pulled was
seen to catch a planted snapshot leak (its own proof aims elsewhere). With REG-2938..2940, 280 of the 470 proofs can now
be saved; from clean-run timings here (nice 19, one law per process) that is about 43 minutes of re-proving per push no
longer paid - an estimate, not a push measurement. CEILING in test_the_unkeyable_laws_only_get_fewer: 91 -> 63.
THE 63 THAT REMAIN, BY WHY: 35 censuses whose denominator IS a folder of the tree (every tv/*.py, every law, every spec,
every workflow - including the three split out below); 12 that read his footage, history or data (frames/hist, .git,
his ledger backups, /proc); 12 that carry a browser marker and are not run on this Mac (venue rule) -
test_a_push_proof_runs_only_where_its_defect_shows (25 proofs) holds the same .github/workflows listing REG-2939 split
out, and is the largest left; 4 kept on purpose (frame_index's os.walk is the verbatim reference its lister is checked
against; a_test_run_leaves_no_scratch_dirs reads the shared temp base; the install-font law checks tv/ before and after;

### REG-2953 - /PLAYERS NOW USES SILOSPEN'S OWN FACTOR: IT STEPS AT /P3, /P5, /P7 AND MOVES COUNTESS AND DURIEL (#190, closes REG-2509)
REG-2509 was open since v3791. effChance divided every 1:N by a model with one NoDrop q per boss:
(1 - q^k)/(1 - q), k = 1 + floor(players / 2). His instruction on the task was to re-measure against silospen RotW 3.0
before changing anything. The pull was read-only from silospen's calculator, the source of every stored 1:N:
D2R_ROW_3_0, party 1, MF 300. It covered the 11 farms the page scales, on Normal, Nightmare and Hell, every unique at
/players 1-8 and every set item at /players 1, 3, 5, 7. That is 468 queries plus 4 at MF 0 and MF 1000, one at a time,
1.6 s apart, cached, with no refusals (494 requests in all, counting the page, the monster lists and the TZ checks).
Every farm's stored /players 1 figure matched the pull, except the Pit (REG-2954). Rainbow Facet is left out because
silospen lists it once per variant.
- THE STEPS. silospen pairs /players 1=2, 3=4, 5=6, 7=8 on every farm and difficulty but one: Hell Duriel gains
  1.4% at /p2. The model paired 2=3, 4=5, 6=7. So the page showed a gain at /p2 that the game does not give, and it
  stepped one /players late after that. The model's pairing came in with 0e22e7d2 (2026-06-01), "correct P#
  drop-quantity formula to canonical k=1+floor(N/2)". That commit replaced ceil(N/2), which pairs exactly as silospen
  does today, and its message says "Verified vs silospen dropcalc" and "the in-game bug Konyo caught" (/p5 == /p6).
  The live calculator refutes that verification on all 33 cells. If his in-game catch was something other than the
  page's own /p5 == /p6, that is his to say. The Prime Evils stop gaining at /p5 (/p5 = /p7).
- THE SIZE. One NoDrop cannot reach silospen's factors. Every treasure class under the top one has a NoDrop of its
  own. Normal Andariel moves x1.78 at /p8, where the model capped at x1.39. Nagelring at MF 300 now reads
  79, 79, 54, 54, 46, 46, 44, 44 across /p1-8, which is silospen's series; the model gave 79, 62, 62, 58, 58, 57, 57, 57.
  Countess and Duriel were held at x1.00 as "guaranteed droppers" and tagged P#-PROOF. silospen moves them x1.39 and
  x1.37 at /p8. Pindleskin is the one farm whose table does not move at any /players, so only he keeps the tag.
  Cows and the Pit are x2.29, not x2.41.
- THE SHAPE. Within one farm and difficulty, the per-item factor p(P)/p(1) varies only with how common the item is: a
  common item saturates over several picks. So PLAYER_F holds one factor per farm, difficulty and /players: the
  rare-item factor, 5 decimals, with index 0-7 for /players 1-8. Over the whole pull (60,679 item x /players cells),
  the page prints silospen's 1:N within one count or 0.023% of N, whichever is larger. A median factor would need
  0.07%. At MF 0 and MF 1000, /p7, every Normal Andariel unique is within one count.
FIX:
- `playerMult` reads PLAYER_F; PLAYER_Q is gone.
- The P# explainer states the measured pairing and its two exceptions, and names silospen. Its Hell table prints
  x@/p3 and x@/p8 for five rows; Pindleskin alone is P#-PROOF.
- The slider tip and the PLAYERS=8 MYTH card name Pindleskin alone as unmoved, ~1.4x for Countess and Duriel, and up
  to ~2.3x for Cows and the Pit.
- The hero P#-PROOF tag's title cites silospen rather than "q=0".
- The pull's raw probabilities for the items the law reads are in tv/data/silospen_players_rotw30.json (53 KB): per
  cell and quality, the most common and the rarest item, the lowest and the highest p(7)/p(1), and named items, plus
  the measured range of the whole table and the MF checks.
- Re-aimed in the same change:
  - test_a_good_mf_never_turns_odds_into_a_percent (reads PLAYER_F; Nagelring at MF 1000 /p8 is silospen's 1:35 from
    the vendored pull)
  - test_the_bible_text_agrees_with_its_own_cards (prose figure and the table read PLAYER_F; two red-proofs re-aimed)
  - test_a_tier_multiplier_names_its_difficulty (docstring)
  - specs v50, v160 and v1616_1 (Countess and Duriel move; Pindleskin is flat; silospen's pairing; 5 tier rows)
GUARD: tv/test_players_moves_odds_by_silospens_own_factor.py, 5 cases. It drives the page's own engine in node and
recomputes every expectation from the vendored raw probabilities. It checks:
- the page steps exactly where silospen steps;
- every vendored item prints silospen's odds within the measured reach;
- only an unmoved farm is called P#-proof;
- the explainer states the pairing;
- the stored /players 1 figures are this pull's (the Pit was declared as REG-2954 until REG-2954 closed it).
It has 6 red-proofs (the retired pairing, Countess at x1.00, Andariel at the model's size, Hell Duriel's /p2,
Countess and Duriel tagged P#-PROOF, the explainer's old pairing), all RED.

### REG-2796 - THE DAILY PICK FLICKERED: THE TASK FORCE REPAINTED EVERY POLL WHEN A ROW HAD AN APOSTROPHE (GrokBot, his screenshot, v3829/v3830)
His Sessions task-force hero row ("Sets 134/135 pieces - finish Cow King's Leathers", DAILY PICK) jumped and redrew on
every status poll (1.5 s idle, 0.8 s hot). hdTaskForce's identical-repaint skip (v1425, made DOM-aware by v2336) compared
`rowsEl.innerHTML === html`, and the browser hands back what it parsed, not the string it was given: esc() writes ' as
&#39; and Chrome serializes a bare ', and an art <img> whose onerror removes it changes the DOM after the paint. GrokBot
measured both round trips unequal in headless Chrome. So the skip never held for those rows, and the flicker came and
went as the pick rotated. The paint now leaves its own mark on the rows element (data-tf-sig, a hash of what it wrote)
and the skip reads that mark - still the DOM's word on whether this paint landed (a rebuilt element carries none), never
a re-serialization. Swept: no other `innerHTML ===` guard is left in control_ui.html. Law:
test_the_task_force_repaints_only_when_it_changed (3 cases, 2 red-proofs); test_control's v2336 law re-aimed to the mark.
### REG-2868 - THE HOME'S LAST SESSION NAMED THE RUN STILL BEING RECORDED (GrokBot #230 6477559571)
The Mac's 📼 LAST SESSION read "session 1 · Oct 28 · 8:14 PM · 19m00s → 22m57s · ◌ OPEN" across two loads while the console
said mode: live. _lastSessionRow (REG-2790/2811: the home digest, the Shelf's ▶ Last session and the Theatre button) skipped
session 1 only while the body was ON AIR, and a shadow-reader recording keeps the body off on purpose - "a shadow reel is not
a session he started". The rows carried no "ended", though the server knows. Every /api/sessions row now carries ended and
endedWhy (control_app._session_ended): true when the run wrote its session end, its reel is sealed (the agent folds its
stills into reel_<sid> at the seal) or a newer run began after it; false for session 1 with an id and none of those (the
live card's own test); null when session 1 has no id. A memoised row is asked again, since its n moves. _lastSessionRow
skips ended false whatever the body says; a null is NOT skipped - that would name an older run "last" for a reason nobody
could see - and the digest says "ended UNKNOWN" beside it; the body's ON AIR still skips session 1. Swept: no other surface
treats session 1 as live by the body (the theatre ribbon only labels a playback). Law: test_the_last_session_is_one_run
(+5 cases: three page cases through all three doors, two on the server; +5 red-proofs).

/api/roster-cache's meLine and the console's roster panel described only the rows' post, so GrokBot could not find a
refused frames post anywhere. The route now serves laneLines, one line per post from its own receipt
(roster_publish.lane_line), and the panel and the route's html draw them under the rows' line: HELD when the beacon is

test_the_roster_lane_says_its_profile_and_sessions_posts (7 cases on each lane's real apply_reply, the route's own lines
and the panel; 6 red-proofs).

### REG-2795 - A CONSOLE START WHILE THE BEACON WAS HELD SPENT ITS BOOT EXEMPTION WITHOUT POSTING (the v3829 second eye, both lanes)
_roster_frames_tick returned True whenever _frames_publish_once did not raise, and the suppressed path returned normally,
so a start under a held beacon cleared the boot flag with nothing posted; once the hold lifted the restart waited out the
3 h gap the boot exemption exists to bypass. Swept: the profile lane (_roster_profile_tick / _profile_publish_once) had
the same shape. A hold now answers False in both, so the exemption survives it; every other path is a decision and clears
it as before. Law: test_the_owner_publishes_its_session_digest (1 case over both lanes, 2 red-proofs, 8 of 8 RED).

### REG-2794 - A REAL SESSION DIGEST PAST 200 KB COULD NEVER REACH ITS OWN DOOR (the v3829 second eye)
roster.js's POST checked every body against the profile's 200 KB cap first, then branched to the frames door, whose own
cap is 900 KB and whose digest is built up to 600 KB of thumbnails: any real multi-session digest past 200 KB was refused
as "too large to be rows", the console banked the refusal and waited 3 h. The law drove framesPost with small digests, so
it passed. The first cap is now the largest any kind may send (FRAMES_MAX_BODY), and each kind keeps its own (rows, profile,
frames). Law: test_a_shadow_frames_record_is_signed_and_small (a 16-session digest past 200 KB stores; 1 red-proof).

### REG-3090 - ON A PHONE THE TRAY COLUMN SAT OVER THE RIGHT EDGE OF THE CONTENT (#224, his Q12 2026-10-29: bottom bar on phones)

### REG-3074 - NOTHING HELD THE RULE THAT A LOCK NEVER EARNS MORE REFUSALS THAN ATTEMPTS (#84, GrokBot #230 2026-10-12)
GrokBot read the Heart fan twice on v3679/v3680 as "printer.stream earned 138/135" (earned above its total). Measured:
v3680's own self_arming over v3680's own ledger scores printer.stream k=135 n=135 (657 rows, 0 row faults; its folded
rows are sabotage 126/126 and live 9/9, unchanged since 2026-09-22), and that build's caption printed L.k + '/' + L.n
as served. GrokBot's next three ticks that day and its 10-16 answer read 135/135. So the 138 was a misread of the
pixels, NOT A DEFECT in the count (the "earned" caption itself is gone since #180: the hover says "trial: k/n").
What makes k above n impossible is two checks - bank() refuses k > n, and _row_fault fails the whole read CLOSED on a
file row with k > n - and no law named either. Test-only: a law that holds both on an isolated ledger (a refused bank
writes nothing; a forged 138/135 row reads UNKNOWN and may() stays LOCKED) and holds the shape over the tracked
ledger (every lock and route: k <= n, attacksPassed <= attacks <= n). The fan-caption overlap half of #84 is NEEDS
LIVE. Law: test_a_lock_never_publishes_more_refusals_than_attempts (python), 2 red-proofs, RED.
### REG-3073 - AN UN-OWNED ITEM LEFT ITS COPY RECORDS BEHIND (#153.13, GrokBot's vault sweep)

Now every removal of a name through vaultRemove (the un-own, a card X, the last copy's X or trade-out) takes the name's
copy rows into its removal-journal batch (`batch.records`) and drops them from the store at once through the guarded
write; a records store that will not read writes nothing (UNKNOWN). vaultRestoreLast puts the carried rows back with the
names it restores, so the undo is whole: each copy's move, cell and entry. The trade door's note that "the removal door
leaves the copy's record in the store" was corrected to say the batch carries it. Observed and not changed: an auto-made
WAR1 for the overflow keeps its "Create mule WAR1" make line after the un-own. Law:
test_an_unowned_item_takes_its_copy_records_with_it (node, the whole page), 2 red-proofs, RED.

### REG-3067 - ONE SESSION THAT SAW A COPY IN TWO PLACES WAS SETTLED BY A GUESS (his done rule 2026-10-28 18:56, #202)
His done rule: "same-session conflict -> a question". A read at a copy's target and a read somewhere else from the SAME
session cannot both be where it is now, and REG-2843 let the newer read win - a guess inside one session: measured on the
whole page in node, a half-way task (seen once at its target by S1) was reopened by S1's own read elsewhere, and a read at
the target after S1's read away would have counted toward closing it. Now one session in two places keeps both sightings as
a question on the row - "Seen at its target and at <place> in the same session - which is it?" - and until he answers the
copy's place is UNKNOWN: neither in place (a verified row opens again, and "in place N of M" counts it apart, REG-3065) nor
moved. He answers with window.vaultConflictAnswer: "At its target" counts that session's read there and sets the other
aside on record; "At <place>" drops the read at the target, and the copy is seen away, so REG-3066 asks next. A read from
another session also settles it. His own tick is his answer already, so it raises no question. A shadow is read only.
Law: test_a_copy_seen_away_from_its_spot_is_asked (with REG-3066), 6 red-proofs.

### REG-3066 - A COPY SEEN AWAY FROM ITS SPOT WAS NEVER ASKED ABOUT, AND WHERE IT WAS SEEN WAS DROPPED (his model 2026-10-28 19:08, #202)
His model: the console locks each copy to its spot, and "a copy seen off its locked spot is a deviation (doubt -> task)
unless a move task explains it". A read somewhere other than a copy's FROM or TO set its task 'moved-elsewhere' and dropped
WHERE it was seen, so its row could not ask "did you move it there?" and nothing could take an answer. Now the task keeps
that sighting (elsewhere) and every sighting he sets aside (setAside). Its row says "moved?", and the opened row asks "Seen
at <place> on <date> - did you move it there?":
- Yes: his hand moves the spot there, through REG-2787's one door for a hand-placed cell (_vaultMoveRetargetCell, "new
  target: you moved it here"), and the task is his tick at that spot; Untick takes the tick back. A place that is not one of
  his lockers is refused, and nothing moves.
- No: the task stays open and that sighting is set aside on the task, recorded with his answer, never deleted.
A read back at its FROM or at its target clears the question. A shadow is read only: the door refuses there and writes
nothing. Law: test_a_copy_seen_away_from_its_spot_is_asked (node, the whole page), 6 red-proofs, RED. The question's
buttons are not checked on pixels here (CI or GrokBot).

### REG-3055 - A RUNEWORD WITH A TV STUB WAS A GUESSED 1x2, AND HIS COPIES' OWN BASES NEVER SIZED IT (GrokBot #230, 2026-10-29)
_itemCells read a TV stub's base (its own name) as a base, so a runeword with a stub never reached _runewordCells: Heart of

Lawbringer have no single size across their legal bases, so they stay an approx 1x2 - by design, since a runeword with no
recorded base has no single size. His copies' own records can settle it (REG-2844 the planner, REG-3002 a read; REG-3001
shows them): when every copy of the name is recorded in a base and those bases share one footprint, that base sizes it.
Measured on the whole page in node: Fury approx, then read in a Phase Blade 2x3, plus a Berserker Axe still 2x3, plus a
Colossus Blade approx again. The bases are read once per stored string (window._vaultCopyBaseCode), because the packer asks
_itemCells for every tile on every paint. Law: test_a_tv_stub_never_outranks_what_the_name_is (with REG-3054), 3 red-proofs.

### REG-3054 - A TV STUB'S 'basic' OUTRANKED WHAT THE NAME IS: RUNEWORDS AND RARES DREW WHITE (GrokBot #230, 2026-10-29)
TV DIABLO stamps {rarity: 'basic', base: <its own name>, cat: 'TV-vaulted'} on a name nothing knew when it registered it. His
boards hold such stubs for runewords and rares: the Mac's Heart of the Oak; the ALT's Call to Arms, Raven Whorl and Doom Eye,
stored without the val:'tv' mark today's writers stamp. Measured on the whole page in node with those stubs:
- every one read rarity 'basic' (white), because _artRarity read the stub before findRuneword and never asked the grammar;
- a runeword's picture asked "which base?" as if it were rolled;
- Doom Eye's unmarked stub was read as a curated entry: it routed to UNI-WEAPONS, and FIND sent him there.
The order of authority now: a catalogue runeword, his evidence's rarity and the rolled-name grammar outrank a stub's 'basic'
over its own name (REG-2903 already reads that base as no base). The stub's word stands only when nothing else knows the
name. A stub stored without val:'tv' is read as a TV stub (in memory; the store is untouched), so the router, the footprint
and the hover read it like every other. The chronicle-apply writer no longer stubs a runeword the prune's catalogue keeps
(d2rCatalogueKnows, the v739 writer's v2208 rule). A runeword that catalogue lacks (Heart of the Oak) keeps its stub, which
is what keeps the name across a reload, and reads as a runeword all the same. Now: the five runewords read 'rw', Raven Whorl
and Doom Eye 'rare' and 1x1, Doom Eye routes to MAGIC & RARE, and a stub of a name nothing knows stays 'basic'. Law:
test_a_tv_stub_never_outranks_what_the_name_is (node, the whole page), 5 red-proofs, RED.

### REG-3002 - A JUDGED GRIEF READ IN ANOTHER BASE WAS THE SAME COPY (his ruling 2026-10-29 02:30, Q3)
A judged read of a runeword only owned the name, so a Grief read in a Berserker Axe beside one in a Phase Blade was the same
copy. The read's base now names its copy (window._vaultRunewordReadJoin, from the AI checker's keep):
- the copy recorded in that base is that copy;
- a copy whose base was never recorded takes it, on its own record;
- a base no copy has is another copy, carrying that base, only for a runeword he keeps several of (a multi-copy keeper) and
  holds fewer of than he wants;
- on a runeword he keeps one of, or holds all he wants of, the read is said ("read in another base ... not counted") and
  nothing is counted - a misread base never mints a copy;
- a read with no base names no copy.
Law: test_a_runeword_keeper_keeps_a_base_per_copy (node, the whole page; with REG-3000 and REG-3001), 3 red-proofs.

### REG-3001 - NOTHING SAID WHICH BASE EACH COPY OF A RUNEWORD SITS IN (his ruling 2026-10-29 02:30, Q3)
