was never recorded says so, and records that would not read are UNKNOWN. Law: test_a_runeword_keeper_keeps_a_base_per_copy,
1 red-proof.

### REG-3000 - THE KEEPERS BOX REFUSED A RUNEWORD (his ruling 2026-10-29 02:30, Q3)
His ruling: a runeword may be a multi-copy keeper, and its copies may sit in different bases. The Keepers box asked only the
grail vocabulary, so "Grief" was refused ("isn't a chronicle item") while the hand door could raise a runeword's want. A
typed runeword name (exact, as findRuneword reads it) is the keeper now, and it beats a grail name that only begins that
way ("Spirit" is the runeword, not an item whose name starts with it). A name that is exactly both a runeword and a grail
item is asked, and nothing is added. Law: test_a_runeword_keeper_keeps_a_base_per_copy, 2 red-proofs.

### REG-2975 - HIS HAND TOOK OUT ONE KEEPER COPY AND THE NAME'S RECORD STILL READ THE COPY THAT LEFT (#202 P3b)
Copy 0 of a Magic & Rare keeper reads its mods off the name's record (d2r_magicFinds). Measured on the whole page in node:
two Small Charms of Vita (+17 and +20 to Life), the +17 one removed through vaultRemoveCopy (REG-2849) - the +20 copy stayed
and the name's record still said +17. Now the copy that leaves carries copy 0's mods on its own row, so the removal journal
holds it whole; the name's record takes the copy that is copy 0 now; and vaultRestoreLast puts the +17 copy back as copy 0
with the name's record reading it again. The profile carries both copies' mods. Law:
test_a_keeper_copy_leaves_alone_and_comes_back_whole (node, the whole page; with REG-2974), 3 red-proofs, RED.

### REG-2974 - ONE LOOK AT A KEEPER COPY DROPPED THE OTHER COPY'S RECORD (#202 P3b)
Once a look named a cell, the copy count was the cells (v3767). Measured on the whole page in node: two kept Small Charms of
Vita, one read at a stash cell -> the keeper counted 1 and the +20 copy's record was dropped on the next rebuild. A keeper's
count only rises where a read or a pick plainly differs from every copy here (REG-2972, REG-2973), so each is a real item,
and the cells never count it below that. Keepers have no MOVE task (Magic & Rare has its own locker, REG-2830), so a
sighting's cell does not choose a keeper's copy; the read doors choose it by its mods. Law:
test_a_keeper_copy_leaves_alone_and_comes_back_whole, 1 red-proof, RED.

### REG-2973 - A KEEPER PICKED AGAIN IN THE PLANNER WAS DROPPED, AND THE CARD DREW EVERY KEEPER ONCE (#202 P3b)
A Magic & Rare keeper is homed by the keeper rule, never in the mule map, so the planner's copy count never reached it.
Measured on the whole page in node: Small Charm of Vita +17, then +20 from the planner -> one copy reading +17. The join
question compared affix ids on the pick with read lines on each copy, so they always differed and the same +17 typed again
was "another copy" too - dropped the same way. Now:
- a pick's affix lines are its mods (_vpMods), on its record (_vrEntryOf) and in the question;
- mods that differ from every copy here file another copy, counted, carrying its own entry (REG-2844, magic too);
- the same lines are asked; "the same item" completes THAT copy (vaultHandJoin, magic too) and never writes over what a
  read gave it; a copy 0 read with no mods takes his lines on its record and on the name's record;
- "another copy", and "the same as copy 2" (_vpCompleteSame now takes the copy), never give their mods to copy 0.
The shelf card draws a keeper cell per copy, titled with that copy's mods. A cell held more than once takes out THAT copy
(vaultRemoveCopy); the last copy's ✕ throws the keeper out of Magic & Rare as before. The card says "1 item in 2 copies",
as the locker window counts. Two red-proofs whose lines changed are re-aimed (REG-2185, REG-2844). Laws:
test_a_magic_copy_is_asked_or_filed_by_its_mods (8 red-proofs) and test_a_magic_keeper_is_a_record_on_every_surface
(2 red-proofs), RED.

### REG-2972 - A SECOND READ OF A KEEPER WROTE OVER THE FIRST: TWO SMALL CHARMS OF VITA WERE ONE (#202 P3b)

- a re-read of the same photo never counts another copy (REG-2401).
Law: test_two_small_charms_of_vita_are_two_copies (node, the whole page), 6 red-proofs, RED.

### REG-2849 - HIS HAND COULD NOT REMOVE THE COPY HE MEANT: THE STEPPER TOOK THE LAST ONE (#154 P3c)
Each copy carries its own entry (REG-2844), but no door took out ONE named copy. The count stepper took the LAST copy off.
Measured on the whole page in node: with an Ist Shako (copy 1) and a Ber Shako (copy 2), removing the Ist one took the Ber
record, and the Ist entry stayed under the copy that was left.

The trade door (REG-2877) already removed THAT copy, and the copies after it closed up. That mechanism is reused here, so
there is no second one. window.vaultRemoveCopy(name, copyIx) goes through window._vaultTradeEvent as 'remove-copy':
- the copy's record (its move and its own entry) leaves in a removal-journal batch on his ✕'s lane (card-click), with no
  trade slot and no traded row the D2JSP card would count;
- the copies after it close up with their own entries, cells and moves, and the count drops one;
- the toolbar Undo is named for that copy, and vaultRestoreLast puts it back where it was;
- the last copy leaves through vaultRemove as his ✕, noted removed (REG-2845).

The opened MOVE row of each copy carries "✕ Remove this copy". Two REG-2877/2881 red-proofs whose lines now read the lane
and the undo words through variables are re-aimed, and the three trade laws prove RED. Law:
test_his_hand_removes_the_copy_it_names (node, the whole page), 5 red-proofs, RED.

The ✕ on a copy's TILE names its copy too. Each mule-window tile is keyed by its own copyIx (REG-2876: the name for copy 0,
"name #2" for copy 1), and a tile whose item is held more than once now carries a small ✕ in the corner the lock leaves free
(top-left). It calls vaultRemoveCopy(name, copyIx): measured on the whole page in node, two Nagelrings on UNI-SMALL - the
"Nagelring #2" tile's ✕ took out copy 2 alone ("the removal of copy 2 of Nagelring" on the Undo chip), and a ring held once
carries no copy ✕. The shelf card's record-cell ✕ is unchanged: it sends the item back to the dock, and copies share one
filing (#111), so it still says every copy goes. The shared stash pages draw unkeyed tiles and carry no copy ✕. Law:
test_his_hand_removes_the_copy_it_names, 1 more red-proof (6 of 6 RED).

### REG-2848 - A SIGHTING NEVER JOINED ITS COPY: A NEW CELL READ AS COPY 0 MOVING, AND HAND COPIES VANISHED (#154 P3c)
His plan is to add his items by hand now and let AUTO's sightings join those same records later. Measured on the whole page
in node:
- A filed item's later reads added no look to its witness row (the filing took its looks once; _ownedProvWrite answered
  'kept'). A Stone of Jordan added by hand, filed on a read at stash c0r0 and then read at c2r0 still counted 1 copy, and
  its MOVE row read copy 0 "moved-elsewhere".
- Two Griffon's Eyes added by hand, then one of them read at c5r0: once a cell was named the count was the cells (1), so
  the second copy's record and its MOVE row were dropped.
- A sighting at a new cell went to the first unseen hand copy, whichever it was.
Now a read of a filed item joins its looks (one per frame), so a second cell is the second copy (v3767, his Q1) and copy 0
stays where it was read. The looks cap (12) drops the oldest look of a place that has another look, never the only look of
a cell. The copies his hand typed (each keeps its MANUAL move row) are never counted below the cells, nor above copies[].
A sighting that carries mods joins the unseen hand copy whose own entry (REG-2844) it matches. Law:
test_a_sighting_joins_its_copy_by_cell_and_by_mods (node, the whole page), 4 red-proofs, RED.

### REG-2847 - ONE UNIQUE DREW DIFFERENT PICTURES ON DIFFERENT SURFACES (v3831 second eye, GrokBot #230 6478351967)
GrokBot measured on his board: Lightsabre drew mr_lightsabre.png on a list card where artUrl gives hd_lightsabre.png;

Measured here:

Now:

The second claim, that a Renewed Sunder hovers as its charm base while its row draws artUrl(name), is NOT A DEFECT. The

### REG-2846 - WIPE ITEMS RECORDED NO REMOVAL, SO EVERY READ BROUGHT EVERYTHING BACK (#154, his "wont these keep coming back?")
He plans to wipe the items and add them again one by one. Wipe items cleared owned, the mules, the witness rows and the scan
ledger, and wrote no removal record. Measured on the whole page in node: after a wipe, an old reel read, a newer read and
the console's sweep ledger each owned the item again, and the cleared scan ledger let the folder re-read every old file. The
wipe now notes every name it took out as removed at the wipe's time, in d2r_vaultRemovedAt (the per-name record his X writes
through _vaultRemovalNote; the 20-batch undo ring is left to single removals). An older read stays out (REG-2845), and a
newer dated read still comes back. The toolbar's Undo loads the snapshot taken before the wipe, so the items and the record
come back as they were. Law: test_a_removed_item_stays_out_of_every_door (node, the whole page; the door's wiring is pinned by
its source), 2 red-proofs for this REG, RED.

### REG-2845 - AN OLD OR UNDATED READ BROUGHT BACK AN ITEM HE HAD REMOVED (#154, his "wont these keep coming back?")

page in node after his X on Harlequin Crest: a read from 8 days earlier through tvVaultRegister owned it again, and so did
the console's sweep ledger (vaultAccumApply -> chronicleApply -> the register), whose witness carries no time. Now ONE rule,
window._vaultRemovedHold, is asked by window._ownedAdd (the one door every add passes), by the register before its

the inbox's auto-accept and the photo intake. His hand and his undo pass, because they are his word now. A read older than
his removal stays out, and so does a read whose time cannot be told: UNKNOWN is never "newer". A store that will not read
holds it, and a reel id s_<ms>_<n> dates its read. A newer dated read comes back, by design. The register's refusal reads
"kept out" in the vault ledger with its reason. Law: test_a_removed_item_stays_out_of_every_door (node, the whole page: X
and Wipe, then old, undated, old-sweep, photo-intake, newer, newer-sweep and hand reads, and the Undo), 5 red-proofs for

follows.

### REG-2844 - AN IST SHAKO AND A BER SHAKO WERE TWO COPIES NOTHING COULD TELL APART (#154 P3a, his front-run)
What makes one copy what it is was kept by NAME. d2r_plannerMade holds one runeword record per name (REG-2185 kept a second

copy's record (d2r_vaultRecords) now carries its own entry: base, quality, sockets, runes, eth, mods and rolls. The
planner's filing of that copy writes it, and his "the same item" fills what it lacks. It rides every rebuild and every move
written (the move writer no longer drops the record's entry or its loose place), and the profile carries it. Two census laws

runeword built before this reads its planner record. Magic and rare picks wait for their keeper record (P3b). Removing a copy
still drops the LAST copy's record (the count model cannot name which copy left). Law: test_each_copy_carries_its_own_entry
(node, the whole page: the planner, a rebuild, a move, a profile save and load), 7 red-proofs, RED.

### REG-2843 - A MOVE TASK CLOSED ON ONE SIGHTING AT ITS TARGET (#230 his done table, agent-guide's recon)
_vaultMoveWitness marked a task verified on ONE sighting at its target cell, and a full look of the target closed it at once
too. His rule, from the design he approved: a task ticks itself on reads at its target from 2 distinct sessions
(VAULT_WITNESS_MIN; s_1 and its re-look s_1#2 are one, the rule _vaultLookSessions keeps), each captured after the task
opened, with no newer read placing it elsewhere. A task now records when it opened and the sessions that have seen it at its
target. One session leaves it open and the row says "seen at target once (date)"; a second closes it. A read older than the
opening, or one whose time cannot be told, does not count; a reel id s_<start ms>_<n> dates its read. A newer read elsewhere
reopens it, and an older one changes nothing. His own tick still closes it at once, and a full look of the target is one
session, and an item first read already at its home closes on its second session there. A task saved before this rule
opens at its first read. Law: test_a_move_closes_on_two_sessions_at_its_target (node, the whole page), 9 red-proofs, RED.
Six laws that pinned one-sighting verification follow the rule: v3767, v3769 and the auto-sighting law (node), and three
Chrome laws (v3769_visual, rules_drive_every_move, throw_out_rows_drain; CI proves them).

### REG-2842 - A CLEARED PLANNER PICK LEFT THE KEEPER TARGET IT HAD RAISED (v3830 second eye)

before the clear (a removal, another tab's merge), the clear said nothing was taken back and left the target at 2. A later
re-read was then drawn as the copy the clear should have put back. The clear now restores the target it set whatever the live
count is (unless something else set it since), and says so. Law: test_a_cleared_pick_puts_back_its_keeper_target (node, the
whole page), 1 red-proof, RED.

### REG-2841 - THE PLANNER'S PICK OF AN ITEM ALREADY IN THE VAULT FILED ANOTHER COPY (#154 front-run, his 10-28 19:25 words)
The planner was the second hand door that counted a name he holds, typed again, as another copy. Its pick and the end of its
edit now ask the same question as + Add an item, on the plate ("Same item?"), with one button per copy and "Another copy".
At the pick nothing is typed yet, so the pick always asks. The question follows the name the edit makes (sockets rename a
base): a name he does not hold drops the question and files at Done; typed mods that plainly differ from the recorded mods

unanswered question files nothing and keeps the planner open, and a new pick over one says that nothing was filed for the
first. "The same item" joins that copy and fills what its record lacked (a magic item's mods, a runeword's base).
vaultPlannerFile asks only when its caller passes {ask: true}; every other caller is unchanged. Law:
test_a_hand_entry_of_an_item_already_here_asks (node, the whole page), 5 red-proofs for this REG, RED. Two laws follow the
new door: test_a_hand_copy_gets_its_move_and_its_sighting answers the second Stone's question "Another copy", and
test_a_hand_added_item_stays_his reads the pick's call with its ask.

### REG-2912 - A VAULT SIMULATION LEFT THE OCR WORKER ITS SWEEP WARMED RUNNING (#36, test_vault_lane's teardown)
test_vault_lane's teardown reported "A TEST LEFT A CHILD PROCESS RUNNING ... ocr_mac --worker". The lead read it as a
worker leaking between the laws of a sweep. Measured class by class on this Mac, the file leaks it on its own:
TestVaultDecisions alone gave 6 passed, 1 error, and the other four classes left nothing. Its cases call
vault_simulate.run. One run of the seen-once scenario over the synthetic reels took exec_hygiene.warm_workers() from
none to one (tv_diablo._OCR), because the sweep's own gate warms the OCR worker and nothing stopped it. Under plain
unittest (heart2, run_gates) the worker outlived the law with no message. vault_simulate.run now records the warm
workers before the sweep and, in a finally, stops any warm worker that was not there before (exec_hygiene, the one door
that knows them). A worker already warm when the run began belongs to someone else and is left alone. A stopped
OcrWorker respawns on its next read(), so a later reader loses nothing. No production path calls run(); its callers
are laws. test_vault_lane: 23 passed, no error. Law: test_a_simulation_leaves_no_worker_behind. Two cases use a
stand-in worker (a live child in `.p` plus `.stop()`) and run on every venue. Two warm the real ocr_mac and skip off
macOS, saying why. 2 red-proofs, both RED on the stand-in cases alone and on the full file.

### REG-2911 - THE GEAR LEDGER NAMED A SESSION BY LOGINS ONLY, A SECOND ANSWER BESIDE THE VAULT'S (#36, the lead on the report)
equipped_ledger bound worn gear to a character by character-select logins only, while the vault's looks read
char_select.session_characters (REG-2906/2908): two answers to "whose session was this", where his ruling is one logic.
Measured over a fixture journal: a reel with no login whose lobby named the character filed its worn items unattributed,
and a login span in which the lobby then named a second character filed its gear under the login's name - the doubt the
vault holds UNKNOWN. Now game_sessions asks named_at (char_select.session_span_at over session_characters' map, built with
no `carried`: the rollover chain stays the ledger's own) for every span: a span the map names takes that character, said
in `named`, and names its game session when that session had none, so the chain carries it; a span the map holds UNKNOWN
files nothing and its game session says why; a span the map does not name keeps the login and the chain as before. A reel
filed with no character is filed again once the map names it (the #234 refile). No second fold: the names come through
the learner's. Law: test_the_gear_ledger_reads_the_one_span_source, 4 red-proofs, RED.

### REG-2910 - THE DOCTOR'S ASK SENT HIM TO THE C PANEL, WHICH NO SCAN READS (#36, the lead on the REG-2909 report)
REG-2909's MISSING line said "open the C panel once". No pixel band finds the C panel - no C-panel frame was ever filmed
(char_select's own CPANEL_SAY) - so no scan ever shows a C panel to the reader, and following the ask could not name the
session: a promise the board would break. The ask is now decided in one place, char_select.session_ask, by what a scan
actually reads: "open character select, or the lobby, once" (both have measured bands and are read on every scan), with
the reason the C panel is not asked for; it names the C panel only once char_select.CPANEL_BAND - None today - holds a
measured band. Law: test_a_session_with_no_character_asks_for_the_c_panel (the ask, the band case, the live row), 3 new
red-proofs and 1 re-aimed, RED.

### REG-2909 - A SESSION NO SCREEN NAMED WAS SILENT: THE DOCTOR NOW ASKS "session N: character UNKNOWN - open the C panel once" (#36, his rule)
His rule: a doubt becomes a guided ask. A session none of character select, the lobby or the C panel named reads UNKNOWN
(REG-2906), and every look in it reads holder UNKNOWN on the vault (REG-2908), and nothing said so - the doctor had no row.
Now 'which character each session is on' reads the newest session on this PC (the character it is on NOW is its last
span's): OK names it, how it is known (char-select / lobby / c-panel / carried) and how many of the last 10 sessions are
named; MISSING asks in his words, "session <id>: character UNKNOWN - open the C panel once", and says what is true today -
no pixel band finds the C panel yet (no C-panel frame was ever filmed), so the panel is read only when a reader is shown
one, and picking the character at character select names the session too; UNKNOWN when the learner will not load, its
ledger will not read or the reel folder cannot be listed - never "0 sessions"; no reel at all is measured empty. One view
feeds the row and the console's answer (char_select.session_view, the rollover chain included), so the two cannot differ.
The row is in CHECKS, declared in WATCHES (no element of its own), and corroborate.NO_JOINT_YET says why it has no joint
(one vision reader names every screen; a real second source would be the session's .d2s). It counts as his: the ask is
his to act on. Law: test_a_session_with_no_character_asks_for_the_c_panel (the pure verdict, the live row over a fixture
ledger and reel tree, the registries), 6 red-proofs, RED. test_a_session_knows_its_character re-aimed at the one view.

Measured on the whole page in node: every look of a filed item read holder null - the stash sweep's sighting has no holder

sight, the move tasks' "from" and the WAR mule's "seen in the game" (REG-2803) all read UNKNOWN for every look, on every

upload's copy answers. Law: test_a_look_carries_its_sessions_character (the whole page, the JS twin checked against the

### REG-2907 - THE CONSOLE NOW SERVES WHICH CHARACTER EACH SESSION IS ON, AND THE SHADOW UPLOAD KEEPS IT (#36)
/api/chars_learned carries `sessions` (sessionId -> its spans: from, character, via, why), built from the learner's

sessions), RED.

### REG-2906 - NO SESSION KNEW WHICH CHARACTER IT WAS ON: THE TWO SCREENS THAT NAME HIM WERE NEVER JOINED TO A REEL (#36, his ruling 2026-10-28 11:30)
His ruling: read the character from the screens he already passes through - the character-select screen at login and the
in-game C panel - into one logic that binds a session's reads, stash cells and witnesses to that character, so each reel
knows whose stash it filmed. Measured on the code: the halves existed apart. char_select.logins() named the row
highlighted at character select, keyed by reel, and only the gear ledger read it (#103 step B); the lobby / C-panel
reader banked a witness naming the character (#149) with the frame's file name and never the reel, so no session could
be told from it; and the vault's sightings carry no holder at all (vault_retro's sight has none, and the board's own note
says every carried receipt in production has character null). Now a witness records the reel it was read in, and
char_select.session_characters joins logins and witnesses per session (the journal's sessionId) through the learner's
own fold (Konylock is KonyoLock): a login is a boundary - he can change character only there - a lobby or C-panel read
names the span it falls in, two screens naming two characters in one span are UNKNOWN with both names (never the newer
guessed over the older), a login whose closing read named no row is a boundary with an UNKNOWN character, the span before
a reel's first login takes the rollover chain's character only when nothing in it names anyone (said as carried), and a
session no read names is absent - UNKNOWN to every caller. A witness banked before this is placed by its frame on this
PC's reels (the newest reel that started before it, and the file must be there); one no reel holds is counted unplaced,
never guessed into a neighbour. session_character_at gives a read the span it falls in. Not built: no pixel band detects
the C panel yet (no C-panel frame was ever filmed - char_select's own note), so a C-panel read happens only when the lobby
reader is shown one; measuring that band needs a filmed panel. Law: test_a_session_knows_its_character, 7 red-proofs, RED.

### REG-2903 - AN ITEM WHOSE BASE THE NAME DOES NOT GIVE WAS A RING ON ONE SURFACE AND A SILENT MARK ON ANOTHER (the house rule on his MAGIC & RARE, 2026-10-28)
The rule: an item whose base cannot be established from its own name or record shows UNKNOWN everywhere - one logic,

decides it (_artRolledBase, asked by artOr and by the hover): a base from the keeper record, the catalogue row or the

reads - there is no base, the mark carries the question as its tooltip ("ring or jewel? the name does not say; a tooltip

### REG-2959 - REOPENING A SESSION COULD PAINT ANOTHER FRAME'S PICTURE UNDER A FRAME'S LABEL (#51, GrokBot #230 tick 403)

GrokBot: reopening Session 175 in the Theatre painted a different picture under the same label "8/67 · 7:54:44 PM.859". thPaint writes a frame's label at once and the film follows when that frame's picture loads (thShowFrame and its probe image). Measured on the shipped thShowFrame, cut from control_ui.html and run in node over stub images: with frame A on the film, asking frame B and stepping back to A before B loaded returned early without re-aiming the film, so B's probe landed afterwards and painted B's picture under A's label (src f_2000 under the label of f_1000). And while a frame not yet loaded was fetched (a first open asks the server to make each frame's 1280 copy), the film kept the previous picture under the new label, unmarked. The step back now re-aims the film, so a late probe paints nothing, and a frame still loading after 160 ms dims the old picture (th-pending) until its own lands; a load inside the beat, a frame already decoded in the prefetch pool and a failed load dim nothing, so playback does not flicker. The specific Session 175 frames were not replayed (his footage stays his); this is the mechanism that paints one frame's picture under another's label. Law test_a_theatre_frame_paints_its_own_picture (3 cases), 4 red-proofs RED.

GrokBot's read-only audit: `d2r_multiKeep` was `{name: wantCount}`, so a multi-copy keeper could hold a count and never a destination, and nothing that places an item read it. ### REG-2861 - THE GONE-DRAIN WOULD HAVE CLOSED ROWS ON THE ABSENCE OF A READ (finding of REG-2860; REG-2300's open end)
`_vaultGoneObserve` (REG-2300) closes a throw-out or move row after VAULT_GONE_SESSIONS sessions whose frames showed its
first-witnessed container without the item. REG-2300 left it uncalled: "the frame reader must hand it {session, holder,
location, items, ground} per frame". Measured before wiring it: no reader produces such a frame. Every read that reaches
the board is one item (_liveReadRoute -> tvVaultRegister -> _vaultMoveApplySight), and a stash read is a hover tooltip
(#197: the read cell is the hover point), so a frame of a stash tab names the hovered item, not the tab's contents.
Joined at that seam, every hover of a neighbour would have counted a session in which each other row in the tab was
"gone", and five sessions of hovering would have closed them "gone 5/5" - against his ruling that a not-seen item is
asked about and never dropped on its own when in doubt. So the door now counts absence only from a frame that says
`complete: true` (a sweep that read the container whole); any other frame still resets and reopens on what it saw, and
the answer says why its absence counted nothing - his approved design (#230 c6473846977, Q2/Q3: absence only from a
FULL LOOK, "a frame that shows a whole container"). NOT JOINED, on purpose: no caller is added, because nothing yet
produces a whole read. The producers it waits for are the guided sweep (P4) and P2's full-look detection; what the count
then does (his later ruling: proven-gone items go to a log with undo, unexplained vanishes ask) is P5's, and the door's
output stays a count. The positive rules (seen at target, seen in its cell) already run through _vaultMoveWitness. The fixtures of REG-2300 / REG-2689 / the tasks panel now say their frames are whole reads.
Law: test_a_hover_read_never_counts_an_item_gone (whole page in node; 4 red-proofs RED); the reopen law re-proved (2 RED).

### REG-2883 - MARK TRADED ON ONE COPY OF THREE CALLED THE WHOLE NAME TRADED (#83, the lead's follow-up to REG-2881: one source, the vault)
Measured in the D2JSP room's own code and on the whole page (node): Mark traded wrote the per-name mark d2r_d2jsp_sold AND

dead. The list posted a SOLD block while the vault still held 2 copies, 2 of them listed. The vault kept no lasting note
of a traded copy: the removal journal is a ring of 20 batches. Now:

  both paths, every rebuild carries it, and vaultRestoreLast takes it back out. It is read through

and window._LP_FORKED), and the newest 12 rows are kept per item. The card shows "Not posted yet", "No post confirmed yet",

key. Law `tv/test_a_d2jsp_card_keeps_its_post_log.py` (node, 8 red-proofs RED).

### REG-2877 - A COPY HAD NO PLACE TO SAY IT IS LISTED, AND ONE TRADED COPY COULD NOT LEAVE THE COUNT WITH AN UNDO (#83, his rulings)
His rulings: "Design it now, wire it later", and a traded-out copy is proven gone, so it goes to the Vault log with an undo,
never a question. Measured on the whole page in node: a copy record (d2r_vaultRecords) had no place to say it is listed or
traded. Nothing could take ONE copy out of the count through the removal journal. The removal door takes a whole name, and
the copy door (vaultCopyAdjust) drops the LAST copy's record and journals nothing. So trading copy 2 of 3 would have left
copy 2's MOVE task standing and deleted copy 3's, with no undo. Now a record carries trade: null | {state: 'listed' |
'traded-out', at, post?}. It is written only when set, and a records rebuild and a task commit both keep it.
window._vaultTradeEvent takes four events. listed and unlisted set and clear the slot; a listed copy still counts. trade-out
of one of several copies takes THAT copy's record out: its move and its slot ride in a removal-journal batch (lane
trade-out, copyOut), the copies after it close up, and the count drops one, so no task is left asking where it is. The
last copy leaves through vaultRemove on the trade-out lane, which leaves its record in the store (measured). vaultRestoreLast
puts either one back with its own cell. trade-in is one more copy through the owned door, with its own MOVE task. No
surface calls the door yet; the D2JSP tab wires it later. Law `tv/test_a_traded_copy_leaves_through_the_vault_log.py`
(whole page in node, 7 red-proofs RED; an eighth, on carrying the last copy's row in its batch, could not go red because the
store already keeps that row, so the code and the proof were dropped).

### REG-2870 - A D2JSP POST ANSWER NAMED NO REASON, AND A CLICK WAS READ AS NOTHING SENT WHEN CHROME WOULD NOT CLOSE (#83, his ask 1, GrokBot 6476487696)
GrokBot's real post from the Linux seat, with his OK, came back "MAYBE SENT: The console answered with no reason, which this
page does not know", and no topic reached board 268. His ask: "surface what the backend got back (HTTP status or d2jsp
error) instead of MAYBE SENT with no reason." The code could not say why. Every refusal was a bare word: chrome-unread never
named the step of the cookie read that failed, and not-posted and maybe-sent never said what the run saw or on which page it
stopped. An error inside the send escaped the route as an exception, which dropped the connection. The page's words for an
answer with no contract reason named no HTTP status and none of the answer's own words. Measured on a fake board (fakes
only, never d2jsp): a Chrome that raised while closing, after the run had clicked submit, turned the result into "unread":
"nothing was posted" about a click that went out. Now the run's result outlives its Chrome's cleanup (the error rides on it
as teardown). Each cookie reader says which step failed (no cookie file, the keychain, the decryption, signed out), and the
lamp's unread says it too. Every answer that is not a receipt carries `why`: what the run saw and its last forum page. An
error inside the send is maybe-sent with why, and the console route answers not-posted with why when the d2jsp module
itself fails. The receipt and the status line show "What the console saw: ...". An answer with no contract reason shows its
HTTP status and its own words. NOT KNOWN: what exactly the Linux seat's console answered. No reason-less answer is left in
this tree's code, so that seat ran other code or another path; GrokBot's repost will show the words. Law
`tv/test_a_d2jsp_refusal_always_says_why.py` (the real flow over the send law's fake board, plus the room in node; 15
red-proofs RED). Three REG-2490 red-proofs and one REG-2492 red-proof were re-aimed to the moved lines.

### REG-2817 - THE ROSTER UPLOAD'S VAULT SECTION WAS THE CONSOLE'S EVIDENCE FILE, DATED BY ITS MTIME (intake design P1, his ruling Q1-Q4)
The upload's vault section was built from vault_accum.json - the sweep's evidence ledger, whose own header says "evidence,

### REG-2816 - THE COPY READOUT COULD NOT SAY WHERE A LOCKER ROW'S COPIES CAME FROM OR WHEN IT WAS LAST SEEN (intake design P1)
His ruling (Q1-Q4 all yes, #230 6473846977) starts the intake design with the instrument: before any behaviour changes,
the copy readout counts copies by source and dates the last-seen, so every later phase can be checked against it.
MEASURED on his board's store 2026-10-28 (a read-only copy, deleted after): 22 provenance rows - 16 receipts (source
aic-judge 11, kai-register 5; 9 carry a measured read time, and all 12 of their looks an `at`) and 6 filing rows
(kept/evidence 4, hand/hand 1, stash/kai-register 1; their 20 looks carry no time); 13 persisted records, each carrying its
name's one source. The store keeps ONE source per name, and capture times only where a read recorded one. So per locker
row the readout now carries `sources` (its records under the class its provenance row records: hand / auto / sweep / photo
/ chronicle - one table beside _ownedProvSourceSay, a filing row's lane read past to its `by` - else unknown, never a
guess), `sourceRaw` (the recorded source/by), and `seenFirst` / `seenLast` (the oldest and newest capture time it records -
a measured receipt time or a look's `at`; a filing's own time and an unmeasured ts are not captures - null when none);
overall `bySource`, `lastSeenOldest` / `lastSeenNewest` and `lastSeenNone`. The console banks them shaped (the six class
names only, a count or nothing). Law: test_the_copy_readout_says_where_copies_came_from (6 cases: the board's half on the
whole page in node, the console's on control_app; 6 red-proofs, each RED). test_a_copy_readout_says_what_each_side_counts'
two red-proofs re-aimed at the moved lines, 11 of 11 RED.

### REG-2815 - A CAPPED OR ERRORING READER WAS COUNTED AS A READ AT SIX DOORS AND IN THE ENGINE'S JUDGE LOOP (#158.8)
The task: "a cap hit returns HTTP 200 + an error body, so callers can't tell it from a read." MEASURED at v3832:
control_app's /api/intake already answers a cap with 429 (REG-2383/2388), so that half is closed. The callers were not.
The Chronicle and grail screenshot readers parsed the cap's body and read its empty lists as a page or a shot read with
nothing on it. The Ask box showed the error as the bible's answer. The set tracker, the craft reader and the item
checker's upload read a 200 + {error} (the website path, v407) the same way. The item checker's judge answered a cap as
"server 429" beside "no magic/rare item readable"; the engine's judge loop posted that to /kai_verdict as a "kai-judge"
receipt ("judge a tooltip - UNREADABLE"), and _judge_already_near then read the hover as judged, so the cap stood in for
a read and the hover was never judged. One rule now, window._intakeRefused(status, body), beside the one intake door,
asked by every door. aicJudge answers a refusal {ok:false, refused:true, why}, and /kai_verdict journals it under its own
mode (_kai_refused_row: "kai-judge-refused", no judge slot), which no judge reader takes for a judge. Swept: all 11
callers of the intake endpoint - 7 fixed (the set tracker, askBible, _craftRead, aicUpload, aicJudge, chronicleShotIntake,
grailIntake); _tallyRead, vaultIntake and vaultGridCount already told a refusal apart; dailyCreateAi writes only an answer.
Law: test_a_refused_read_is_never_a_read (5 cases: the rule and aicJudge in node, the journal row and _judge_already_near
on control_app, each door at its one-line site; 8 red-proofs, each RED).

Every change in the vault planner's EDIT tab reached ctx.write and was filed. Measured on the whole page in node, GrokBot's

### REG-2800 - THE V1816 LAW RELOADED WHILE THE PAGE'S DEFERRED VAULT WORK RAN, AND BLAMED THE REPAIR FOR A STORE THE RELOAD HAD NOT CARRIED (#160, CI shard 8 on ci/claude-v3826e)
tests/v1814_vault_routes_by_base_data.spec.ts:212 failed on shard 8, first try and retry ("the migration ran a second
time and overruled a placement he made by hand"); the same bytes passed on three other runs. MEASURED in the retry's trace:
the second load logged "[vault] re-routed 1 mis-filed item(s): Homunculus uni-weap->uni-armor" - the repair really ran
again - but on a store holding none of the first load's writes: the first load's last snapshot drew 3 owned items (its
seed cleanse removed 6), the second load's first snapshot drew all 9, and every one-time stamped step of the first load
(provenance backfill, seed cleanse "removed 6", set-piece reconcile, records migrate "persisted 3") ran again. The spec's
init script re-seeds the pre-repair vault whenever its marker is missing, so the lost store became a new pre-repair vault
and the repair rightly ran on it. The reload had been sent while the page's deferred vault chain (~1.5 s after load:
cleanse -> reconcile -> records arm) was running; the spec's 1500 ms sleep sat on that chain's start. MEASURED in node,
both orders forced, the store carried across: the page never re-runs the repair on a stamped store and his hand wins; but
a map written straight into storage behind the page's memory (the spec's old "hand") is carried away by the chain's
whole-map write (vaultRemove -> saveA) when the chain lands after it. FIX: the page raises window._vaultLoadSettled after
the chain's last step; the spec waits on it before acting and before reloading (never a sleep), files his hand through
his own door (vaultAssign - with the one-shot check removed that door is still overruled, so it does not blind the law),
reads his hand back before the reload, asserts as a PREMISE that the second load was handed the first load's stamp (so a
lost store names itself instead of accusing the migration), and asserts no re-route on the second load. Swept: v1817 in
the same file slept 1200 ms and then reloaded the same way - it waits on the signal now. Not swept: 92 spec files sleep
and then read d2r_muleAssign / d2r_owned; none has a measured race, and the signal is there for them. Law:
tv/test_the_vault_repair_runs_once_whatever_the_load_order.py (node, two whole-page loads, store carried, both orders):
5 red-proofs, 5 RED. The spec change is Chrome-only: CI proves it.

Spellsteel and Ethereal Edge...), which the game draws alike, and the only group mixing kinds of item is this runeword in

### REG-2805 - A UNIQUE DREW ITS BASE'S PLAIN SPRITE, AND ITS ROW AND HOVER COULD DRAW TWO DIFFERENT ITEMS (#111, his ruling 2026-10-28 (b), reviewers C2/E/D)
His ruling: each unique shows its own picture, the same on every surface. v406 put every unique and set piece onto its
base's sprite from the game files, on the note that D2R has no picture of its own for a unique. Measured on the repo's own
art (the whole page in node): of the 398 uniques tv/unique_roster.json names, 288 drew their base's plain sprite
(Nightwing's Veil a Great Helm, Harlequin Crest a Cap) and 280 of those had their own icon registered (art/mr_*.png, the
base sprite in that unique's own in-game colour); the game files carry a sprite of its own for 69 (v384's extraction:
Lightsabre, The Minotaur), and those are the most exact picture there is. Now ONE resolver, window._keeperArt, answers for
every name in the v406 table - its own game sprite, then its own icon, then its base sprite as the stated fallback - and
D2IO_ART holds its answer, while artUrl asks it before its label rules. So the vault cells and rows (artOr), the hover, the
locker and mule cards, the console's copy of D2IO_ART and the bridge's art fields draw one picture. Three things the old
order hid were fixed with it: "Ethereal Edge" drew the runeword Edge's bow (the prefix rule), the v408 runeword table drew
a poleaxe over "Crescent Moon", and Bul-Kathos' Wedding Band's icon was registered without the apostrophe. Swept: every
roster unique's row against its hover - the six Latent Sunder charms drew their own icon in the row and the plain charm's
carving in the hover; the hover now draws an own icon (the Renewed names, on a generic charm logo, keep the carving). Result:
of the 356 uniques the resolver knows, 66 draw their own game sprite, 282 their own icon, and 8 fall back to the base
because the repo holds no picture of their own (Darkforce Spawn, Goldstrike Arch, Peasant Crown, Pompeii's Wrath,
Que-Hegan's Wisdom, The Atlantean, The Redeemer, Thundergod's Vigor). Outside the v406 table, 4 uniques draw a base

an earlier decision). Found and left: "Crescent Moon (sword)" is registered with the amulet's bytes. Law:
test_a_unique_wears_its_own_picture_everywhere (node, the whole page; every surface and the whole roster). 9 red-proofs,
all RED. tests/v406_hd_uniques_sets.spec.ts rewritten to the ruling (Chrome, CI proves it).

### REG-2810 - IN A SHADOW, THE SHELF SHOWED NOTHING OF THE OWNER'S SESSIONS (#218 phase 3b, his ruling 2026-10-28)
His ruling: a shadow renders the owner's exact data one to one, with summarized frames - a few small key frames per

whose sessions, the record's age (shadow_sessions.view now carries `ago`, the profile view's one age rule), "this PC's

frames, each an <img> built as data:image/jpeg;base64 over a body that is base64 and nothing else - or the record's own
why when it has none. ok:false prints its why as UNKNOWN, never an empty list; its one request is a GET; Leave closes it.

(13 cases: the list's helpers and its opener run in node over a mock DOM and a recording fetch, the age joined from the

### REG-2786 - THE MULE CARD HEADER STOPPED COUNTING AT 3 COPIES: A KEEPER TARGET WAS DRAWN AS COPIES HELD (#111, reviewers C2/E/D)
Located: every copy count on the vault (the locker card's cells and its "N items in M copies" line, the mule card's
"N items total · M copies" header, the records model, the mule packer) asks _vaultPresenceSpan, and once any look named a
cell (v3767) it answered the distinct cells, or the keeper TARGET when that was larger, never copies[]. The page's default
targets are 3 for The Stone of Jordan, Mara's Kaleidoscope and Shako. Measured on the whole page in node: Mara's seen in
one cell drew 3 cells and "3 copies" held x1; held x3 and typed twice more by hand it still read 3 while the door answered
"x5 - another copy, its own row and cell"; Griswold's Edge seen in 3 cells and typed twice more read 3 on the card, the
mule card and the records, and its two typed copies got MANUAL move rows naming the mule and no cell; a planner pick of a
filed Obedience seen in one cell said "copy 2 filed" and the count stayed 1. Now a target counts only as far as copies[]
holds (his v3767 rule: a multi-keep re-read under its target is a real copy; the target alone is none), and a copy his
hand types past what the cells count raises the target at the hand door - the rule L1 already kept for a set piece - in
vaultHandAdd and in the planner's copy, whose undo puts the target back. Swept: _vaultMoveCopies (the move planner) kept
its own cell count and now asks the same span, so each typed copy gets its own cell beside its siblings (measured, and a
multi-keep copy under its target had no planned cell either). The v3767 guard stands: one cell re-read into copies[] 4 is
one copy, and a name with no cell gains no target from a typed copy. Left as it was: a store whose copies[] already sits
above the target with no hand record (typed before this fix) still reads the target - raising the target on the keeper
row draws them. Law: test_a_copy_past_the_cells_is_counted (node, the whole page, five stores). 7 red-proofs, all RED;
test_v3767_copy_witness red-proof 11 re-aimed at the new line (same sabotage, RED).

### REG-2785 - AUTO-SORT FILED A FOUND-EVER TICK WITH NO PICTURE WHEN ITS NAME HAD A PLANNER RECORD (#111, reviewers C2/E/D)
_plannerHandRow tells his Auto-Sort click "his hand put this here", and the click then files a dock name to its mule (and,
in the shared-stash arm, past REG-2223's chronicle gate) without the stash picture every other dock name needs. It read the
row's words (the Vault planner, + Add an item) and also answered true for any name with a d2r_plannerMade record. That
record is kept per name for the base he built (the cell's picture, footprint and hover read it) and nothing takes it out
when the item leaves: vaultRemove drops the witness row and keeps the record. Measured on the whole page in node: Obedience
picked in the planner, removed, then read off a Chronicle page in two sessions (a found-ever tick, loose in the dock) - his
click filed it to RUNEWORDS and rewrote the row as an Auto-Sort hand filing; Grief, the same road, went to the shared stash.
The 10-28 triage called it by design because the record means "he built it", which is true of the copy he removed, not of
the row in the dock. Now the hand gate reads the row alone; the planner's words reach the row on every pick (the hand
receipt, the filing's where, and the receipt a cell X demotes the filing back to). Swept: the other readers of the record
(_itemCells, artOr, the built-base hover) draw a base and never decide ownership. One case changes (measured the same way): a planner pick of a
name already owned through a found-ever tick, later sent back by its cell X, demotes to that tick and now waits for a
picture or a drag instead of re-filing on the click. Law: test_a_planner_record_is_not_his_hand (node, the whole page; the
shipped gate cut and run with a record for every name). 2 red-proofs, both RED.
### REG-2791 - THE CAUGHT-TEXT CHIP PRINTED OCR GARBLE BARE, SO IT READ AS LEAKED MARKUP (#86, GrokBot's `CHAKm •<li•`)
GrokBot, Shelf > Theatre Sess 48: "missed → KAI caught (retro): CHAKm •<li•" - "an HTML fragment is leaking into the
chip". MEASURED: it is not markup, and it was already escaped. kaiMissTexts and a kai beat's kai.texts are the KAI
closer's missed[].texts - OCR off a film still no eye read. Read-only on his tree 2026-10-28: 1,029 such texts on 38
sealed reels (10 with a '<' or '>'), 8,637 on the journal's kai rows (45 with one, 4 distinct: 'FAsT ArrA<K SpfE',
'kf>uiRfD STRENGT', '*NVS T• A TTA<X RATIN', '>-Diablos') - each a letter the OCR misread, none a tag. Stripping the
marks would alter a read, so nothing is stripped, at display or in the ledger: one helper (_ocrRawSay) prints each text
escaped and quoted, verbatim, and the footage chip, the kai chip and the kai caption say it is raw OCR ("KAI caught unread
text · raw OCR: “CHAKm •<li•”"). Swept: those three are every surface printing these texts; the dossier's stamp already
says "unread:". Law: test_unread_text_is_shown_as_the_ocr_read_it (3 cases in node, each quoted text unescaped and
compared to the read character for character; 6 red-proofs, each RED). The REG-2154 law's harness carries the helper.

### REG-2790 - "LAST SESSION" NAMED ONE RUN ON THE HOME PAGE AND OPENED ANOTHER ON THE SHELF (#86, GrokBot's 28 vs 48)

### REG-2766 - THE LIVE SHELF CARD COUNTED ITS LOOSE FILM AND NEVER DATED IT (the v3824 second eye, REG-2748's sweep)
REG-2748 made a sealed reel's card span its footage stills. Before a reel seals there is no reel_<sid> folder: the LIVE
card counts the loose f_<ms>.jpg stills at the reel root (v908) and never added their capture times, so one short read
beside an hour of loose film could still read "0m00s" until the seal. The live branch now spans its first and last

test_a_session_is_dated_by_what_it_captured (1 new case: no reel folder, two loose stills; 1 red-proof).
### REG-2770 - A SECOND-EYE ROW OF FILLER WORDS COUNTED AS A LOOK WITH 3 FINDINGS (v3825's first look)

### REG-2769 - A PROFILE LOAD COULD PRINT "runeStash: 6 -> 6" FOR RUNES THAT MOVED (the second eye on v3825..v3828)

### REG-2773 - NO CONSOLE COULD READ AN OWNER'S PUBLISHED SESSIONS (#218 phase 3a, his ruling 2026-10-28)
REG-2772 publishes the digest; a shadow's Shelf and TV·D need to read it. GET /api/roster-cache?frames=<owner>
(control_app._frames_view) fetches that owner's frames record and hands back the sessions with the record's own time,
by the profile view's rule: this PC's last copy (tv/roster_frames_cache, gitignored) stands in only when the site could
not be READ, and says it is a copy and how old; "nothing uploaded" and "corrupt" are answers no old copy is drawn over;
a suppressed beacon reads the copy and says why. The shadow's Shelf / TV·D drawing it is phase 3b. Law:
test_a_shadow_reads_the_owners_sessions (5 cases, the site stubbed, 4 red-proofs).

### REG-2772 - NOTHING POSTED THE OWNER'S SESSION DIGEST (#218 phase 2b, his ruling 2026-10-28)
REG-2765 built the digest and REG-2771 gave it a signed record; this joins them. The roster publish lane (rows, then the
profile, every 60 s) posts the digest to the frames door after the profile: on the console's start, then only when it
changed, at most every 3 h, never rebuilding thumbnails every minute (it looks again after 30 min), never while the
beacon is suppressed; a refusal waits 3 h; the reply lands in its own per-machine state (gitignored). Its law caught my
own first cut: the digest carried its build time, so its hash moved on every build and change-only could never hold -
the build time is out of the digest now (the site record keeps its own time). Law:
test_the_owner_publishes_its_session_digest (7 cases, the console's real publisher on a fixture journal with the post
captured, 6 red-proofs).

### REG-2771 - THE OWNER'S SESSION DIGEST HAD NO DOOR TO THE SITE (#218 phase 2, his ruling 2026-10-28)
REG-2765 builds the digest a shadow can carry; nothing could store it. The roster route's profile door refuses every
picture (his 10-07 ruling: pictures stay on that PC), so the digest gets its OWN signed record, roster:<owner>:frames -
the one place a picture rides, and only the theatre's 160 px JPEG thumbnails: the worker checks every frame (a read
frame's id, a JPEG, under 20 KB), at most 3 per session and 16 sessions, no path or token anywhere, and the hash the
owner signed; change-only, at most every 3 h unless the console just started, 8 a day; GET ?frames=<owner> reads it
back, served only while the key that signed it is the owner's registered key. It answers to the SAME gate as the
profile: the signing check, the replay rule and the served-key rule moved VERBATIM into three shared helpers
(signedOwnerIntent, signedAtRefusal, signedByRegisteredNow), so the second kind added callers, never a second copy of a
safety routine - proved by the 161 red-proofs of the three roster laws, all still RED after the move. The console's
publisher is phase 2b; the shadow's view is phase 3. Law: test_a_shadow_frames_record_is_signed_and_small (6 cases on
the worker in node, real signing keys, 7 red-proofs).

### REG-2765 - A SHADOW HAD NOTHING OF THE OWNER'S SESSIONS TO SHOW (#218 phase 1, his ruling 2026-10-28)
In a shadow, THE SHELF answered with a refusal toast and TV·D showed the viewer's own pane: the owner's sessions never
travel (the upload keeps tvdHist and the session log home on purpose - they are large), and a full reel is 8-12 GB. His
ruling: the shadow renders the owner's data one to one, with summarized frames - "a few small key frames per session".
tv/shadow_sessions.digest builds that on the owner's PC: the newest 16 sessions, newest first, dated by what they
captured (REG-2736), read counts by the Shelf's own rule (control_app._is_a_live_read, passed in), the names read, and up
to 3 key frames each as the theatre's own 160 px thumbnails (cache160; named frames first) - made by the theatre's sips
resizer on a Mac when missing, and on a PC with no resizer the session rides without pictures and says why, never a full
frame. A thumbnail over 20 KB is left out and named; the record stays under 600 KB by dropping the OLDEST sessions'
pictures first. Phase 2 signs and publishes it as the owner's own roster record; phase 3 draws it in the shadow's Shelf
and TV·D. Law: test_a_shadow_carries_the_owners_sessions_summarized (5 cases on fixtures, 5 red-proofs).

### REG-2764 - NO HAND-TEST SCENARIO KNEW WHICH OF HIS FRAMES TEST IT (#22, his rulings 2026-10-28)
His words: "if you can take my sessions and frames and reels and do the tests your self scenario by scenario then great"
... "sync each scenario to each visual frame related" ... "make sure to join anything needed to be joined for that
logic". The 33 TESTING_PHASE scenarios named items and screens; his journals hold every read with the screen it saw, and
retro_triage.json labels 8,160 stash frames of older reels - but nothing joined them. tv/scenario_frames.py (a report:
reads, never writes) joins each scenario to its ITEMS (names from its Items block, kept only when a roster or a recorded
read knows them), each item to the FRAMES whose reads named it, each frame to its own PICTURE, and REC-03 to its recorded
check. Two wrong joins were caught on the way: the reel folder's f_<ms>.jpg are footage stills, not a read's picture (the
first cut found 0 of every sample on disk - a read's picture is <frameId>.jpg at the reel root); and LOOKED AT, MR-01's
only joined frame was a Spirit tooltip whose "Monarch" is the runeword's base, not the white-base control - a base read
beside a runeword no longer joins. On his data: REC-03 PASS (9/9 items read on 28 frames; the newest long session's deep
reads all warm, every commitment answered); MR-01's items were never read as themselves (his hands). Law:
test_a_scenario_names_its_own_frames (7 cases on fixtures, 6 red-proofs).

### REG-2763 - A SAVED PROFILE COULD NOT REBUILD ITS OWN VAULT ON ANOTHER PC (his ruling 2026-10-28, GrokBot's round trip)
GrokBot (#230 6467035373) loaded a profile made from his real Mac data into a fresh browser: every store came back
byte-exact, the chronicle read 0/99 · 6/403 · 0/135, and the VAULT changed shape (Grief 3x2 -> 2x1, Heart of the Oak 2x1 ->
3x2, Bul-Kathos' Wedding Band gone from the shared stash) - the vault view also reads the chronicle ledgers (a runeword's
base, the set pieces, the found log), and the profile left them out by design ("the chronicle has its own backup"). His
ruling: "profiles should carry them". The chronicle ledgers ride in their own profile group now (found log + who found,
set pieces, runewords made/unmade/profile, grail unfound, crafts); the load's question names the chronicle when it would
replace this PC's, and a store of counts says its units ("runeStash: 2 -> 6", where it counted keys). The vault's Undo
snapshot leaves the chronicle out (_vaultProfileBuild({chronicle: false})) - undoing a vault change never takes back a find
made after it. One list rules both doors: every fleet_mask ledger store is in the profile, and the shadow upload admits
every profile store but the intake history it keeps home on purpose (his order: a shadow is the owner's data one to one;
measured on his Mac's last upload: the chronicle stores all rode, nothing unsent). Law:
test_a_profile_carries_what_its_vault_reads (7 cases on the whole page in node, 4 red-proofs);
test_vault_v3_layout_keeps_every_door now asserts the chronicle rides (its old "never the chronicle" case inverted).

### REG-2762 - A SHORT FOOTAGE DISK COULD DELETE GROK CHATS THAT DO NOT FREE IT (#151, the v3823 second eye)
_grok_prune_pass read free space at the footage folder, and the plan counts each removed chat as room regained there
until the ON AIR floor plus 1 GB is met. That holds only when the chats sit on the footage disk: on a PC whose footage
lives on another volume (a Windows PC with reels on D:), a short footage disk would have removed chats older than a week
for a disk they do not feed, and the plan would have believed it recovered. The console now compares the two folders'
volumes; when they differ, or cannot be read, the disk does not decide and only the 2 GB budget can, and the prune's line
says the disk did not decide and why, never "over its floor". Live chats and the age floor held either way. Law:
test_free_space_counts_what_macos_frees (2 new cases, 2 new red-proofs).

GrokBot (#230 c6319274564): vaultAssign('Grief', WAR1) wrote the filing and both Grief tasks still targeted SHARED STASH
through a reload, which read as his hand being ignored. His ruling 2026-10-28: war items go to the Shared stash (the war
stash), and the WAR mules only when its 5 pages are full - L1, BY DESIGN; the move task should say why. The target stays
(_vaultMoveHome honours a hand filing only on a NORMAL mule) and the row now carries "war stash first", its title the
whole reason naming the mule he filed it on (_vaultMoveL1Why). Nothing is said for a filing on a normal mule or a task
that goes elsewhere. Law: test_a_war_item_on_a_war_mule_says_why_it_waits (4 cases on the whole page in node, 4
red-proofs). Its first cut borrowed the L1 laws' board, which drives headless Chrome - it ran on his Mac five times
before I saw it; moved to node, and no browser was left running.

### REG-2760 - NO SEAT COULD MEASURE WHETHER HIS LOCKERS' COPIES AGREE (#144.9, his pick 2026-10-28 12:41 IDT)
GrokBot proved on a guest that the locker card draws copies from the copies store (copyCount, through _shelfCopyCount)
while the mule window and FIND pack the vault records (_vaultRecordsForMule): a plate said "2 items in 5 copies" over one
cell each. His own records live only in his browser, so neither seat could say whether his real vault splits the same

what the card draws, what the records hold for it, how many cells FIND names, the copies store's count, the war cap where

/api/vault/copy_audit. Which side is right is decided after his numbers are read. Law:
test_a_copy_readout_says_what_each_side_counts (9 cases; the board's half driven on the whole page in node, 6 red-proofs).

### REG-2759 - A SHELF ROW COUNTED THE DEEP READER'S COMMITMENT NOTE AS A READ (GrokBot's v3823 question)
GrokBot asked whether "3 reads in 310 ms" (session 71) and "2 reads in 574 ms" (session 81) could be a read cadence. Read

journals: 2,272 deep-owed rows, every one counted; one chronicle visit note too. Both are notes about frames now, not
reads (REG-2744's class); a known-scene row (the classifier's look at a frame) stays a read. Law:
test_a_session_is_dated_by_what_it_captured (1 new case from session 71's own rows, 1 new red-proof).

### REG-2758 - IN A SHADOW, A MOVE TASK ROW WOULD NOT OPEN (#218, GrokBot's v3821 pass)
The shadow's click veil passes only the handlers named in VIEW, and _vaultTaskExpand (a task row's from -> to picture,
read only) was not there, so the owner's rows opened on his screen and not in the shadow. And the key filter stopped
Enter and Space everywhere, so a view control could be opened by mouse only. _vaultTaskExpand is in VIEW now, and Enter or
Space on the focused control itself passes when that control only moves the view; on a write control, or with a
modifier, the key is still stopped. The click veil and the key filter read one control list. Law:
test_shadow_mode_reads_their_console (veil + key cases, 3 new red-proofs; one older proof re-aimed at the longer list).

### REG-2757 - THE LAST SESSION DIGEST SAID NO DATE (#86 nit, GrokBot's v3821 pass)
The home page's 📼 LAST SESSION line read "session 74 · 1h 12m · 611 reads": which run, from when, it did not say, while
the Shelf card beside it carries the date. It now leads with the run's own capture date (_lsWhenSay from t0 - the date
REG-2736 gives a session from what it captured); a run with no t0 gets no date, never today's (REG-2752). Law:
test_the_last_session_digest_says_when (3 cases, the helper driven in node, 2 red-proofs).

### REG-2756 - FIND'S "WOULD GO" ANSWER NAMED ONE CELL FOR AN ITEM HE HOLDS THREE OF (the REG-2741 sweep)
REG-2741 made the filed answer keep every copy's cell. The router's answer for an item not filed yet ("unsorted · would
go to <locker>") still stopped at the first copy's cell, so the same item read 1 cell before Auto-Sort and 3 after. It
keeps every copy's cell now, `cell` stays the first, and FIND's would row says "3 copies: ..." as the filed row does.

(1,204 gates, the census from before it): frame.release has 120 guards, printer.stream 82, reel.route 71; a lock whose
door is control_app (prune.reports, vault.sweep_start, console.pixel_rescue) has ~485, so it still goes stale on most
console edits - that is where those acts live. A lock with no declared door, every route, an unreadable census, a
refusal that is not STALE and a law that seats the global answer keep the global rule. Law:
test_a_lock_goes_stale_only_through_its_own_guards (9 cases on a fixture census, 7 red-proofs).

His words, 2026-10-28: "identical bytes saved from the windows alt pc that has already been proved. he doesnt need to
reprove it all". Steps 1+2 (REG-2715, v3819) made a PC's census serve what that PC banked; nothing carried one PC's bank
to another, so Dean's PC re-proved every law the ALT had already proved at the same commit. The carrier, inside the $5
plan (no new product): functions/api/proofs.js takes a PC's `heart2 --export-proved` file signed exactly as a roster

### REG-2733 - THE ROUTES AUDIT CHILD NEVER ONCE CACHED, SO THE COLD PARSE STAYED IN THE CONSOLE'S HEAP (#172)
REG-2701 (v3817) sends the console's cold route census to a short-lived child (tv/audit_child.py) so ~600 MB of parse
memory leaves with it. Read from both consoles' /api/status on 2026-10-28: the routes child had FAILED on every run - 3 of
3 on the Mac, 2 of 2 on the ALT - "the routes were derived but their cache was not written", and each time the console
derived it in its own memory (the ALT console held 1,308 MB private 40 min after its v3819 start). The three route keys

ledgers the live console rewrites all the time (.char_roster.json, .tvd_roster.json) - files _routes_on_disk() has skipped
since REG-1954 because a hidden file is a private ledger, never a route. So the key moved under the child's derivation and
cached() saw a different key. Reproduced in a worktree: touching .tvd_roster.json 4 s into the child made it exit 3; left
alone it cached. The keys now skip hidden files. And on the ALT (Python 3.12) the child's reason was buried: run() showed
stderr's last line, a SyntaxWarning from a parsed law; the child's own sentence now leads.
Law: test_a_source_audit_runs_in_a_child (4 new cases, 4 new red-proofs). Open beside it: 8 invalid escape sequences in 6
law files (Python 3.12 warns; 4 are in test_control, whose re-prove costs ~90 min) - noted on #172.

### REG-2731 - THE SECOND EYE LEFT A GROK SESSION FOLDER PER LOOK, AND TWO LANES MATCHED SESSIONS BY SUBSTRING (#151)

### REG-2732 - A PROVER RUN WITH NO KNOWN START COULD ADOPT AN EARLIER RUN'S REUSE LINE (#186)
The #231 eye on v3819 (finding 2, half of it): _log_reuse reads only the bytes this run wrote (logFrom), but when that
start was unknown it read the last 256 KB of the whole log and could report an EARLIER run's "#186 CENSUS CACHE" counts
as this run's. An unknown start is now UNKNOWN (None), and mem keeps the older figure with its own time. The other half -
a long run pushing its own line out of the tail - does not happen: heart2 prints that summary at the end of the run.
Findings 3 and 4 were refuted against the code: the census cache serves per proof only for the gates the run proves
(_census_one), and _vaultUndoTake is the snapshot a door takes before it changes anything, not the undo.
Law: test_the_census_reuses_byte_identical_proofs (1 new case, 1 new red-proof).

### REG-2715 - THE CENSUS RE-PROVED WHAT A PUSH HAD JUST PROVED, AND BANKED NOTHING (#186, his ruling 2026-10-28)
"NO IT DOESNT NEED TO PROVE ITSELF. it can accept a proof earned on byte identical ... it should work with that same
recipe". Measured 2026-10-27: a push banks its PROVENs in the machine's verdict cache (29,991 entries on the Mac), and the
census on the same PC then re-proved those very laws from scratch (test_control: 27 proofs, ~92 min) while frame.release
and every river lock waited on it; heart2.prove() opened the cache only under push=True. Now `heart2.py --prove ...
--reuse` - the self-prove lane's census and only it - opens the cache: each proof is served over byte-identical inputs
through _cache_serve or run as the census always ran it (_prove_one, the whole law) and banked through _cache_bank once
the gate's closing clean run kept it PROVEN (_census_bank, flushed per gate, so a slice that stands aside keeps it). The
serve and the bank were cut out of _prove_push_one: one implementation, asked by the push and the census. A proof needing
what the PC lacks (or cannot probe) is never served. A served gate keeps the age it was measured at (_reused_ages, the
push's rule, now one helper; the slice banker stamps with it too). A served proof is kept on the banking tree's word with
no clean run here - REG-2599's rule for a run that changes no law, and his ruling. A plain --prove (run_gates, CI, a hand
run) never opens it, and HEART2_PROVE_CACHE=0 closes it (one predicate, _prove_cache_off, for push and census). The lane
spawns with --reuse and reads the prover's own "#186 CENSUS CACHE: N of M reused · K banked" line back as selfProve.reuse
(None until a run has said it). A cache that raises costs a re-prove, never a BLIND. Law: test_the_census_reuses_byte_identical_proofs (11 red-proofs, each seen RED).

re-look s_1#2 are one). Then it registers AND files in the same call, both sessions in the receipt, and the hold clears.

of route-failed, and the vault's population line says "N seen once (not yours yet - a 2nd session registers them)".

(both items already his), test_every_owned_door_writes_provenance (two sessions, a one-session case). Open questions to him

says the real elapsed time ("... in 83 s, one reload included"). Law: test_a_tab_click_is_never_silently_dropped (a board
that boots at 32 s and routes at 36 s is never reloaded; one that never boots: 60 s, one reload, 20 s).

### REG-2675 - "KOnyORush", "SOcket", "ArmOr" ON HIS CHARACTER LIST (GrokBot bug 11)

keys and 'O' sorts before 'o'. Socket, Armor and Weapon are his real level-1 mules, so a "UI word" denylist would have
refused them: the fix is the spelling. A capital O inside a word is a small o (a leading O stays, all-caps still

rewritten. Law: test_a_name_read_with_a_capital_o_is_shown_right.

### REG-2631 - AN ALL-HIT PUSH STILL SPENT MINUTES PROVING (heart2 keyer, GB-box, 2026-10-24)
v3792's hook served 303 of 303 proofs from the cache and still spent 2m39 proving. MEASURED on the box (19 gates, 226
proofs, all served, 0 clean runs): 563,770 file reads - ~1,250 inputs for each of 452 keys, since the clean wave's peek
and the main pass's lookup each key every proof - every read under the cache's one lock, plus a clean wave that built
and deleted a sandbox per lane to run nothing. Fix: the keyer serves a digest only within a QUIET STRETCH keyed on
(path, size, mtime_ns, ctime_ns, inode, generation); _run_gate and _prove_one end it on entry and exit, so no digest
outlives a law run or a tamper write; hashing left the lock. The clean wave leaves out a gate the cache serves whole on
this tree's keys with no REG-2599 clean run owed (the wave is order, never a verdict). Keys are byte-identical to before
(checked on 278 proofs). Law: tv/test_an_all_hit_push_reads_each_input_once.py (5 RED_PROOFs).

### REG-2630 - A PROOF THE BOX OR THE CENSUS BANKED NEVER REACHED THE MAC'S HOOK (proof-keys import, GB-box, 2026-10-24)

the hook it was meant to shorten; the box's own --prove --push cache had no import path at all, so a push touching
bible.html or control_app.py re-proved its whole set on the Mac. `heart2 --export-proved DIR` now writes the PROVENs a
clean checkout's HEAD bytes still key, with an `export` manifest; `heart2 --import-proved FILE...` banks a box export
or any finished census shard of THIS HEAD (a partial set too), each entry only under the key this checkout computes -
a key the file claims for other bytes is dropped, named and never served. Each entry keeps its tree (REG-2599 clean run
here still owed where the push changes the law). Law: test_a_proof_proved_elsewhere_counts_only_under_this_trees_key
(23 cases incl. the real keyer on a real gate, 10 red-proofs).

### REG-2602 - A SHIP MOVED THE KEY OF EVERY PROOF THAT HOLDS A STAMP SURFACE (proof-keys step 4, GB-box, 2026-10-23)

b58879ec (v3790) 337 of 5162 keyed proofs kept their key, so a census banked on the commit before a ship was a miss on the

reviews: inert-text, strict TASKS rows, literal counts (per surface, exact case, regex matches), byte-keyed memos, fixed
gates-row words, short versions in a proof. Law: test_a_version_bump_keeps_the_proofs_of_laws_that_never_read_the_version
(19 cases, 21 red-proofs).

### REG-2598 - A GATE NEVER STARTS ON A RUN RECORD THE GATE BEFORE IT WROTE (proof-keys build, GB-box, 2026-10-23)

### REG-2595 - THE 16-SHARD RUN IS A POST-PUSH CENSUS THAT NAMES THE NEXT BATCH (proof-keys build, GB-box, 2026-10-23)
Elad's ruling 17:04: the shard run no longer blocks a push; it runs after it, on ci/proof-keys-<sha12> at the pushed
sha, and its findings are the next version's fixes. `proof_shard.py --census DIR [--head SHA] [--out F]` reads the shard
artifacts and writes one markdown report: assigned / PROVEN / owed / unbanked counts, slowest and mean shard wall (from
each prove.log), a dir with no store named, a foreign sha flagged, and a table of every law owed a fix (law, proof,
verdict, why, shard). It always exits 0. The fan-in job runs it with `if: always()`, appends it to the job summary and

### REG-2613 - THE BACKGROUND PROVER RAN OUTSIDE child_guard: A CLOSED CONSOLE LEFT IT RUNNING - board #34

self_prove.spawn started `heart2.py --prove` with a bare Popen. On Windows nothing tied it to the console, so a console
that closed or crashed left the prover, and every gate process under it, running beside his game. It now goes through
child_guard's one door as role "prover" (scope checkout, 0..1). Windows: a Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, with its
below-normal, no-window flags unchanged. POSIX: its own session, under nice. The door ends a previous prover of this
checkout first, and the watchdog ends an orphan whose console is gone. The watchdog knows a self-prover only by the
`-X tvd_self_prove` marker in its argv (a free-form CPython -X option; heart2 is unchanged), never by bare
`heart2.py --prove`, so a pre-push or hand-run prover is never ended. The store records the console that started a
prover (startedBy); a prover that ended because its console ended is booked a stand-aside, not a failure with the 3 h
backoff. A law's recording popen never enters the real door's ledger. child_guard is imported at spawn time only, so the
pre-push gate loads nothing new. Measured: spawn() median 0.6-0.9 ms before, 0.9-1.3 ms after; hooks/ reference
neither module. Scope: Dean's PC and the ALT (the Windows sync check). Law:
tv/test_the_prover_is_owned_by_its_console.py (12 cases, 8 red-proofs; Windows command lines with spaces, the real door
under a faked kernel32). Lands after or alongside claude/m4-perpc/c, which also edits tv/self_prove.py.

### REG-2616 - THE KEEPALIVE COULD NOT BRING A CONSOLE BACK AFTER A REBOOT WITH NOBODY SIGNED IN - 2026-10-23 (his ruling on REG-2614)

REG-2614's task runs as the signed-in user (InteractiveToken), so a PC that rebooted to the sign-in screen - the ALT

then too. An OPTIONAL install, the default unchanged: `console_keepalive.py --install-unattended USER` re-registers
the same task as USER with LogonType Password through Register-ScheduledTask. The password is read from an
environment variable (default TVD_KEEPALIVE_PASSWORD) and handed to the one PowerShell child in its own environment
(TVD_KA_PW; the caller's variable is not passed on; review r3: stdin under -Command never reached it), and is never
in argv, the task XML, the repo, a log or an answer (Windows' refusal text, CLIXML unescaped, has it replaced by
***). Made = the task's own XML says LogonType Password. A console pass finds the owner's task 'already' there and
never removes a task whose LogonType is not InteractiveToken, even one it first made (review r3). Law: tv/test_a_dead_windows_console_comes_back_by_itself.py
(class Unattended, 7 red-proofs). Note: a console started with nobody signed in runs in the background session -
its server and sync run, no window shows until it is restarted from a signed-in session.

Round 3 of REG-2614 (review r2): schtasks output is read as bytes (UTF-16 with or without BOM, UTF-8, else the locale
page with bad bytes replaced) and parsed inside the try - text=True on a Hebrew Windows raised and the task was never
made; the 90 s pass deadline is driven by the law in a child process.

### REG-2614 - A WINDOWS CONSOLE THAT DIED STAYED DEAD UNTIL THE NEXT SIGN-IN - 2026-10-23 (Windows console watchdog)

2026-10-16: the ALT's console died with no error and nothing relaunched it until someone signed in to Windows, so it
missed 302 commits. The sign-in start (REG-1660) runs once, at sign-in; nothing watched a console that died after.
Fix: tv/console_keepalive.py, run every 5 minutes by a per-user scheduled task "TV DIABLO keepalive" (pythonw,
hidden, InteractiveToken - no stored password, no administrator - on battery too, IgnoreNew, 2-minute limit,
registered from XML so a long path with spaces fits). A pass connects to :17772 only: REFUSED is gone and starts
start_tvd_win.ps1 -Background hidden and windowless; up, slow (a timed-out connect) and unknown are left alone. A
console closed on purpose (control_app's one exit surface writes tv/.tvd_exited_on_purpose, the next boot clears it,
primary Windows console only) or a stood-down supervisor (.tvd_supervisor_pause) is never relaunched; one launch per
10 minutes, booked before it is tried; a torn memory file is said and rewritten. The console makes the task beside its
sign-in start (console_doctor.ensure_keepalive_task) on the SAME consent: never made after a removal, withdrawn with
a removed or refused sign-in start (only if this console made it), nothing done on UNKNOWN.
LIMIT: "without a sign-in" means without a NEW sign-in - the task runs in the signed-in (also locked) session. A PC
that rebooted to the sign-in screen has no session to film in; starting a console there needs a stored password or
S4U, which also cannot capture the desktop. That is his call, not made here.
GUARD: tv/test_a_dead_windows_console_comes_back_by_itself.py (31 cases, 25 red-proofs) and, on real Windows (run by
tv/windows_boot_check.py in the tv-windows-boot job, no workflow edit), tv/windows_keepalive_check.py (the XML registered, read back, left on a second pass, deleted;
a closed port reads gone; a pass launches once then holds).

Round 2 (review r1 FAIL, 3 majors + 1 minor + 1 nit): the task runs with ExecutionTimeLimit PT0S and the launcher is
started with CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB (retried inside the job if the job forbids it) - a PT2M limit's job kill took the
console it had just started; the pass ends itself after 90 s instead. Exits recorded when the WINDOW LOOP ended under
the console (window-closed, webview-finally, main-after-window - a WebView crash leaves that way) never write the
on-purpose mark, and the keepalive ignores one already on disk. A missing task is settled by the full
`schtasks /Query /FO CSV /NH` list (exact name), not English "cannot find" - a Hebrew or German schtasks never made it.
A refusal on stdout is kept; the lastAction write builds on the booked memory, not a re-read.

### REG-2612 - #144 RECURRED ON LINUX AND NOTHING RECORDED WHO REMOVED THE SANDBOX - board #71

The 2026-10-23 01:11-02:21 IDT stage prove on the Linux box lost every root .md/.html/.json and 13 tv files from lane 4's
sandbox in one gate, while a gate that touches no files ran; later gates read "bible.html is not in the sandbox", and the
sandbox left behind had lost its owner file. That box has no dirhelper, cron or tmpreaper, so REG-2438's macOS atime
theory (on Claude's unshipped M2 branch, marked "root cause UNVERIFIED") is not the whole cause. The pattern is a
whole-sandbox rmtree's. Instrument, not a fix: every stale sweep and every run's own drop writes one line
(time, remover pid, sandbox, owner, why) to heart2-sweeps.log in the temp dir before it removes, and a vanish now
reports whether the owner file survives, the sandbox root's age, and any journal line naming that sandbox. Law:
tv/test_a_vanished_sandbox_names_its_remover.py (4 cases, 5 red-proofs). Rides with M2's heart2.py track.
Round 2 (grok-4.7 review r1 FAIL, 5 findings): the witness never raises (any Exception -> "witness unreadable",
the restore always runs); every new sandbox writes a `created` line, so its age comes from its birth, not a root mtime
any unlink moves; the journal holds only integers, the basename and a fixed code (an owner file's raw text could have
put `skipped=` into the gate tail heart2 parses), is 0600, written in one O_APPEND write under flock (Windows: no lock,
a torn line fails the exact-field match), capped at 1 MB -> last 256 KB, read as a capped tail with errors replaced, and
a failed write is said on stderr. Laws: 11 cases, 11 red-proofs (order pinned: the line exists when _rmtree_hard runs;
root GONE read before the restore rebuilds it). Not taken: a /proc fd scan for the deleter - by the time the witness
runs the gate has exited and an rmtree is done, so it would name nobody on the case it exists for.
Round 3 (review r2 PASS, 2 minors): the cap trims the journal IN PLACE under the same lock (no temp file, no replace
another lane could race, the 0600 inode kept); laws pin the drop's line-before-remove order, the cap (newest kept, no
torn line, still private) and that an owner file's `skipped=` never reaches the gate tail. 14 cases, 14 red-proofs.
Round 4 (review r3 FAIL, 1 major + 3 minors): the journal is opened WITHOUT O_APPEND - every write is placed by lseek
under the lock, so the cap's kept tail really lands at offset 0 on every OS - and the cap writes the kept tail FIRST and
cuts the file to it after, so a reader never sees it empty. Every write is finished (a short os.write is looped). On
Windows the writers lock one byte at 0x7FFFFFF0 with msvcrt (a lock on a byte a reader reads would fail its read). Laws
add: a keep size off the line length (an older line kept, size within the cap), no empty journal at the cut, a short
write finished, the Windows lock byte, and owner-file text driven through the real owner file into
_skipped_every_law. 17 cases, 19 red-proofs.

Round 5 (review r4 PASS, 1 nit): on Windows the journal lock was taken with LK_LOCK, which gives up after about ten seconds, and the writer then capped UNLOCKED beside a holder - a cut that could drop the line just written. The lock is now polled with LK_NBLCK for up to 30 s (as _win_lock does); a writer that still has no lock appends its line, skips the cap, and says so on stderr. Two new cases and two new red-proofs (lock not had never cuts; the lock is polled, not tried once).
