GrokBot on v3784 (perf3.py, relayed 2026-10-22): the 550-item speed test finishes but takes ~7.5 min; a hand add costs 30 ms at 50 items, 145 ms at 250, 0.9 s at 350, 2.0 s at 450, 2.7 s at 600. A paint rebuilt every record three times per locker card (36 rebuilds per paint with ten lockers).
FIX - eight memos, each with the reason it cannot change an answer in its comment:
- REG-2420 suggestMule's fold hop keeps the canonical per trimmed string name (_sugFoldCanon); dropped if the engine, resolver, roster or fold is replaced; capped at 5,000.
- REG-2421 _vaultWarKeeper's walk of the saved moves runs once per bag object (_vaultWarKeeperIx, a WeakMap on the bag), same key order and rule.
- REG-2422 _itemCells and artOr's _vpMadeBase read the planner store through _vpMadeRec: the store is still read on every call, and parsed again only when the stored string changes; _vpMadeOf still parses fresh (its callers hold the record).
- REG-2423 d2rItemLookup's catalogue walk runs once per trimmed name (_d2rItemLookupWalk), dropped when ITEMS or ITEM_REGISTRY is replaced or ITEMS changes length; the memo law pins that the BOSSES build is their one writer.
- REG-2424 one router ask per name per READ PHASE outside renderVault (_vaultSeamPhase opens the paint memo for code that writes nothing - the plan of one hand row, one records pass, the collect loop before its commit, the unrouted check after it - and drops it when the phase ends; inside renderVault the paint's own memo is used unchanged). _vaultRecords re-enters with an explicit flag, so a phase that opens no memo can never recurse.
- REG-2425 _spNorm (the set-piece fold) once per string; cleared past 5,000 or when _etherNorm is replaced.
- REG-2426 the shelf is one records pass (window._vrFindPass, the pass FIND already used): 31 of a paint's 36 rebuilds are gone.
- REG-2427 _vaultKeeps tests ITEMS membership with one Set (rebuilt when ITEMS is replaced or changes length; a non-object entry keeps the old walk).
window._vaultMemoOff = true turns all eight off (the v3784 path). It is how the memo law makes its reference run, and how tv/vault_speed_bench.py measures before and after on one tree.

Per add at 160 items: 480 router asks (3 per name; 1,452 with the phases off), 0-1 folds, 1 catalogue walk, 2 keeper walks, 1 ITEMS walk, 0 planner parses; one paint rebuilds the records 5 times. Node is not Chrome (no DOM cost): GrokBot re-measures with perf3.py on his screen.
VERIFIED identical: the memo law's fixture (136 steps) gave byte-identical answers with the memos on, with them off, and on the pristine v3784 page; the 36 existing node laws that drive these functions still pass; the hook's anchor check reads all 5,301 declared red-proofs well formed.

### REG-2557 - THE SCRUB READER BOUND A POINTER FIRST-WINS AND FROM A QUOTED MENTION (GB-L, 2026-10-22, v3788)

and `echo '_n=GIT_DIR'; export "$_n=.."` reported a GIT_DIR export bash never makes, and `env echo "$_n"` was a hit.

only when the held name is assigned. Law: 5 new `_REACH` cases, 2 RED_PROOFs "REG-2557" (first-wins, any position).

### REG-2551 - THE SCRUB LAW READ ONLY THE SCRUB BLOCK: A POINTER RE-EXPORTED AFTER IT KEPT EVERY CASE GREEN (the Grok CLI review of Push A2, MEDIUM M2)

test_a_leaked_git_dir_never_writes_the_real_repo's scrub cases (TheHookUnsetsThePointerBeforeAnyStage,
ThePushsOwnOptionsSurviveTheScrub) run ONLY the hook's `# >>> scrub-git-env` block in bash. An `export GIT_DIR=...` - or a
`GIT_DIR=... cmd` prefix, or the same for GIT_WORK_TREE / GIT_INDEX_FILE / GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY / GIT_COMMON_DIR - written
anywhere in hooks/pre-push after `# <<< scrub-git-env` would hand every later stage the pointer back while each case stayed
green. Found by the Grok CLI review of Push A2.
FIX: class NoStageAfterTheScrubPointsGitBack reads the WHOLE hook after the block as bash reads it: comments out (a `#` opens
one only at a word start, outside quotes), quotes followed the way bash nests them ('...', $'...', "...", and $(...) and `...`
inside "..."), backslash-newline joined, and every heredoc body read whole - none is excluded, so none has to be shown to be
data (under an unquoted delimiter bash expands its $(...); a quoted one costs nothing to read). It fails on any assignment or
export of a pointer - git's own --local-env-vars list less the two option carriers (REG-2394), plus those five by name - in
the forms bash has: NAME= / NAME+= / ${NAME:=...} (a plain assignment, a `NAME=... cmd` prefix, env), export / declare /
typeset / local / readonly, read / printf -v / mapfile; strings are read too (`env "GIT_DIR=$x" cmd`, `eval "export ..."`).
Its reach is DRIVEN before its verdict counts: 37 texts whose answer is known (30 it must find, 7 it must not - a comment, a
use of the value, an unset, TV_PUSHED_GIT_DIR, `git --git-dir=`); and on the real hook a canary re-export planted where the
reader could lose its place (the first line after the block, after each heredoc, the end) must be found there, or the verdict
is UNKNOWN, not passing. Its reach, stated: a name built at run time (`v=GIT_DIR; export "$v=..."`) and a `case` pattern's `)`
inside $(...) (the hook has none) are not read.
MEASURED: on the hook today 0 re-exports, its one heredoc (PYGATE) closed, nothing left open. Bash's own parse of the same text
(`declare -f` of it as a function body - comments dropped by bash itself) holds the same GIT_* tokens as the reader's code view:
none on the hook, one GIT_DIR on each tampered hook below. 25 single-point mutants of the reader (each quote kind, the comment
rule, the continuation, each heredoc spelling, the $(...) close, each assignment / export / read form) - each red BY ASSERTION
against the real hook.
GUARD: RED proofs [12] (`export GIT_DIR=/tmp/x` on the line after the block) and [13] (a `GIT_DIR="$TV_PUSHED_GIT_DIR" git
diff` prefix inside $(...) in a string, past the heredoc 1,100 lines on) - each red BY ASSERTION in
test_no_line_after_the_scrub_points_git_at_a_repo_again (failures=1, errors=0; clean 10/10 OK). No `needs`: the reader is
Python and git, so a PC without bash proves them too. heart2 --prove (one worker): 14/14 PROVEN.

### REG-2359 - THE NODE RULE READ ONLY SKIP COUNTS, SO A LAW THAT SKIPPED FOR ANY REASON WAS EXCUSED ON A PC WITHOUT NODE (round-3 review of REG-2354, push-proof track T2)

The round-3 review of REG-2354, 2026-10-22. That rule filed a tamper ELSEWHERE when both runs skipped every case (the counts in their tails), the PC had no node, and the gate's source mentioned node. It never asked WHY the cases skipped. A law that mentions node and skips everything for want of his D2R install or his footage was excused on a PC without node: a BLIND turned into an ELSEWHERE. Its comment and its line also claimed more than was measured. They said every law skipped "no node on PATH", but only 2 laws in the tree print that message (109 distinct skip reasons name node: "node is absent", "node unavailable", ...). They also said "it is proven on a PC that has it", though nothing was proven.

FIX: heart2 now arms a skip watch on every proof run (TV_GATE_SKIPS=1 beside TV_GATE_KILLS). gate_trace/sitecustomize.py wraps unittest.result.TestResult.addSkip in the run's OWN process and writes one O line per skipped case: `case=<unittest's id> reason=<its words>`. It works at any verbosity. 73 of the 236 node-reaching laws with red-proofs print at verbosity 1, where the log shows only an `s`. The variable is taken off the environment at boot, so a child's skips are never counted as the law's. The tamper is ELSEWHERE only when REG-2354's conditions hold AND:
- the watch saw every skip the tampered run reported (`skipped=N`);
- at least one reason names node;
- every other skip is a case that the gate's source runs only on POSIX (REG-2357's reader), on a PC that is not POSIX.

That last clause covers T5's reader-cap law on Dean's PC (Windows): 11 cases skip for node and 2 for Windows. Checked against T5's branch: the reader finds exactly those 2 cases. A skip for anything else, a skip the watch did not see, or a run with no watch is judged as before. A law that should be excused anyway declares "needs": "node" (REG-1686). BLIND_RULE stays 2: rule 2 never shipped, so every census stamped 2 will have been judged under this rule. The ELSEWHERE line now gives the counts and a reason it measured, and claims no proof.

GUARD: tv/test_a_proof_that_needs_what_this_pc_lacks_is_elsewhere.py (36 RED proofs with REG-1686/1688/2354/2355/2357, heart2 36/36 PROVEN). The cases: a reason that is not node's, one such reason among node's, a skip the watch did not see, no watch, T5's node-plus-POSIX shape (ELSEWHERE without POSIX, BLIND with it), and the line's words. A real fixture law at verbosity 1 runs through `_run_gate_once`: the watch names each of its own skips and none of its child's.

ROUND 4 (the review of round 3): the ELSEWHERE line said "every case skipped in BOTH runs, each for what this PC lacks", and only the TAMPERED run's reasons are read (the clean run's are dropped before the tampered run). The line now says only what was measured: both runs' counts, each from its own tail ("clean run: 4 of 4 skipped; tampered run: 4 of 4 skipped"), and the tampered run's reasons ("the skip watch read the tampered run's 4 skip reason(s), each for what this PC lacks: 4 name node ..."). The rule did not change. The clean run's reasons are not required. Its verdict is often one run reused across the gate (REG-1669) or taken from the clean wave (REG-1992), and a reuse path that did not carry the reasons would turn a node-less PC's JS laws BLIND again, Dean's PC's 53. 2 RED proofs hold the words.

LEFT: a reason that names node in another sense ("a DOM node") would read as node's on a PC without node, in a gate that reaches for node. Scanned: none of the 109 node-naming skip reasons in the tree uses another sense. A law whose result class never reaches TestResult.addSkip is judged as before (BLIND). Not run on Windows here. The O lines come from the same audit hook the kill watch already runs there. A tamper that changed WHY its cases skip (a clean run skipping for something else and a tampered run skipping for node) is excused on the tampered run's reasons. Both runs skipping everything for want of node on such a PC is the case the rule exists for.

### REG-2358 - A SIGNAL THE LAW SENT ITS OWN HELPER EXPLAINED THE NEXT DEATH OF THAT PID (round-3 review of REG-2356, push-proof track T2)

The round-3 review of REG-2356, 2026-10-22. `_kills_in` let an X line explain every K line of its pid below it. A law kills its own helper (X, then K: explained). Later a NEW process gets the same pid (pids are recycled) and is killed from outside (a second K). That second K was explained by the old X, so a run that a kill from outside ended read as an ordinary red. A group X explained every later death of any member pid the same way, and so did a signal to every process.

FIX: an X explains at most the FIRST K of each pid it reaches below it: its target pid, each member of its group, or every pid for `all`. The first K uses up that X's one chance at the pid whether or not it is explained (a different signal, a pipe, a member already gone). A pid that died once is a new process the next time.

GUARD: tv/test_a_killed_run_is_never_a_red.py, now 29 RED proofs (2 new for this, 1 for REG-2357), heart2 29/29 PROVEN. The reader fixtures cover a second death by pid, by group and to every process; a pipe death that uses up the chance; and the law killing the recycled pid again (explained, because each X has its own death).

ROUND 4 (the review of round 3): only a K used up an X's chance at a pid, so a target that ENDED WITHOUT a K kept it. Two common shapes do. A helper handles the law's SIGTERM and exits 0, and the hook wrote K only for a negative returncode. Or the law kills its helper and drops the Popen unwaited: `Popen.__del__` and `subprocess._cleanup` reap it through `_internal_poll`, which nothing watched, and the object leaves the exit sweep's WeakSet. The next process to get that pid, killed from outside by the same signal, was explained by the old X, so the run read red, and a tampered run red that way is PROVEN. The review measured both with the real hook, and this Mac's pid counter wrapped during it (79005 to 700 in about 15 minutes).

FIX (round 4): the hook says every child's END, not only a death by signal. It writes `E pid=N rc=R head=H` for an exit with any code, from wait, from poll, and from `_internal_poll`, which is now watched too (so a dropped child's death is said, K or E). At this process's exit, every child it started that is still running is written `E ... rc=left`: init reaps it, and no line of the run will ever say its death. Only the process that started a child says its end. A forked copy inherits the parent's Popen objects, and its wait or poll on one answers ECHILD, which Popen reads as an exit 0; written, that end would close the parent's own kill of the same child. `_kills_in` treats a K and an E alike as an end. An X explains a death only if it was written after that pid's previous end, by pid, by group or to every process. That also covers a first death the X never reached. Both of the review's shapes now read UNKNOWN through the real hook, and so does a helper still running when its parent exits.

GUARD (round 4): tv/test_a_killed_run_is_never_a_red.py, now 34 RED proofs (7 new, and the 2 round-3 anchors moved onto the new reader), heart2 34/34 PROVEN. The review's script runs through the real hook. The graceful helper's E, the dropped helper's K and the left helper's `rc=left` are each written, the law's own signals stay explained, and the next process to get any of those pids, killed from outside, is unexplained. A forked copy writes nothing about its parent's child. Through the real `_run_gate_once`, `_prove_one` and `_prove_push_one` with a fixture cache, the graceful and dropped shapes followed by an outside kill of the recycled pid read UNKNOWN / UNPROVABLE and bank nothing. Without the outside kill they are judged as before (red, PROVEN). The OS cannot be asked to hand a pid out again, so the recycled process's death is written in the hook's own K format; the X and the end are the real hook's.

LEFT: a K line carries no start time, so a process that joins a signalled group AFTER the signal and dies first is still explained by it. No known killer does that inside one run. Round 4 closes a pid's chance only at an end some traced process writes. An X stays open for the rest of the run when its target is a grandchild reaped by a shell or by init, a pid outside the run, a child reaped by a direct os.waitpid (asyncio's child watcher: such a child's end is said only by the exit sweep), or a child of a helper that ended by os._exit or a kill before its exit sweep. A group X explains the first death of any pid in a group of that number, and the number can be reused once every member of the group is gone. Each of these needs the recycled pid killed from outside by the same signal inside one run. The fix makes no attempt at Windows, where the watch never fires (REG-2350).

### REG-2356 - A TEARDOWN SIGNAL EXPLAINED A KILL FROM OUTSIDE, SO A BLIND LAW WAS BANKED PROVEN (review of REG-2350, push-proof track T2)

An adversarial review of REG-2350, 2026-10-22, reproduced against this branch. `_kills_in` treated a K line as explained by ANY X line to the same pid or group. It ignored order and signal number. The hook wrote an X even when the signal went to a child that was already dead but not yet reaped. So a helper killed from OUTSIDE the run (jetsam, a reap) and then signalled by the law's teardown before it was reaped read as a death the run caused. That teardown is `os.killpg(p.pid, SIGKILL); os.kill(p.pid, SIGKILL); p.wait()`, child_guard._kill_tree_default's shape. The run read as an ordinary red. MEASURED with the review's script: a probe law that never reads its subject (its true verdict is BLIND) came back PROVEN from `_prove_push_one`, and the fixture verdict cache held the PROVEN. `_run_gate_once` read red for the killpg+kill teardown, and for a by-pid SIGTERM against a SIGKILL death. The same law with a `Popen.kill()` teardown (which polls first) was UNPROVABLE. Exposure in the tree was latent: render_check, child_guard `end()` and shard_suite poll before they signal. Any teardown that does not would have reopened it.

FIX: the hook checks the target BEFORE it writes the X (the audit hook runs before the signal leaves), and it reaps nothing to do so. It writes `dead=1` when the signal can end nothing at its target number. That is a pid already dead (a zombie or no process: macOS getpgid answers ESRCH for both; on Linux /proc says Z or PF_EXITING), or, for a group, a live pid that leads no group (killpg then reaches no one, ESRCH). It names in `gone=` every tracked member of a signalled group that was already dead. `_kills_in` lets an X explain a K only when the X is ABOVE the K in the watch file, carries the SAME signal number, is not `dead=1`, and does not name that pid in `gone=`. The review proposed reaping the dead child (Popen.poll) before the X instead. That was measured and not done: kill() on a zombie succeeds (POSIX), and on the reaped pid it raises ESRCH, so a reap inside the watch would change what the law's own os.kill returns. A RED_PROOF holds that line. MEASURED on macOS: a killed child's pipe never read EOF while its pid still answered getpgid (0 of 700 trials, 400 of them under 12 busy loops), so a teardown sent the moment a law sees its helper die is already `dead=1`. After the fix the review's scripts read UNPROVABLE with nothing banked (killpg and Popen.kill teardowns; 6 of 6 repeats of the killpg one under load), and UNKNOWN for the killpg+kill, by-pid SIGTERM and Popen.kill teardowns (5 of 5 repeats).

GUARD (registered in tv/run_gates.py): tv/test_a_killed_run_is_never_a_red.py (26 RED proofs with REG-2350, heart2 26/26 PROVEN). New cases: six probe modes, each red only because of a kill from outside followed by a signal of the law's own, through the real `_run_gate_once` (UNKNOWN). The review's shape also goes through `_prove_one` (UNPROVABLE) and `_prove_push_one` with a fixture cache (UNPROVABLE, nothing banked). The same teardown on a LIVE helper stays PROVEN. Real zombies through the hook (`dead=1`, `gone=`, and a zombie that still takes the law's own kill), and the reader one rule at a time.

LEFT: the microseconds between the hook's check and the signal itself. A child killed from outside in that window by the SAME signal is explained, though the effect on the law is the one it was about to cause itself. A child the law signals while it is still alive but already shutting down on an outside SIGTERM (a handler that takes time) is explained too. No known outside killer sends one: reap sends `kill -9` (its only kill, measured) and jetsam SIGKILL, which no handler delays. Only a child of the process that sends the group signal can be named in `gone=`. A group member that another traced process reaps is judged by order and signal alone. The Linux /proc branch has no heart2 RED_PROOF, since no PC that runs heart2 has /proc. The law's zombie probes depend on it on Linux CI; they have not run on Linux yet.

### REG-2355 - A BLIND FILED UNDER THE OLD RULE WOULD NEVER HAVE BEEN JUDGED AGAIN (Dean's PC, push-proof track T2)

Companion to REG-2354, from Dean's diff 01. A census gate is owed a proof only when its OWN file changes. self_prove stops for good once the census reads current. So the 56 BLIND verdicts Dean's census filed under the old rule would have stood for ever under the fixed one, unchanged gate files and all.

FIX: `heart2.BLIND_RULE = 2`. A census written under an older rule (no `blindRule`) owes its whole BLIND list again, by name (`blind_rule_owed`); a census stamped with this rule carries what is still owed as `blindRuleOwed`. A gate judged by any run leaves that list whatever its new verdict, so a slice always shrinks it. `slice_owed` owes the list; `self_prove.census_state` reads the census stale while it is not empty. On his Mac this re-judges the census's BLIND gates once.

### REG-2353 - A PASSING PUSH LEFT NO ACCOUNT OF WHAT IT PROVED, REUSED OR RE-RAN (#42 R16, push-proof track T2)

Spec R16 and section 6, 2026-10-21. hooks/pre-push deletes its prove log when heart2 exits 0. The v3783 series (six attempts, ~355 minutes of proving) could be reconstructed only from logs that happened to survive. Nothing said beforehand what a push would reuse, narrow or run in full. Nothing said afterwards whether a banked proof had been run again for the same bytes.

FIX:
- `python3 tv/heart2.py --forecast NAMES` prints, before any proving, a block headed "#42 FORECAST". Each law in scope gets one row: hit (the verdict cache will serve it), narrow (the red memory names its cases), full, and UNKEYABLE with the reason. Each row also gives the runs and, where gate_costs.json measured the gate, the seconds of the full runs. It uses a sandbox, the run's own key_for, and the predicates the serving reads answer with (peek for the cache, _red_peek for the red memory), so a forecast hit is exactly what the push will reuse and nothing it asks is marked used. Any failure prints UNKNOWN; it always exits 0.
- Every `--push` run appends one record to `heart2_pushes.jsonl` in git's common dir. That is one file per machine, shared by every worktree, outside every work tree, so never in `git status` or a sandbox. HEART2_PUSHES_PATH points it elsewhere. Per proof the record holds: the forecast path decided before any run of it, the path taken, the verdict, seconds, whether it was banked, and missWhy. It also holds wall and wave seconds, the seams, runs a signal ended (REG-2350), exit / failures / stop / unmatched names, and the cache summary.
- A proof whose key the cache would serve when the run BEGAN, and which ran anyway, is a PROVE-ONCE VIOLATION, printed and recorded. This is the shape of the live store() trim to CACHE_MAX that evicts entries mid-run (spec section 0).
- `--pushes [N]` prints the table. tv/prove_record.py is the one writer: exclusive lock, one fsync'd line, keeps the newest 200, refuses any file not named like its own.

ROUND 3 (the review of T2, with track T1): `_servable_keys` (the run's servable set, taken at push start over EVERY entry) and the forecast asked `cache.lookup()` and `_red_recall()`. Under T1's stores those are the serving reads, which record usedAt (both stores evict by use), so every entry would read as used at push start, before one proof ran. `_VerdictCache.peek()` is now the one predicate a banked verdict must pass, side-effect free; `lookup()` answers with it and is the only reader that may mark. `_red_peek()` is the red memory's read that marks nothing; `_red_recall()` answers with it. The clean wave's all-hit check (does every proof of this gate stand banked in this tree?) asks peek() too. It is a question, not a use: the main pass's lookup() marks what it serves. Merging with T1 means its usedAt mark goes in lookup()/_red_recall() and its facts rule in peek().

GUARD (registered in tv/run_gates.py): tv/test_a_push_records_its_forecast_and_actual.py (29 RED proofs with REG-2352 and REG-2357, heart2 29/29 PROVEN). Round 3 adds a cache whose serving read records every key it is asked. The servable set, the forecast and the clean wave's all-hit check ask it nothing, the push marks the hit it served, and lookup() and peek() agree on every entry shape.

ROUND 4 (the review of round 3): that guard tested a proxy. It asked who CALLED lookup() and _red_recall(), not whether anything MARKED an entry used. The default merge with T1 puts T1's usedAt mark inside peek() (the clean half of the merge) and inside _red_peek() (its one conflict, taken as T2's side), and every law of both tracks stayed green (measured by the review). The law now asserts the EFFECT. `NothingAskedMarksAnEntryUsed` builds a REAL verdict cache and a REAL red memory: fixture files written by heart2's own writers, the real _red_key / _red_peek / _red_recall, and nothing of the machine's. It asks the servable set, the forecast, a push run's start, the clean wave's all-hit check, peek() and _red_peek(). The 128+N rule reads only the LAW's own exit code, and the kill watch reports deaths only of children that a TRACED python process started through subprocess.Popen. Any other descendant killed from outside writes no K line: a shell helper's job (the shell then exits 137, written as an ordinary E line, not a death), a non-python child's own children (a Python-Playwright law's Chrome under its node driver, which is what reap's Chrome pattern kills, and Chrome's renderer/GPU helpers), a multiprocessing worker, or any child of a python run with -I/-E or a scrubbed PYTHONPATH. The review's probe: a law runs `sh -c 'sleep 30 & echo $!; wait $!'` and kills the job with an unwatched `kill -9`; _run_gate_once returns False, _prove_one returns PROVEN, and _prove_push_one banks PROVEN. origin/main has the same exposure today, for every kill. This push narrows it: the law's own signal death, its own 128+N exit and every watched Popen child's death now read UNKNOWN. It does not close it. A possible narrowing, not attempted here: read a watched child's own 128+N exit as a death by N of an unseen descendant, explained only by an X of N that reaches that child's group. First measure which laws' helpers exit 128+N on purpose.

Windows has no negative exit codes, so the watch never fires there. That is a NEVER-WRONG hole, not just a missing feature (the round-3 review): on Dean's PC or the ALT, a law or a helper killed from outside (taskkill, TerminateProcess) exits with the terminate code (1 by default), which reads as an ordinary red. A tampered run ended that way is PROVEN in that PC's census. The protection above is POSIX-only and this item stays open. A fix needs the reaper to record what it terminated (or a terminate code no law exits with), and was not attempted in this track.

### REG-2342 - THE RED MEMORY WAS PER CHECKOUT AND KEYED BY POSITION, SO A FRESH WORKTREE RAN test_control's 27 TAMPERED PROOFS IN FULL (2026-10-21, prove-once R2)

Measured on the v3783 push 13 (prove-once spec section 2): the worktree push ran test_control's 27 tampered proofs in full at 187-227 s each, serial in the browser lock, while main's memory held proofs 0-26. `RED_MEMORY = os.path.join(HERE, ...)` (per checkout, though its comment said per machine); the key hashed the proof's idx, so inserting one proof re-keyed every proof below it; eviction was by learn time at a 2,000 cap (main's file held 2,269 entries on 2026-10-21, over the cap old code applies at its next write); the tmp name was fixed and an unreadable memory was read as empty and then overwritten.

The key is (gate, file, find, replace) with no idx (`_red_key` returns a str carrying `.legacy`, the pre-R2 key); a recall falls back to the legacy key and the next write re-files the entry under the new key, marking the old one. Every recall stamps `usedAt` (written on the verdict cache's per-gate flush, on the next learn, and at exit); at the 20,000 cap a re-filed old key leaves first, then an entry no gate file still declares, then the least recently used or learned. Writes go through REG-2341's one writer. A push's first open (the prover's own process only, the machine's own memory only) folds main's and every live worktree's pre-R2 `tv/.heart2_red.json` in, newest `at` winning - those files are only read; old code keeps writing them.

GUARDS: tv/test_a_proof_remembers_where_it_went_red.py (7 new cases; 10 new RED_PROOFs: path back to HERE, idx back in the key, no legacy fallback, evict by learn time, a corrupt stamp raising inside the merge, dead entries not first, unreadable overwritten, worktrees not found, fold inside a law, fold into a fixture) - 14 of 14 PROVEN by heart2. tv/test_two_provers_never_tear_the_store.py drives the memory's two writers (REG-2341).

LEFT: the archived union of tonight's memories (outside every repo) is not ingested by code; once main's tv/.heart2_red.json holds what should carry, the first push folds it in.

### REG-2341 - THE VERDICT CACHE HAD ONE TMP NAME AND NO LOCK, WROTE OVER AN UNREADABLE FILE, AND ITS CAP WAS UNDONE BY ITS OWN MERGE (2026-10-21, prove-once R4)

Read in the v1 writer (main's cache measured 320,595,504 B on 2026-10-21): `flush()` wrote `path + ".tmp"` with no cross-process lock while a worktree pre-flight can run beside main's push; a merge-read failure (`_dwhy`) was ignored, so the write held this run's entries alone; `store()` trimmed to 4,000 by provedAt and the next merge re-added every trimmed entry, so the file only grew; every entry carried its whole inputs list.

FIX: one writer for heart2's two stores, `_StoreFile.commit`: an exclusive flock on the store's DIRECTORY across read-merge-write - on Windows, which has no flock, msvcrt's byte lock on ONE lock file in that directory (`.heart2_cache.lock`, shared by both stores as the flock is, polled for up to 300 s and then written unlocked and said; a machine with neither writes unlocked and says so) - a tmp named `<path>.<pid>.<thread>.tmp`, F_FULLFSYNC/fsync, the replaced file hard-linked to `.prev`, then os.replace and a directory fsync. An unreadable store is renamed `.unreadable-<ms>` (the newest kept) and `.prev` is merged in its place; at the open `.prev` stands in and the line says so. The v2 store lives in a NEW place old code never opens (`<git common dir>/heart2/.heart2_cache.json`, REG-2340), so an old-code flush can never strip or shrink it; it starts empty (every v1 key holds the old heart2.py's bytes). Entries keep `nInputs` and `inputsDigest`, never the list. The cap (50,000) runs AFTER the merge: unusable entries first, then a proof superseded by a newer proof of the same gate/proof/target/widths, then a gate no longer registered, then the least recently used (`usedAt`, stamped on every hit) or proved. An entry of a kind this byte-key reader cannot check (a traced kind, a facts table or reference) is a MISS, never served. A dead writer's tmp is swept when the cache opens. PUSH A1 INTEGRATION (T1's open review minor): beside the red memory too - it has no open of its own, so nothing swept a dead writer's `.heart2_red.json.<pid>.<thread>.tmp` or its `.tmp.prev` link in `<common>/heart2/`; now a process's first read of the memory (`_red_load`) sweeps it, once per process and memory file (`_StoreFile.sweep_once`).

GUARDS: NEW tv/test_two_provers_never_tear_the_store.py (5 cases - two REAL processes through a barrier under flock, and again with flock gone and msvcrt's lock in force (Windows' own there, modelled elsewhere); no lock at all; a dead writer's tmp (on Windows: nothing swept, REG-1725); an old-code flush - 8 RED_PROOFs, the flock and sweep ones `needs: posix` so a Windows census files them ELSEWHERE, never BLIND; 8 of 8 PROVEN, and 8 of 8 again with a stand-in msvcrt on PYTHONPATH driving the writer's Windows branch), NEW tv/test_an_unreadable_store_is_kept_not_overwritten.py (3 cases, 5 of 5 PROVEN), tv/test_a_proven_verdict_is_reused_only_on_identical_bytes.py (7 new cases, 8 new RED_PROOFs plus REG-2340's gitignore proof, 1 re-anchored; its unreadable-cache case now asks for the OPENER's line - the writer's own "UNREADABLE" line had masked that proof, measured BLIND then PROVEN; 27 of 27 PROVEN). PUSH A1 INTEGRATION: tv/test_two_provers_never_tear_the_store.py gains a 6th case (a dead writer's tmp and .prev link beside the RED MEMORY leave at the first read; this process's own stays) and a 9th RED_PROOF (`needs: posix`: the sweep call in _red_load removed - the case goes red, seen by hand in a sandbox before heart2 proved it). Two more catches on the merged tree, both things the hook or CI would have refused: T1's four laws printed non-ASCII without `console_safe.enable()` (the hook's encoding stage, `python3 tv/console_safe.py`, refused all four - now enabled at the top of each), and three new swallowed reads in heart2.py raised CI's swallow ratchet 66 -> 69 (`swallow_census.py --check`, RANK 1): the sweep's listdir and the pre-R2 fold's worktree listing now tell ABSENCE (nothing there: 0 / []) from a failure (the sweep answers None, the fold says it), and the kill watch's unreadable file (REG-2350) is said before the run is judged without it. The ratchet holds at 66.

LEFT: R6's census eviction needs a tombstone through this writer (a key popped in memory comes back from the disk merge, as it did before); R16's push record must merge its own section (unknown top-level sections are carried as they are). Hashing inside key_for still holds the cache lock. The Windows lock is driven on the Mac only modelled (flock on the descriptor standing in for msvcrt's byte lock, which binds its handle the same way); the same case runs the real msvcrt on a Windows PC, and none has run it yet. On Windows a reader holding a store open at the instant of a write (another process loading it) makes os.replace fail with a sharing violation, as in v1: the cache's write is said and retried at its next flush; a red learned in that instant is said and asked in full at the next push.

### REG-2364 - FROM A WORKTREE, HEART2'S SANDBOX HAD NO GIT HISTORY; LAWS READ HEAD THERE ONLY THROUGH THE GIT_DIR THE HOOK LEAKED (unversioned)

Found by the adversarial review of REG-2360, 2026-10-22. make_sandbox brings `../.git` into every sandbox (two gates declare it). From his main checkout `.git` is a directory and arrives as a private clone; from a linked worktree - where every push now starts - it is a one-line pointer into the real repo, and make_sandbox refuses to copy a pointer (a door), so the sandbox had no history at all. Nobody saw it: git exports GIT_DIR into a pre-push hook run from a worktree (MEASURED on git 2.50: GIT_DIR=<main>/.git/worktrees/<name>; from the main checkout, none), the hook passed it to heart2, and every git call a law made in the sandbox answered from - and could write - the real worktree through it. Once REG-2360 unset it, MEASURED on that branch: a sandbox from the worktree answered `git rev-parse HEAD` with "not a git repository"; test_control's TestV2153 relaunch case ERRORED (a red clean run refuses the push at --push); the version-stamp law's red-proof [7] went BLIND (its only catcher, RoutineIOnRealHistory, skips without history). FIX: heart2._share_history gives the sandbox a PRIVATE `git clone --shared --no-checkout` of that checkout: HEAD is the worktree's HEAD, the objects are borrowed read-only through alternates, the refs, index and config are the sandbox's own. make_sandbox uses it for a worktree's `.git` pointer on every platform (the pointer itself is still never copied); _bring_across's off-Mac branch for a `.git` directory now calls the same routine (one copy). Its git calls run with no GIT_* variable - MEASURED on a fixture worktree, the old routine's `read-tree HEAD` under a leaked GIT_DIR rewrote the REAL worktree's index (the staged entry gone), and a leaked GIT_WORK_TREE makes the clone refuse. The clone's origin IS the real checkout, so its push url points at a path that is no repository, and a history whose push cannot be shut is not kept. After the fix, a sandbox from this worktree answers HEAD = the worktree's HEAD, TestV2153 is 4/4 and the version-stamp law 32/32 with nothing skipped. SWEPT, not sampled: all 960 non-browser gates were run in the new worktree-shaped sandbox with every git call logged. 43 read the sandbox's history; those 43 and every gate that was not green (49 in all) give the same verdict and the same ran/skipped counts as in a sandbox shaped like the main checkout's. test_control, which heart2 classes as a browser gate, ran whole: 2272 OK, 21 skipped. The same 49 in the no-history shape show how far the blocker reached: test_a_ci_push_skips_the_mac_and_never_main goes red (2 cases); test_eye_declares_reach and test_no_footage_tracked skip every case, so every proof of theirs goes BLIND; test_a_stamp_is_not_a_blind_spot skips 3 more cases; and test_atomic_write_keeps_the_mode, test_live_version_is_not_the_working_tree and the version-stamp law skip one case each.

GUARD (registered in tv/run_gates.py): tv/test_a_worktree_sandbox_carries_its_own_history.py - drives make_sandbox on a fixture main repo + linked worktree (a staged entry in its index) under GIT_DIR=<the worktree's git dir>, with the registered gates' own `../.git` declarations: the sandbox reads the worktree's HEAD and an old commit through a git dir of its own; building it, then a commit, a push to origin and core.bare=true made inside it, leave the fixture repo identical (refs, objects, both HEADs, both indexes, the common config) and the push fails; a main checkout's sandbox still carries its history; and some registered gate still declares `../.git`, the premise TestV2153 and RoutineIOnRealHistory stand on. 4 RED proofs (no history for a pointer; the push door left open; the GIT_* scrub dropped; the pointer copied), heart2 4/4 PROVEN.

4. `d2r_copies` (extra copies, multi-copy / WAR overflow) is also a keep of both doors.

FIX: a third door, `window.vaultWipeItems` ("🧹 Wipe items (keep runes · gems · materials)", first of the reset buttons, asks a confirm that names what it clears and what stays). It clears through the same scope: assignments, witness rows, intake log, scan ledger, linked folder, owned, plus two new scope steps `magic` (d2r_magicFinds, in place) and `copies` (d2r_copies, in place). It rebuilds nothing. Its self-check watches every keep it does not itself clear (`_vKeepsFor`): runes / gems / materials, set pieces, runewords, the chronicle, tallies, unknown reads, copy targets and the roster. The two older doors are unchanged.

- After a hand add, the first sighting at a real cell did not fill FROM. `_vaultMoveWitness` saw neither FROM nor TO and set `moved-elsewhere`, so the MANUAL row became ELSEWHERE with no from-cell (ruling 4).
- An item seen on MAIN equipment got a move row (ruling 8).
- A row click opened the evidence panel. There was no BEFORE | AFTER view (ruling 12).

FIX:
1. `_vaultMovePackHome(home, bag)` reserves every saved target in that holder (its footprint, per grid) before first-fit, and keeps those cells. New items take the next free cell.
2. `_vaultMoveApplySight`: a manual `to-move` row with no FROM cell, or one last seen worn, takes the sighting as its FROM on the same row. The target and the row stay, and the frame becomes its proof.
3. `_vaultMoveWorn` (equipment or equipped) hides the row in `_vaultMoveShown`. Seen off the character, the row comes back routed from that cell.
4. `_vaultMoveCompareModel/Html/Open/Close`: the row click opens BEFORE | AFTER. Both sides are `gridHtml` at 36 px with real art, the same gold ring on the from-cell and the to-cell, and one arrow and one instruction line ("Move X from MANUAL to UNI-SMALL private stash (2,1)"). BEFORE shows the MANUAL badge until a frame sees the item, then the real container. AFTER shows every saved target in that container. Closing works by the button or the backdrop. The witness button still opens the evidence.

GUARD: tv/test_vault_l1_a_hand_add_routes_by_type.py, 14 RED_PROOF attacks, all PROVEN by heart2 --prove, Wilson 0.7847 against the vault.apply bar 0.722.

BASES (round 2): a white or eth base the builder catalogue names passes the hand door (`_vaultHandBase`). The packer and `_vaultRecords` add only `_vaultHandBasePool()`, which is owned bases whose receipt is the + Add an item hand door. `ownedPool` and the dock are unchanged, and a base owned through another door stays out (test_a_hand_typed_base_changes_no_other_list). Monarch, Archon Plate, Eth Thresher and Ethereal Archon Plate route to SOCKETED.
ALIASES (round 2): the hand door folds case and a leading "The" (`_vhAlias`), only when one ITEMS name matches. "Stone of Jordan" now resolves to "The Stone of Jordan".
LIVE REPORT (round 3, Elad on v3772): there is no add-a-move control (a guard fails on any button or input reading add a move or "Type an item, or select one", and on any input in the move list). FIND ON A MULE names a hand add's mule and its target cell ("MANUAL move"), not "unsorted · press Auto-assign". A hand-typed set piece that is thrown out only by DEFAULT (Arcanna's Sign) is his keep: the seam files it to SETS-REST, so it gets a MANUAL row and the organizer line stops advising throw-out. ### REG-2296 - A BUMP-ONLY RUN STILL TOOK 4750 s: REDS RERAN IN FULL, THE PROOF QUEUE DIRTIED 147 PROOFS, LISTINGS WERE NEVER STORED (v3775)

Measured on v3774 (7793ac8a): `--full` 4924 s, then a bump-only `--changed` (v3775 stamp, local commit f49305f2) 4750 s against a ~600 s target. 1014 gates carried, 497 ran (4606 s summed). The stamp lines were exactly the expected ones; the time went elsewhere:

1. 50 gates that failed in the `--full` baseline had no stored row (a FAIL was dropped), so all ran again: 2647 s, five of them to 120-300 s timeouts. The same 51 failed in both runs. FIX: a FAIL from a traced run is kept in the ledger's `reds` map, never in the PASS entries. On `--changed` a red gate whose inputs did not move prints `still red, carried, unchanged`, goes to the back of the queue and runs once under `RED_CAP` (45 s, `TV_RED_CAP`). A cap hit or a failure is a FAIL with that reason. A pass inside the cap is a real pass and is recorded; a red row is never carried green.
2. 147 passes (599 s) were refused as "proved on uncommitted tv/.self_arming.jsonl": the Wilson gates bank into that tracked file mid-run. FIX: while run_gates records proofs, `self_arming._bank_path` sends a default-queue row to a `TV_SELF_ARMING_DEFER` scratch file outside the checkout; run_gates folds the rows in after the last gate (`fold_deferred`) and removes the scratch file. A fixture that redirected the queue still writes where it pointed.
3. 80 gates (404 s) were refused because the gate file itself lists a directory, and 40 (229 s) because the run listed `tv/frames/hist`. FIX: every PASS is stored from a traced run, and the trace records each listing, so the static walk no longer refuses a listing law. A listed folder with no tracked file is keyed by a name/size/mtime snapshot of everything under it (`listing_snap`, at most 2000 entries); any difference or an unsnapshottable folder runs the gate.
4. 107 passing gates reran on the stamp. 22 of them only because their NAME held build|title|status|fresh. FIX: the name rule keeps version|stamp|bump|ship|resume. The script-word and reader-module rules are unchanged.
5. `sleep`, `ps` and `pgrep` children made a gate's reads UNKNOWN (pgrep 39 s, sleep 12 s). FIX: they read no file here (a pgrep pattern is matched, never opened). lsof on a path here, bash, sh, git history reads, chrome and the rest still untrace a gate.

GUARDS (each registered in tv/run_gates.py, heart2 --prove): tv/test_a_red_gate_is_never_carried_as_a_pass.py (13 RED proofs), tv/test_a_gate_run_does_not_dirty_the_proof_queue.py (11), tv/test_a_build_word_in_a_gate_name_is_not_a_version_read.py (11), tv/test_a_listing_is_keyed_by_what_the_trace_listed.py (10), tv/test_an_inert_child_does_not_untrace_a_gate.py (10). tv/test_a_gate_proven_on_these_bytes_is_carried.py follows the new listing and red rules (3 tests, 4 RED proofs retargeted, one footage proof moved to the listing guard).

REVIEW #248 (independent reviewer NO, fixed in v3775): B1 - a gate that raised mid-run skipped the fold, so the banked rows stayed in an unnamed scratch file and TV_SELF_ARMING_DEFER stayed set. FIX: the gate loop is in try/finally; `_fold_deferred_bank` clears the defer, folds, removes the scratch file, and if the fold fails prints the scratch path and keeps it. Guard tv/test_a_gate_crash_still_folds_the_banked_rows.py (10 RED proofs). B2 - a gate killed by its clock on a loaded box was stored red and capped at red_cap forever after. FIX: a timeout stores nothing (`led.record(g, False, trace=None)`), so the next --changed run gives it its full g.timeout; red_cap is never below the last measured runtime in gate_costs.json (the reader also had to read the `costs` level). Guard tv/test_a_timeout_is_never_stored_red.py (10 RED proofs). Minor: the push-proof scrub law now also requires `_queue` to be derived from GATES (new RED proof).

LEFT: git children (26 gates, 182 s) still untrace a gate. A gate that reads the version through `VERSION`, `"ver"` or a reader module still reruns on a bump (by design). The folded proof-queue rows still dirty tv/.self_arming.jsonl after the run, as before; they no longer do so while proofs are taken. CI never consults the ledger.

### REG-2295 - A VERSION BUMP RERAN NEARLY EVERY GATE (v3774)

Elad: release wall-clock is top priority. Under gate memory (REG-2293) a bump-only change was measured at 2172.2s with 154 carried, against 574.9s for no change. `bump_version.py` rewrites stamp lines in `bible.html` (D2R_BUILD, `<title>`, three d2r-build metas), `tv/control_app.py` (`"ver"`), `tv/tv_diablo.py` (`VERSION`) and `tv/WINDOWS_SHIP.json` (`ver`, `note`); `_regen_blueprint` and `_record_ship_in_tasks` then touch `BLUEPRINT.md` (generated time), `RESUME_HERE.md` (fp, version stamp, derived time) and the `TASKS.md` ship table. Those paths sit in most gates' closures, so `Ledger.lookup` saw every one as an input change.

1. `gate_ledger.STAMP_SURFACES` names one strict regex per stamp line (quoted values cannot hold an unescaped close quote, so no code or key rides on the line). `Ledger.stamp_only` runs `git diff -U0 --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-renames <proven sha> -- <path>` once per path and `stamp_file_versions` accepts a path only when every hunk swaps stamps in place: same hunk start, same line count, same kind, same indentation, and a `<title>` keeps its words. TASKS.md must gain exactly the single new top ship row in bump_version's format, with the previous row bound to a sha and otherwise byte-identical.
2. `coherent_bump` drops the stamp surfaces only when every required surface (bible.html, control_app.py, tv_diablo.py, WINDOWS_SHIP.json, RESUME_HERE.md, TASKS.md) moved, none was doubted, and all removed versions are one old version and all added ones one new version. A partial bump (one that died before RESUME_HERE was regenerated) or a hand edit of one stamp reruns every gate, as before.
3. A gate still reruns when its name says version/stamp/bump/ship/build/title/status/resume/fresh, when its own script names the version or a version-reader module (resume_state, RESUME_HERE, version_stamp_gate, stamp_versions, second_eye_ledger, tooltip_oracle_lane, windows_boot_check, _tree_version, _check_version_drift, current_version, _shipped_versions, bible_stamp, TASKS.md...), or when its closure holds a reader-only module (version_stamp_gate.py, windows_boot_check.py). resume_state / stamp_versions / second_eye_ledger / console_doctor are each in 619-633 closures through hub imports, so closure membership of those would rerun everything; the script test and the coherence rule cover them. The second look on PR #245 found test_the_resume_cannot_go_stale carried over a one-file hand bump; it now reruns on any bump.
4. Round 1 counted 760 -> 144 reruns before the round-2 content rule below; 90 unkeyable gates run either way.
5. ROUND 2/3 (second look on #245): the stamp lines carry FREE TEXT (build name, notes, the ship row), so a coherent bump carried test_no_new_home_path_is_published over a note naming a home directory. Now `tv/stamp_leak.leak_problem` (the home-path ratchet's own pattern, pinned equal by the guard; IP, hostname and token shapes, and `guest_profile._secrets`) is checked twice: `bump_version.py` refuses a leaking name or note before writing, and `Ledger.stamp_only` runs it on every ADDED stamp line and carries nothing if one fails or the check cannot load. So a note pasted into a stamp line by hand still reruns every gate, and a clean bump's only new bytes are proven clean, which is why content scanners may carry. `test_no_new_home_path_is_published` always reruns on a stamp move. Round 2's keyword always-rerun set (~200 gates) is gone.
6. ROUND 2: carried gates keep their proof sha, so the second bump in a row saw a TASKS hunk of three rows and reran everything. `_tasks_row_versions` now accepts N back-to-back bumps (up to 20): one `(this commit)` top row, N-1 shipped rows each in exact bump format, the proof's row bound to a sha and byte-identical, versions strictly rising to the top.
7. ROUND 3: `map_key` hashes BLUEPRINT.md with its one `generated <time>` line blanked. BLUEPRINT is generated from the code; that line is the only byte a bump moves and is not a fact about any gate. Every other byte still rekeys (a gate added or removed changes the gate list in the blueprint), so the input map is no longer rebuilt per bump (~35s).
8. ROUND 3 (second look on #245 at 56a862d): the leak check guarded leaks only, so the note "see bull-4-u.com/api/intake for the fix" carried test_guest_intake_door while the direct run failed ("named 3 time(s)"). Free text is content. Now, layered: (a) `stamp_leak.free_text_problem` admits only letters, digits, spaces and - , ( ) + #, a period only at a sentence end, at most 120 characters; `bump_version.py` refuses anything else, and `Ledger.stamp_only` extracts the NEW free text of every stamp line (build name and note, meta note, ship note, tv_diablo comment, new ship-row subjects) and carries nothing unless every field passes both the whitelist and `leak_problem`. (b) Literal-hit rerun: a string-count or forbidden-string test must hold the string it checks, so a gate reruns when any string literal of its own script (3+ chars; bare words as whole words, case-insensitive; phrases and punctuated strings as substrings, exact and case-insensitive; the words of literals handed to `re.*`) has a different count in the added stamp lines than in the removed ones. The removed side counts too: an old note leaving changes counts. A script that does not parse reruns. Plain word matching was measured first and rejected: "the" alone is in all 914 gate scripts. (c) Every bound ship row (the proof's row and each middle row) must name a commit in HEAD's history whose own TASKS.md holds that row as `(this commit)`, so a made-up row is refused. (d) `leak_problem` now also catches escaped and lowercase Windows paths, %2F- and &#47;-encoded /Users, /Users/name with no slash, /home/, /root, IPv6, .home.arpa/.localdomain, glpat-, AIza, 16+-char ghp_ and Bearer. The home-path RATCHET keeps its pattern (pinned equal by the guard): widening it was measured to raise the count in 20 tracked files, which only a human baseline rewrite may accept; `test_no_new_home_path_is_published` still passes unchanged.
9. COUNTED on real bump_version.py runs (CI-weighted s on the refreshed cost table), old vs new rule over the same diff. A typical bump between two whitelisted notes ("Click freeze hotfix" / "The console no longer freezes on a tab click (REG-2294)" after "Fast version bump" / "Stamp lines no longer invalidate gates, so a bump carries the gates that ignore the version"): 761 -> 215 reruns (1522 -> 588 s). The first bump after this lands, which removes v3772's long legacy prose note: 761 -> 419 (1522 -> 983 s). Two back-to-back bumps measured across that legacy note: 761 -> 422 (1522 -> 984 s). Round 3's 164 (391 s) carried content gates over unchecked text; the literal-hit rule costs about 51 gates on a typical note. 90 unkeyable gates run either way.

GUARD: tv/test_a_version_bump_carries_the_gates_that_ignore_the_version.py, registered in tv/run_gates.py. 43 tests, 46 RED proofs (heart2 --prove all PROVEN), Wilson 0.9229 against 0.722. gate_costs.json gains the guard's own row; the 51 CI-timed estimates from run 39248362022 reached main with v3773, so the rebase kept main's table.

LEFT: a version reader reached only through a hub import and not named by its gate is carried on a coherent bump (round 2 judged this safe). A gate that checks bible.html text through a string built at run time, or held only in an imported module rather than its own script, or that rules on file size, is carried over an inert note. CI never consults the ledger and runs everything. A real edit to a stamp file alongside a bump reruns every gate that reads any stamp file, as #243 did.

### REG-2294 - A VAULT PAINT WALKED THE WHOLE DOCUMENT, THE D2JSP LIST FROZE THE CONSOLE WINDOW, AND ADD A MOVE DID NOT ADD A ROW (v3773)

Since v3771 (69817adf) clicks inside a tab took seconds. The top tab bar still switched. Two causes, one per engine.

The first is in every browser. `_vaultRoomReadFloaters` ran `document.body.querySelectorAll('*')` plus `getComputedStyle` on every node, from every vault paint, from boot, and from the tab observer. Nodes hidden during the lower kept `z-index:20 !important` because the restore skipped `display:none`. The same build grew a typed ADD A MOVE control. An empty name returned quietly, a name with no target cell was filtered out, and there was no suggestion list. Elad's ruling: moves are not typed. AUTO INTAKE off means he adds an item and it reads MANUAL -> target cell. He ticks a row off by hand.

The second is only in his console window, which is WebKitGTK (pywebview). It paints CSS `filter: drop-shadow` in software. Every one of 228 D2JSP cards carried a drop-shadow on its art. Every price reading, sold toggle and typed fg repainted all 228 cards, and every Options click repainted the list under the picker. In WebKitGTK v3771 held the main thread 91-96% of the time and grew the web process past 3 GB. The kill guard took it at 3.3-3.7 GB. Typing never reached an input because the main thread never came back. Chrome does not show it.

1. The room sink names `#shortcut-hint` and `#control-dock`, caches them, and restores every element it lowered, including one hidden while lowered. It runs once per mode (on or off the Vault), which the code now says. A rewrite of the dock's inline z-index while the Vault stays open is not re-applied until the next tab change.
2. D2JSP card art has no filter in the D2JSP room. The glow is baked as a radial gradient per rarity (`--d2glow`). Each card is `content-visibility:auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size:auto 230px`.
3. `paintPrices(name)` repaints that card only: a finished reading, a sold toggle, a typed fg. listedNames dedupes names, so one name is one card, and the lookup stops at the first match. A refresh starting or ending is one full pass.
4. Options keeps the list. The picker host keeps its markup when it is unchanged and does not repaint the list. A filed pick repaints the list once. The D2JSP desk builds its 1,220-row builder list once per query (`_cbPickListHtml`). Other builder hosts build it fresh, as before.
5. The move panel has no typed add-a-move control. `+ Add an item` writes a row with `manual: true`, and the FROM cell shows a MANUAL badge until a sighting fills the real cell. A row still needs a known target cell; with none, no row is painted. The d2r_vaultHand migration no longer writes a move row per migrated item.
6. Focused inputs wear the gold outline, and it is `!important`, because `:is(#tab-funi,#tab-fsets) .tsrch-i{outline:0}` won over it on Sets and Uniques. The no-op `pointer-events` lines on hidden panels are gone. `body:not(.theatre-open) #theatre` stays. Click-to-paint is still published on the ui beat as `inputLatency`, and a missing number is UNKNOWN, not zero.

WHY THE WATCHERS MISSED IT. The heart rows score lanes, receipts, shelf, orphans and shadow, not the main thread. The v3771 gate ran the lift on a handful of fake elements, so the scan was O(1). Every browser check here is Chrome, and Chrome paints filters on the GPU. The v3773 first cut judged wall-clock p95, which a loaded box moves, and its parser read one 3.8 MB "function" because it did not skip comments or regexes.

MEASURED (box, 1440x900; v3771 then the fix).
- Counts per action, Chrome: getComputedStyle per vault switch or `renderVault` 28,486-39,674 then 0. Whole-document walks 1 then 0. Every other tab 0 on both.
- Chrome, 228 synthetic filings: filtered art outside a contained card in D2JSP 227 then 0. Vault 0 and Runewords 15 on both. Cards one reading touches 227 then 1. Cards an Options open touches 228 then 0.
- WebKitGTK, D2JSP phases, console app mode, 228 synthetic filings, guarded at 3 GB: D2JSP open blocked 96% then 13%. The guard killed v3771 at 3.3-3.7 GB before the price refresh or Options ever reported. On the fix, refresh 7%, Options 13% and 11% (sync 25 ms then 9 ms on the cached second open), and the web process grew 122 MB over idle.
- WebKitGTK per tab with his store copied to the box: see the PR body. The D2JSP rooms were the only ones over budget. Vault is about 18-21% blocked on both builds, with or without filters, so its cost is script, not paint.
- Uniques and Sets still carry 567 and 142 filtered art nodes outside a contained card. They are under the WebKit budget (9-13% blocked), so they are reported, not changed.
- FOLLOW-UP (not this build): Uniques 567, Sets 142 and crafts 5 still have uncontained filtered art (drop-shadow or blur outside a contained card). Counting every filter, Chrome reads Uniques 1,132, Sets 281 and crafts 14. The same no-filter and contained-card treatment should reach them before a longer list freezes those tabs in his window.

GUARDS, registered in tv/run_gates.py:
- tv/test_input_stays_responsive.py has ten behaviour attacks, Wilson 0.7225 against the vault.apply bar 0.722. Counts, not clocks: at most 20 getComputedStyle calls and 20 whole-document walks per tab switch and per vault repaint, in node on a 5,000-element fake page and in Chrome. A comment- and regex-aware parser covers `doc.querySelectorAll('*')`, `getElementsByTagName('*')` and TreeWalker. The TV-D step closes bible's `#tvz-theatre` with `window._tvdTheatre.close()` and checks with elementFromPoint. The Chrome half goes RED on v3771 by itself. Click p95 is a report only.
- tv/test_d2jsp_cards_stay_cheap.py has fourteen behaviour attacks, Wilson 0.7847. CSS rules are read, not grepped. Node runs the one-card reading, Options and the desk list. Chrome counts filtered art and touched cards in D2JSP, Vault and Runewords. Round 2 closed two false passes. The wrap needs `filter:none!important` too, or the global `.d2art-wrap{filter:saturate(1.1) contrast(1.05)}` comes back. Any `!important` filter other than none whose selector can reach card art is a hit, whatever its specificity. So is an inline filter in cardHtml, d2jspArt or artOr. Chrome counts every element that computes any filter other than `none`, not only drop-shadow or blur: 0 inside D2JSP cards (v3771: 454). Outside a contained card the budget is D2JSP 0, Vault 24 and Runewords 32. Runewords has 29 colour filters on v3771 and the fix alike. WebKitGTK runs under a 3 GB kill guard: at most 40% blocked per phase and 1 GB growth over idle. No Chrome or no WebKitGTK is a declared skip.

- test_03 race (local flake, not a Vault bug): drive() started before the boot's home-tab timeout (0 ms) and hash route (+250 ms) had run, so on a loaded box #tab-vault was briefly hidden while pick() looked. It now waits for readyState complete plus 1s (2/4 -> 4/4 under unshare -rn).
- FIND ON A MULE froze 12.9 s per key on his store (CDP profile: _provAll JSON.parse 29 s self over three keys, _vaultRecordsSource rebuilt per matched name). _provAll keeps its parse keyed on the raw string, one FIND pass shares one records answer, and the box paints the key first (140 ms pause). After: keys 13/3/2 ms, one FIND 30 ms. Guard: tv/test_vault_find_stays_cheap.py, 11 attacks.
- Round-4 review: typing in FIND ON A MULE then the x or Escape inside the 140 ms pause brought the old results back, because the pending _vaultFindSoon timer was never cancelled. Any direct vaultFind now cancels it, and the timer reads the live box when it fires. Guard: test_vault_find_stays_cheap.py now 13 attacks, 13/13 PROVEN, Wilson 0.772.
- The + Add an item box was a fixed inset:0 layer at z-index 130 with a dark scrim: it covered the tab bar and FIND ON A MULE and swallowed tab clicks. It now opens inline right under the find results, no scrim. The top search hover title (on .gsearch-wrap) sat on its first result row; removed, the placeholder says the same. Guard: tv/test_vault_hand_box_stays_inline.py, 10 attacks, 10/10 PROVEN, Wilson 0.722.
- Opening the vault took 1,106 ms and a hand add 848 ms on his store (CDP profile): findSetPiece spent 148 ms self re-norming all 135 set pieces per call. It keeps a normed index per set-table shape, first piece in table order still wins. After: vault open 925 ms, hand add 631 ms; the rest is layout of 957 cells and _vaultRecords (~200 ms), not cheap. Guard: tv/test_set_piece_lookup_stays_cheap.py, 10 attacks, 10/10 PROVEN, Wilson 0.722.
LEFT: the Vault tab in WebKitGTK with his store copied to the box still takes about 2.1s from click to paint (v3771: 2.75s). Its switch is 888ms of script (v3771: 1,612ms) and it is 21% blocked, under budget, so it is reported here and not fixed by this build. The Unsorted dock Frostwind click was not reproduced, so it is not proven fixed. His console was not touched. Uniques and Sets art filters stay, as above.
### REG-2293 - A PUSH RE-PROVED GATES WHOSE INPUTS HAD NOT MOVED (v3772)

A version was paying for about four full `run_gates` passes. Hashing every input of every gate, to decide whether it could be skipped, cost about as much as running it: on this machine a full execution was 9320s (943 passed, 46 failed) and the next run, with nothing intended to change, was 9066s.

v3772 stores, per gate, the commit a PASS was proved at. `--changed` carries that gate when the stored sha is an ancestor of HEAD and none of that gate's inputs are in `git diff --name-only <that sha>..HEAD` plus the dirty worktree. One diff is cached per distinct sha. A later PASS at a new HEAD does not drop the other gates. The input map is rebuilt for a gate when its script, any file in its closure, or `tv/heart2.py` is in the change set, and `map_key` hashes `tv/heart2.py` as well as `tv/run_gates.py` and `BLUEPRINT.md`. `run_gates.py` is not an input of every gate: the hashed Gate def covers a new registration, and a module the gate does not itself import is not walked. `bible.html` is an input when the gate opens it, or when a function the gate can reach opens it, including a callee in an imported module. A string constant in an imported module is not an open. A module that does not parse, and a relative import, keep `bible.html`. Both filters fail closed. A carry does not open the gate's files. v3771 took REG-2292 for the vault console face, so this entry is REG-2293.

Fail closed. A missing sha, a sha that is not an ancestor, a failed diff, a gate whose inputs cannot be named, a corrupt ledger, and a FAIL all run. Only a PASS is stored. `--record` stores a PASS only when `suite_verdict` already proved these bytes for `test_agent` or `test_control`. `--full` does not consult the ledger. GitHub CI does not either. CARRY is not a fresh pass and does not bank Wilson evidence.

`test_agent` is nameable: its directory listings are temp dirs. `test_control` stays unnameable. Its globs read `tv/*.py`, `tests/*.spec.ts`, `tv/*.sh`, `hooks/*`, and `tv/frames/hist/**/*.jpg`. That footage is gitignored, so a glob watch cannot see a new frame that changes pass versus skip. The hook never skips `test_control`.

v3771 added `_fleet_fetch_kick`, `_fleet_fetch_wait`, `_self_arming_kick` and `_self_arming_state_cached` in `control_app.py`. The call graph sees each one. `_self_arming_kick._run` calls `_self_arming_state`, which calls `self_arming.report`. That module opens no `bible.html`, so those four functions are not readers. `status_payload` calls `_self_arming_state_cached` and `_bible_ver`. `_bible_ver` opens `bible.html`, so the status payload stays a reader. `fleet_origin_status` calls the fetch helpers and `_app_ver`. `control_app` is not an import-time reader. `test_the_session_gets_a_vote_on_where`, `test_a_1440_tooltip_joins_the_panel` and `test_tooltip_read_failures` still keep `bible.html`, because they reach `_kai_fullnames` or `_kai_compile_register`. A method that stores an imported module on `self` or `cls` is followed too. `TheStatusPublishesIt.setUp` does `self.ca = ca` and `_published` calls `self.ca.status_payload()`, which reaches `_bible_ver`, so `test_the_beat_says_which_dossier_is_on_screen` keeps `bible.html`. Storing the module and never calling into it still carries. A module that escapes into code the walk cannot follow is a read of every reader in it: a local alias, an argument, a return value or a tuple. `hasattr`, `setattr`, `inspect.getsource` and `mock.patch.object` only inspect or patch it. `self.ca, self.n = ca, 1` is unpacked, and a subclass sees what its base stored on `self` in the same file. Round 5 (the round-4 look said DIFFERS: four ways to carry a gate that was red right now). The cause was one thing: a carry was checked against the inputs of TODAY's tree, named by a static walk that misses real reads. Now `run_gates` runs each gate with `tv/gate_trace/sitecustomize.py` armed (a python audit hook on open, listdir, scandir, glob, stat, import and every child process; `node_trace.cjs` does the same for node children), and the PASS stores what that run read: `inputs` (walk + opened + stat'ed), `listed`, `imports` and an `untracked` snapshot. (1) A deleted input is still an input: lookup checks stored ∪ today's walk, and `git diff --name-status --no-renames` gives deletions. (2) `record()` refuses a PASS when a dirty or untracked path is one of those inputs, so edit-prove-revert no longer files a red HEAD as proven. (3) A glob or listdir anywhere in the run is a `listed` directory, and an added or deleted file under it is a hit; `git ls-files` is a listing of the whole tracked set. (4) bible.html opened through `p = path or BIBLE`, a default arg, or a dispatched handler is an input because the run opened it. (5) `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`, so a file inside a new folder is dirty. A run the hook cannot follow is never stored and always runs: a child that is not python or node (chrome, bash, gh, a git command that reads history or the index), a child that did not trace itself, an ES module from the checkout, a read of a gitignored file (except the two key-validated caches test_cold_caches_invalidate pins), or a listing of a folder with no tracked file (tv/frames/hist). A row from before this change has no `traced` mark and runs once. A bare `gate_ledger.py --record` has no trace and stores nothing. Reviewer repros on ae6739a0: --carry rc=0 for all four; on this head rc=1 for all four.

sweep that took the slot in the lock gap is not wrongly declared hung and quarantined. Finding 3: `vault_sweep_start`

**2026-10-17 — THE ROOT DEADLINE WAS BUILT (fleet) AND BACKED OUT; it is harder than it looks. DO NOT re-ship a
simple per-reel deadline.** Recon (both lanes): the grouping hang is `isLoopOverFrames:True` — `still_runs(frames,
sig_of)` iterates ~150 frames, each sig_of BOUNDED (chron jpeg_sig ~0.08s; **vault tooltip-locate up to ~36 OCR
tiles × 4s ≈ 144s PER FRAME**). The built guard was a CUMULATIVE per-reel wall-clock bound (45s/90s) wrapped at
sig_of; an adversarial skeptic REFUTED it: a cumulative bound below a healthy large reel's grouping time
FALSE-KILLS healthy footage. And the deeper hazard the whole area carries: **skipping a slow-but-still-reading reel
DISCARDS his vault footage — the opposite of what he wants (his vault POPULATED). A deadline may fire ONLY on a
GENUINELY FROZEN grouping, never on one that is merely slow-but-progressing.** A correct deadline therefore needs
(1) progress instrumented at PER-OPERATION / per-TILE granularity (per-frame is too coarse — one legit frame is
≤~144s), (2) a NO-PROGRESS bound (not cumulative), (3) a budget set from MEASURED real per-operation costs, and

slow-but-progressing (must read → no safe speedup, skipping = footage loss)? ⚠ The shipped watchdog (v3758/v3759)
shares this blind spot: its progress sig (classified/pagesRead/runReelsDone) does NOT change DURING grouping, so a
reel whose grouping legitimately runs past 240s would be quarantined by the watchdog too — the per-operation
progress instrumentation would feed the watchdog as well, so it never quarantines a progressing reel. Backed-out
build diff (reusable chronicle note="deadline"/not-sealed + vault quarantine wiring, at the WRONG sig_of
granularity) saved at scratchpad/river_drain_build_REG2271_BACKED_OUT.diff.

**v3776 — THE FOOTAGE-SAFE PER-TILE DRAIN SHIPPED (the #399-owed root deadline, done right).** A per-reel NO-PROGRESS grouping deadline (`chronicle_retro.reel_deadline` — ONE helper, thin vault/chronicle callers, copy-drift) bounds ONLY the grouping phase and RESETS on every COMPLETED tile (vault) / frame (chronicle). So a reel that keeps completing units — however slowly, however far past 240s — is NEVER skipped (footage-safe BY CONSTRUCTION); only a genuinely frozen unit trips it, in ~budget seconds. VAULT: the poll fires from the per-TILE callback and raises `ReelDeadline`, a **BaseException** (NOT Exception) so it ESCAPES `still_runs`' `except Exception` and aborts a frozen frame MID-tile-loop; on a fire the lane HOLDS + QUARANTINEs the reel (the same `_VAULT_SWEEP_QUARANTINE` store the watchdog writes and the autoreel picker + the `vault_sweep_start` door both skip) and reads PAST it, so the sweep RETURNS and `running` clears via the done-path without the 240s wait. CHRONICLE: the per-frame poll returns note="deadline" and the seal loop SKIPS it (like "already-swept"), so the reel stays OWED — a frozen reel look-stamped "nothing here" would hide footage. Per-tile/frame progress is threaded UP to `_VAULT_JOB.groupTiles` / `_CHRON_JOB.groupFrames` and ADDED to the river watchdog's sig, now PHASE-SCOPED to grouping: a progressing grouping keeps the sig changing (never false-killed at 240s), while an UNINTERRUPTIBLE freeze (a lock with no timeout — no in-thread check can run) is still recovered out-of-thread within ~budget; `OcrWorker.read` bounds its lock ACQUIRE so a wedged holder cannot block a second read forever (closes the v3758/v3759 blind spot that the grouping sig did not move during grouping).

3 ADVERSARIAL ROUNDS refined it: (A) the CUMULATIVE-vs-no-progress refutation — a primed `_TOOLTIP_MEMO` (vault_scan_cost primes his whole corpus) makes every `_tip_of` a cache HIT that skips `locate()`, so the per-tile beat never fires; the cache-hit now beats and sig_of surfaces per-frame progress, or a primed HEALTHY reel would be false-killed (footage loss); (B) the single-frozen-frame case only the per-TILE BaseException can catch (the per-frame backstop has no next frame to fire on); (C) the phase-scope — the SAME stall must clear a GROUPING freeze at ~budget yet NOT touch a legitimately long paid READ.

PHASE 2). A single migrate on his FRESH (empty) board — the GrokBot verify — is UNAFFECTED (no prior store, no
rename, one persist), so the verify of count+location correctness is safe. **These must be closed BEFORE phase-2
arms repeated/trusted operation:**
1. **HIGH recId is NOT rename-stable (claim correction).** `_vaultRecordsRename` keeps recId, but the next
   `_vaultRecordsPersist` rebuilds priorIds keyed by the CURRENT derived name → a renamed name finds no prior ids →
   re-mints + the guarded set replaces the store (the rename is lost). ⚠ v3760's note/commit claimed "stable opaque
   recId surviving a rename" — that is TRUE for rename-alone, FALSE for rename-THEN-persist. The parity test tested
   rename WITHOUT a subsequent persist (the gap). recId is in truth POSITIONAL (name+position), not a physical-copy
   anchor.
2. **HIGH corrupt-guard gap:** a store that PARSES but is not `{records:array}` (`[]`, `{"v":1}`, `{"records":{}}`)
   is treated as ABSENT (not UNKNOWN) → overwritten AND the migration stamp latches (won't retry). Fix: `_vrRecLoadRaw`
   must treat parse-OK-but-wrong-shape as UNKNOWN (refuse), same as a throw. [[unknown-stays-unknown]]
3. **MED corrupt `d2r_vaultProv` → `prov:null` on every record** (absent and UNKNOWN collapsed). Carry an UNKNOWN
   marker when the witness store is unreadable, don't write null. [[unknown-stays-unknown]]
4. **MED positional recId reuse** shifts identity on copy-loss: name C `rec_1..rec_4`, first copy leaves → next
   persist writes `rec_1..rec_3` onto the survivors → a surviving copy wears a removed copy's id. Inherent to the
   count-only model — phase-2 needs a per-copy ANCHOR (not just name+position) to make recId a true physical-copy id.
5. **LOW `_vaultRecordsMigrateUndo`** always returns `undone:true` + swallows a `removeItem` throw → reports re-armed
   while the stamp still gates. Report honestly.
6. **NOT JUDGED:** classification parity of `_vaultRecords`'s kind/copyIx choice vs production `_sharedNames` (outside
   the eye's excerpt) — phase-2 must verify it.
The dormant store (v3760) stands; these are the trust-gate items the prove-before-trust phase exists to surface.
CLOSED in v3761, still dormant, still not armed: item 2 (wrong shape is UNKNOWN and is not overwritten, stamp does not latch; v3764 asserts all three named shapes [], {"v":1}, {"records":{}}), item 3 (unreadable d2r_vaultProv sets provUnknown and does not write prov:null), item 5 (undo reports undone:false when remove throws), item 1 for the measured case (rename writes prevName; the next persist of the live name reuses that recId). Re-verified green at the v3764 HEAD before the classification edit (tv/test_v3758_records_persist_parity.py, 10 tests).
CLOSED in v3764 (REG-2279), still dormant: item 6. A shared-locker name the never-muled regex misses is sharedStash (carried, loose and keep still win), the persisted loc is the rule-E copy split, and overflow membership is _sharedNames on both the live view and the loaded store. Measured before the fix: Enigma assign shared, muleById('shared') present, kind filed, mule shared.
LEFT OPEN — item 4. Measured at this HEAD on the dormant persist: name C held rec_3..rec_6, copies.C 4 to 3, the next persist wrote rec_3..rec_5. That is prefix reuse. It keeps those ids on the survivors only when the copy that left was the last one. copies[name] is a count, so which physical copy left is not in the source. The notes require a per-copy anchor and do not name it (cell, witness, frame, or an explicit drop). Choosing one would decide whose id survives. ### REG-2270 - RECORDS-FAILED ORPHAN COUNT RENDERED SILENT (FALSE-AGREE) INSTEAD OF UNKNOWN (#76, #231 eye on v3756, v3757)

Found by the Grok CLI second-eye on v3756 (run as the v3757 push prerequisite — v3756 shipped during the Grok
`--no-verify` week with no review). `_vaultPopHtml`'s orphan-agreement check was `if (p.orphans === null)`, catching
only the dock-unread case (null). Its SOLE caller — the vault header at `bible.html:42458` — passes
`orphans: (_rh76 ? _rh76.orphans : undefined)`, i.e. **`undefined` when `_vaultRecords` FAILS** (`_rh76` null).
`undefined !== null`, so a records FAILURE fell through to SILENT, which the convention reads as "they agree" —
a records failure rendering as a false agree. FIX: `== null` catches null AND undefined (both UNKNOWN); `0 == null`
stays false so `orphans:0` (measured agreement) stays silent. GUARD: `test_v3754_header_surfaces_orphans.py` — the
`absent`/undefined case now asserts agreement UNKNOWN and `zero` asserts silent; RED-proven by reverting to
`=== null` (undefined renders silent → the absent assertion goes red). [[unknown-stays-unknown]]

The other two v3756 findings, REPRODUCED and triaged: finding-2 (the `carriedUnkUnk` test's `UNKNOWN` assertion is
satisfied by the carried line) is a FALSE POSITIVE — `"agreement"` appears ONLY in the orphan line, so
`assertIn("agreement")` already locks it; finding-3 was the eye's own "NOT SHOWN / could not verify the producer",
not a defect.
