### REG-2268 - ORPHAN CORROBORATOR DROPPED WHEN CARRIED IS UNKNOWN (#76, review-after-ship on v3755, v3756)

The #231 cross-family eye on v3755 found a real Medium defect in INC-1 (v3754): in `_vaultPopHtml`, the
`p.carried === null` early return fired BEFORE the orphan lines, so when the mule map read (filed a number) but
the carried strip did not (`_carUnknown` true) and `_vaultRecordsHeader().orphans > 0`, the header showed a
confident filed count + "carried UNKNOWN" but NEVER the "unsorted and the mules disagree" line — the orphan was
silently dropped. The orphans derive from `_vaultRecordsHeader` (dock + mule map), independent of the carried
strip, so they must surface regardless of carried. FIX: moved the SINGLE orphan check ABOVE the carried-UNKNOWN
early return (right after the filed count), so it fires in EVERY path — no duplication (the two-line attempt
collided in the red-proof: the 4-space anchor was a substring of the 6-space one). GUARD:
tv/test_v3754_header_surfaces_orphans.py now carries the `carriedUnkOrph` / `carriedUnkUnk` cases, and the
single red-proof on the orphan line stays PROVEN. [[review-after-ship]] [[the-unjoined-end]]

### REG-2267 - PLANNER SWAP LEFT A PHANTOM EXTRA COPY (the #76 copy-inflation class, in the planner) (2026-10-16, v3753)

Surfaced by the v3753 push gate: `test_a_planner_pick_files_where_a_reel_of_it_would_go` was RED untampered
(`griefAfterSwap: 2 != 0` at :731). PRE-EXISTING — RED on the clean v3751 tree, and `#76` does not touch the
planner swap path, so not introduced by the set-piece work; it entered during the Grok `--no-verify` week and the
v3753 gate is the first gated push to catch it. The defect: `vaultPlannerFile`'s copy-undo at `bible.html:45716`
only fired on a same-id RE-ROLL (`_vpMade.id === entry.id`), so SWAPPING a planner slot's pick to a DIFFERENT
item (different id, same token) stranded the previous pick's extra copy — a `copies[]` count with no item behind
it, which is exactly the #76 defect class (drop copies with no real item). FIX: drop the `_vpMade.id === entry.id`
clause; a token changing its pick — re-roll OR swap — undoes the copy it contributed under the old name.
`_vpCopyUndo`'s REG-2240 name-check (`b.name !== name → return`) + the token-check still scope the undo to the
previous pick's own bump, so the "a later pick must not revert an earlier copy" protection is untouched. Traced
every token-reuse case in the guard (Alpha→Beta same-id: unchanged; Gamma→Delta diff-id: no matching bump, no-op;
Grief swap: the one behavioural change, 2→0). GUARD: the same test (now 26/26 green); baseline proven RED by
restoring the id-check (`griefAfterSwap 2 != 0`), GREEN with the fix.

### REG-2256 - SELF-UPDATE RELAUNCH OPENS MINIMIZED, DOES NOT STEAL FOCUS FROM HIS GAME (2026-10-16, his request, v3746)

His ask: a self-update relaunch should not alt-tab him off his game - "maybe it can open automatically minimized". The
machinery EXISTED (`TV_QUIET_RELAUNCH` crosses os.execv -> `_control_window_kwargs` -> `minimized=True, focus=False`,
wired for the shadow-reel relaunch), but `quiet_relaunch_reason` was only quiet when the console was tracked as
BACKGROUND (`_BACKGROUND["on"]`). While he plays, the console sits fullscreen BEHIND the game with background False, so
the self-update relaunch (`_drift_loop`) - and the rescue/green-light execs - opened fullscreen and pulled focus.
FIX (2 edits, control_app.py): `quiet_relaunch_reason(where=...)` is quiet for the 3 AUTOMATIC os.execv sites
(`_drift_loop`, `_exec_relaunch_now`, `_exec_relaunch_soon`) regardless of background; `_before_exec` passes its `where`.
`/api/relaunch` (the foreground button he clicks) + a fresh Desktop launch (no `where`) stay NORMAL/focused. REUSES the
existing TV_QUIET_RELAUNCH signal (no parallel env var - avoids copy-drift). CROSS-PLATFORM: the flag crosses os.execv on
both his Mac and Dean's Windows PC via the shared `_before_exec` choke (os.execv spawns a new pid on Windows -
win_relaunch.py handles that; the env still crosses).

HEART: RED-first `tv/test_v3746_relaunch_opens_minimized.py` (7 tests, registered in run_gates.py), RED on the current
tree (3-arg calls error on the 2-arg fn), GREEN on the patch. ⚠ macOS: a Cocoa window created minimized MAY still briefly
activate - GrokBot MUST verify live on his screen (and Dean's PC) that the auto-relaunch does not pull focus from D2R.

### REG-2240 - v3740/v3741 REVIEW-AFTER-SHIP: 6 VAULT & CONSOLE FIXES (2026-10-15, #108/#11/#134/#137/#14/#44, v3742)

Review-after-ship on v3740/v3741 (one cross-family look + the board retest cluster), six fixes shipped as v3742:

   quota/private throw — so a failed owned-write stranded the stray under a done-stamp. Now an in-memory
   `_vaultDedupeBusy` flag guards the re-render re-entrancy, the remove runs first, owned is re-persisted
   UNSWALLOWED to confirm, and only a confirmed remove stamps + folds.

   painted the placeholder; `_spareHtml` is now hoisted above the notes section and suppresses it (mirrors the
   v3739 shelf fix). The REG-2231 red-proof in `test_the_mule_inventory_takes_items_like_the_doll.py` is re-anchored.

### REG-2218 - #54 TOOLTIP-JOIN HARDENING: 3 CROSS-FAMILY FINDINGS (2026-10-15, #54, v3730)

Three real findings the v3725 cross-family (Grok) second-eye raised on the shipped #54 tooltip join, fixed:
1. **`area_floor` noise clamp ignored the actual sweep.** `tv/tooltip_find.py area_floor(w,h)` scaled the 8%
   floor by capture area but hard-wired the noise clamp to half a tile of the DEFAULT 6x6 sweep (0.5/36), so
   `locate(cols=4,rows=4)` on a small capture admitted a cluster smaller than half its own 4x4 tile. Fix: added
   `cols`/`rows` params; `noise = 0.5/(c*r)` uses the ACTUAL sweep (defaults to 6x6 when omitted).
2. **`_kai_compile_register` conflated a read FAILURE with "not on a panel" + re-OCR'd per row.** On a row with
   no tooltipRect it called `locate()` once per kai row, and `except Exception: return None` made an IO/reader
   failure indistinguishable from a measured not-located ([[unknown-stays-unknown]]). Fix (tv/control_app.py):
   `tooltip_find.LocateFailed` at the source + a `TooltipLocUnknown` sentinel (bool False so `if loc` still files
   nothing, but the TYPE separates failure from miss) that `_kai_stamp_tooltip_loc` skips; and a per-frame cache
   `_tip_by_frame` passed through `_kai_compile_register` so each frame is located ONCE, reused across its rows.
3. **`place_of` majority rule had no straddling-rect test.** A rect grazing past the midline is called wholly
   on the majority side (the documented contract — only an even split is None). Fix: documented it + added a
   straddling-rect case to the guard.
**Coded by Grok CLI; Claude eagle-eyed + verified:** 2 tooltip guards green, test_control OK (2286 tests),
diff reviewed (cache+sentinel wired). **Guards:** `tv/test_tooltip_find.py` + `tv/test_a_1440_tooltip_joins_the_panel.py`
(extended). Not specs, no routine_i_costs entry.

### REG-2216 - THE D2JSP ROOM RE-ASKED EVERY FILED NAME ON EVERY VISIT (2026-10-15, #107, v3728)

Opening the d2jsp room ran `refreshQuotes()` which asked d2jsp for EVERY filed name every time — even a
name whose public reading was already cached — because the quote cache `quoted{}` had no freshness notion
(`ask()` only skipped an in-flight `pending[name]`, and the planner-open path skipped only on `!quoted[name]`,
never on staleness). Each visit hammered the d2jsp lookup for prices it already had. **Fix (bible.html ~11417,
client-side only):** a named TTL `D2JSP_QUOTE_TTL_MS = 15 min`, `quoteFresh(name)` (cached object + numeric
`_ts` + within TTL), `ask()` gains a `force` arg and returns early when `!force && quoteFresh(name)`,
`finish()` stamps `quoted[name]._ts = Date.now()` on cache (quote SHAPE preserved — readers use `.fg` etc.),
and `refreshQuotes(force)` skips fresh names in its pump loop (with the all-skipped completion handled by a
new `quiet()` helper so `reading` never stays stuck). A forced refresh (`ask(name,done,true)` /
`refreshQuotes(true)`) still asks. The d2jsp DESK (cookie-decrypt + POST) is untouched — HIS-CALL.
**Coded by Grok CLI; Claude eagle-eyed + RED-proved the guard independently** (ran it on HEAD:bible.html ->
FAILED (failures=2); green on the fix). **Guard:** `tv/test_a_fresh_d2jsp_quote_is_not_asked_again.py`
(registered in run_gates.py; a source-shape test + a NODE behavioral test — second ask in TTL skipped, stale
re-asked). Not a spec, so no routine_i_costs entry needed.

### REG-2214 - A SHARE OVERRIDE WAS DROPPED FOR DASHED / PLANNER-LABEL ITEM NAMES (2026-10-15, gh#235, v3726)

The v3723 per-item share override (`_setShareOverride` → `d2r_vaultShareOverride`, keyed by `_keepName(name)`,
which straightens apostrophes only) was SILENTLY IGNORED by `suggestMule`'s two fold hops for any name that
folds: the byte fold (U+2013/U+2014/U+2212 → hyphen, ~40450) and the fuzzy/planner fold ("Harlequin Crest
(Shako)" → "Harlequin Crest", ~40469) each RECURSE on the inner spelling and RETURN before the outer name's
`_ov` is read (~40502). The inner call reads `_shareOverride(innerName)` — a different key — so the override
was not seen and the item took its default (high-trade/war → shared). Found by the #231 Grok monitor AND the
v3724 cold second-eye look (both named "the fold-key split"). **Fix (bible.html ~40391, engine only):** read
the OUTER name's override at the TOP of suggestMule and thread force-in/force-out through the hop via
`opts._shareForceIn`/`_shareForceOut`, so the recursion applies the outer name's setting; and HOIST the keeper
(`KEEP_IN_INVENTORY`) + standing-kit (`_FURNITURE_*`) checks above everything (`_keepHome`) so a keeper/charm
still wins over a force-in. `_shareDefault` stays override-free (no recursion). Preserves the byte-fold
Sunder-charm null=shared return + REG-2080 Unsorted exception + the REG-1913 planner "filed as" message.
**Coded by Grok CLI (coder seat); Claude eagle-eyed + CDP-verified RED/green independently** against the
shipped-v3725 bytes: planner-label force-mule after=uni-weap (fix) vs shared (bug); force-in after=shared (fix)
vs uni-armor (bug); Annihilus/Horadric Cube stay __keep both ways. **Guard:**
`tests/v3726_vault_share_override_folds.spec.ts` (5 cases, synchronous evaluates — no async-render race per
[[a-playwright-spec-races-an-async-rerender]]). [[the-unjoined-end]]

### REG-2213 - THE SHARED/WAR-STASH CHECKBOX HANDLER WAS DEAD ON THE LIVE SITE (2026-10-14, gh#235, v3725)

The REG-2212 panel rendered each row's checkbox with
`onchange="window.vaultShareToggle(' + JSON.stringify(r.n) + ', this.checked)"`. `JSON.stringify`
emits DOUBLE quotes, and they sat inside a DOUBLE-quoted HTML attribute — so the browser ended the
`onchange` value at the first `"` after `vaultShareToggle(`, leaving a truncated, dead call. The
checkbox drew, took a click, and did NOTHING: no override written, nothing re-homed. The feature he
asked for (uncheck War Traveler → mule it) was invisible-broken on the published page. **Why the
v3724 guard missed it:** `tests/v3724_vault_share_panel.spec.ts` called `w.vaultShareToggle(name,false)`
DIRECTLY — it exercised the function, never the rendered attribute, so a dead handler read as green.
**Fix (bible.html ~46731):** wrap the arg in the page's own `esc()` → `esc(JSON.stringify(r.n))`,
which entity-encodes the quotes to `&quot;` so they survive inside the double-quoted attribute and
the browser decodes them back to a valid call. Panel appearance is UNCHANGED (render_check
`vault-share-settings` still green). **New guard:** `tests/v3725_vault_share_checkbox_fires.spec.ts`
drives a REAL `.uncheck()` (a trusted change event, exactly the user's action) and asserts
`_shareOverride('War Traveler')==='mule'` and that the route leaves `shared`; it goes RED on the
pre-fix bytes (esc absent → truncated attribute → no call → no override). Seen RED/green via the CDP
harness (scratchpad/cdp_checkbox.py). [[a-law-goes-blind-without-being-edited]]

### REG-2212 - THE ADVANCED SHARED/WAR-STASH CHECKMARK PANEL (2026-10-14, gh#235, v3724)

His ask: "a list within the console like advanced setting for vault.. so i can checkmark what should
or should not be in the shared/war stash ... like war traveler.. eventually i dont want it there and
might mule it.. so if i uncheck it it can remove it from the shared and mule it." The v3723 ENGINE
(REG-2211) shipped the override store with no UI; this is the visible half. **New (bible.html):**
`renderShareSettings()` (a `#vault-share-settings` drawer under the REGISTERED unit) lists every OWNED
item the rules keep in the shared stash — war-gear (`warGearRole`) + high/vhigh (`_itemValue`) — each a
checkbox with its reason; keepers (`KEEP_IN_INVENTORY`) are never listed (they live on MAIN). A tick forces
it in; an untick writes `_setShareOverride(name,'mule')` and re-homes it to its slot mule via a his-click
`vaultFile` move. Collapsible, hidden when empty. **Two second-eye engine fixes rode along:** the two
suggestMule fold hops now pass `opts` (so `ignoreShareOverride` survives a folded name), and
`_setShareOverride` reports the ACTUAL effective route (a keeper "forced" to shared reports `mule`, not a
false `shared`). **Covered by:** render_check target `vault-share-settings` (green at 6 widths, 0
clipped/covered, looked at the PNG); guards `tests/v3724_vault_share_panel.spec.ts` (lists candidates,
excludes keepers + med items, untick→override) + `tests/v3723_vault_share_override.spec.ts` (the engine).
⚠ A different-FAMILY visual eye is OWED — Grok MCP vision was out of credits; GrokBot to look on the live
screen after publish. [[grok-second-eye]]

### REG-2211 - A PER-ITEM SHARED/WAR-STASH SWITCH THE RULES DO NOT OVERRIDE (2026-10-14, gh#235)

His ask: "a list within the console like advanced setting for vault.. so i can checkmark what should or
should not be in the shared/war stash ... like war traveler.. eventually i dont want it there and might
mule it.. so if i uncheck it it can remove it from the shared and mule it automatically". The war-gear
(`warGearRole`) and high/vhigh-trade (`_itemValue`) rules in `suggestMule` are the DEFAULT; before this
there was no way for him to keep ONE item out of (or into) the shared stash. **Fix (bible.html ~40460):**
a `d2r_vaultShareOverride` store with `_shareOverride(name)` → 'shared' | 'mule' | null, `_shareDefault(name)`
(the rules asked override-free via `suggestMule(name,{ignoreShareOverride:true})`, so it cannot recurse), and
`_setShareOverride(name,want)` which persists an override ONLY when it DIFFERS from the rule default — so
retuning the tiers still flows through to items he never touched. `suggestMule` gained `opts`; an early
`_ov==='shared'` forces the shared stash (keepers still win above it), and the war-gear and high/vhigh
branches gained `&& _ov !== 'mule'` so an unchecked item falls through to its normal mule. This ships the
ENGINE; the checkmark panel (gh#235, v3724) is the UI half. **Law:** `tests/v3723_vault_share_override.spec.ts`
(4 cases) pins the law through `_shareDefault` so it survives tier retuning. Seen RED via the CDP harness
(scratchpad/share_override_probe.py): with the `_ov !== 'mule'` gate removed, unchecking War Traveler leaves
it `shared`. Probe-verified: War Traveler default shared → uncheck → uni-armor; Andariel's Visage force → shared.

### REG-2209 - THE THEATRE T+ CLOCK JUMPED BY THE PRE-ROLL LENGTH AT THE RUN START (2026-10-14, #96)

`_clockSay` (tv/control_ui.html) floored a wall-time before the run start to T+0:00, but measured a wall
AT or after the start from the FILM ORIGIN (`relFrom = org`). When the film axis opens on a pre-roll
frame (origin < start), the clock read T+0:00.000 on the pre-roll frame and then JUMPED to T+0:10.000
the instant the run began (Session 175 ≈ T+0:09.7). Reproduced in node (origin = start − 10s): pre-roll
T+0:00, AT start T+0:10 (jump), start+5s T+0:15. The existing law was BLIND — every case used
origin==start, never the pre-roll scenario. **Fix (tv/control_ui.html):** T+ is measured from the RUN
START when one is known (`relFrom = (start > 0) ? start : ((org > 0) ? org : wall)`); the film origin is
the T+0 reference only when no start is known. After: pre-roll 0:00, AT start 0:00 (no jump), start+5s
0:05. **Law:** `test_the_clock_does_not_read_before_the_run_start.py::test_a_pre_roll_origin_does_not_jump_T_plus_at_the_start`
drives the shipped function with origin < start and asserts 0:00 at the start, 0:05 after. Seen RED by
the HEAD repro; the #96 red-proof reverts `relFrom` to the film origin and the jump returns.

### REG-2208 - A SHORT SHELF CLAMPED THE OPENED REEL CARD TO A SLIVER TO KEEP THE HIGHLIGHT ROW (2026-10-14, #98)

`_shOpenScroll` (tv/control_ui.html) scrolls an opened reel card into view and tries to keep the
highlight row visible. It clamped the scroll to `maxKeep`/`minKeep` whenever the card's TOP was merely
inside the viewport (`(top - keep) < ovH`) — which, on a SHORT shelf, left the reel card as a 4-89px
SLIVER to preserve the row. Reproduced in node at HEAD with the law's own furniture (card top 708,
highlight 197..371): ovH 660 → 149px (ok), but ovH 600 → 89px, 560 → 49px, 530 → 19px, 515 → 4px —
the REG-2175 sliver returned. **Fix (tv/control_ui.html):** keep the row only when the clamp still
leaves the card ≥ 104px (the shelf card's own minimum — `.shc-hero`'s `clamp(104px,13vh,140px)`, NOT the coincidental 104 in the v2772 lane-basis comment, a #231 catch) — `(top - keep) <= ovH - 104`;
otherwise the head scroll (which shows ~82% of the shelf) wins over a sliver. Measured after: ovH 660
unchanged (149px, row kept), 600/560/530/515 → 492/459/435/422px (card shown, no sliver). **Law:**
`tv/test_a_short_shelf_keeps_the_highlight_row.py::test_a_short_shelf_shows_the_card_not_a_sliver`
drives the real function in node at all four short ovH and asserts the card ≥ 104px. Seen RED: the
HEAD repro slivered every one; the #98 red-proof reverts the floor to `< ovH` and re-slivers. The
REG-2174 red-proof was re-anchored to the new line (an edit orphans other laws' red-proofs).

### REG-2207 - THE THREE KEEPER CHARMS SAT LOOSE IN THE DOCK, SO "DELETE UNSORTED" REMOVED THEM FROM OWNED (2026-10-14, #109 E#5)

Annihilus, Hellfire Torch and Gheed's Fortune route to `__keep` (suggestMule) — they only work in the
inventory of the character being played, so no mule holds them. But nothing writes them a stored
`__keep` assignment, so with `assign[n] == null` they fell into `_dockNames()` — the ONE list the dock
display, Auto-Sort AND "Delete unsorted" all read (bible.html:43740). "Delete unsorted" then passed them
to `vaultRemove`, stripping three grail keepers from `d2r_owned` on a single click (data loss). Reproduced
in headless Chrome: owning the three, `_vaultDockNames()` returned `[Annihilus, Gheed's Fortune, Hellfire
Torch]`, each `assign=None`, each `suggestMule=__keep`. REG-2191 made them DRAW as keepers (the "Don't mule"
advisory) but never kept them OUT of the loose dock — the-unjoined-end, a keeper recognised in one reader
and not the other. **Fix (bible.html, read-side, no store mutation):** `_dockNames()` now excludes any
`KEEP_IN_INVENTORY.test(_keepName(n))` name (the same identity rule REG-2191 established, apostrophe-folded),
and `renderVaultRegistered` counts such a name as `kept` rather than `loose` even without a stored `__keep`.
A keeper is handled by NAME, not by a filing. Measured after the fix: the dock is empty, all three excluded,
0 regressions. **Law:** `tests/v3721_keepers_stay_out_of_the_dock.spec.ts` — owns the three (curly Gheed's),
asserts each routes to `__keep` and NONE is in `_vaultDockNames()`. Seen RED by construction: the pre-fix
dock held all three.

### REG-2206 - A UNIQUE'S VAULT FOOTPRINT WAS GUESSED FROM ITS NAME, NOT ITS FIXED BASE (2026-10-14, GrokBot batch T #230)

GrokBot's live-board footprint audit of SHARED STASH + UNI-WEAPONS found ~12 owned uniques drawn at
the wrong grid size: The Oculus 2x2 (true 1x3), Bonehew 1x3 (2x4), Death Cleaver 2x4 (2x3),
Schaefer's Hammer 1x3 (2x3), Arioc's Needle 1x4 (2x4), Bartuc's 2x3 (1x3), Jade Talon 2x3 (1x3),
Titan's Revenge 1x2 (1x3), Warshrike 2x2 (1x2), Wizardspike 1x3 (1x2). `_itemCells` (bible.html:~20085)
resolved an owned unique that carries NO stored base by matching keywords in its name against a flat
size table, and the table is wrong for a dozen bases (e.g. Berserker Axe sat in the 2x4 two-hander
branch though it is 2x3). Reproduced in headless Chrome: every current value matched GrokBot's wrong
"app size" EXACTLY (deterministic, not a vision artifact). A unique's base is FIXED, so the game's own
footprint is authoritative — GrokBot's ACT: "build the size from the base item type, not per-item
guesses." **Fix (bible.html):** a tier before the runeword/keyword heuristics resolves the name to its
CB_DB record (`_cbDb().it`, exact name, `it[2]` 'u' or 's' only) and sizes it by `_cbFoot` of its base
(the game's invwidth x invheight). A RUNEWORD (`it[2]==='r'`) is EXCLUDED: its base varies, so it keeps
the stored-base path or the honest runeword-CLASS approx, never pinned to one base. Measured after the
fix: 10/10 of the mis-sized uniques now draw true D2; 0 regressions on the SAW uniques, the three named
charms, or the runewords (Grief stays an honest 1x2~ guess without a stored base). **Law:**
`tests/v3721_unique_footprint_from_base.spec.ts` — pins the mechanism (a unique's cells == its base's
`_cbFoot`), the ten true-D2 sizes, and the runeword exclusion (a baseless Grief stays `approx`). Seen
RED by construction: the pre-fix resolver returned every wrong value above. ⚠ One still open: Astreon's
Iron Ward resolves to 2x3 from its CB_DB base while GrokBot read 1x3 on screen — a base-DATA
disagreement (CB_DB base vs the game), flagged to #230, not a resolver-logic bug.
GrokBot batch U (71 more tiles) then listed 18 more mis-sizes: measured against the FIXED resolver,
13 of 18 are already corrected by this base-derived tier (same class). The rest are base-DATA
disputes, NOT resolver logic, and GrokBot's readings are self-inconsistent, so they are flagged not
applied: Stormshield (Monarch) resolves 2x3 — which batch T itself called correct (SAW 2x3) before
batch U called it 2x4; Kuko Shakaku (Cedar Bow) resolves 2x4 (bows are 2x4) vs GrokBot 2x3; Gerke's
(Pavise) resolves 2x3 vs GrokBot 2x4. The authority for a base's footprint is the game's own
invwidth x invheight (what `_cbFoot` reads), never a vision transcription (grok-second-eye: a
low-precision reporter of sizes). If a CB_DB base dim is genuinely wrong that is a data-extraction
fix, confirmed against the game, not GrokBot's say-so.

### REG-2205 - THE ROSTER STATIONS COUNT INCLUDED GONE REELS (2026-10-14, #99)

reels_read set counts.stations from the summed station_counts, built upstream from EVERY river
stamp — and a stamp survives the reel's deletion, so it counted reels no longer on the shelf
(measured 198 stamps against 67 live reels). It now counts a station only for a reel still on the
shelf it was handed (names), resolved through the same stamps map the rows use, and skips an
UNKNOWN stamp. [[stale-reading]] Law: `test_reels_stations_count_only_live_shelf_reels` (red-proof
counts over every stamp again, seen RED). Note: control_app._roster_reads still builds the now-unused
station_counts dict; a harmless dead computation to drop in a future control_app batch.

### REG-2204 - THE "BEACON CARRIES NO ITEM NAMES" LAW GREPPED A COMMENT (2026-10-14, #99)

`test_the_console_posts_roster_on_its_own_route` asserted the sentence "No item names ever cross
this boundary" was present in functions/api/console.js — but that is a `//` COMMENT on line 229, not
the code. The invariant is ENFORCED by the tally shaper: each count is `Number(p.have)` and a
non-number (an item name → NaN) is dropped by `if (!Number.isFinite(have) || have < 0) return null`,
so only have/total cross. The comment could stay while the shaping was torn out and the law would
pass (source-reading-guard §4b). Re-anchored to the coercion + the non-number drop; the `roster:`
absence check stays. Red-proof drops the non-number guard (a NaN would cross), seen RED. (#99's
other sub-items — stations count, _ROSTER_FAIL surface, KV cap, the 1.4MB parse — stay open.)

### REG-2203 - A SUPPRESSED CONSOLE FETCHED THE LIVE ROSTER EVERY 5 MIN (2026-10-14, #99)

`_roster_fetch_once` GET bull-4-u.com/api/roster with no `_beacon_suppressed_by()` guard, while its
sibling `_roster_publish_once` has always had one. So a CI runner, a test harness, or a scratch

### REG-2202 - A FLAKY PUSH GATE: THE BACKUP-LOOP DOCTOR CHECK WAS IN THE CHEAP SUBSET (2026-10-14, #124)

`_check_the_backup_loop_is_actually_WRITING` GETs /api/status, measured 11.6s COLD (0.26s warm),
and sat in the CHEAP doctor subset the eagle runs at every console boot and the push gate times. A
cold call hit ~15s and tripped the pathological ceiling (BUDGET_MS*5), flapping the gate. Moved to
PERIODIC — NOT SLOW: a backup loop that fails silently is the "backed up nothing for 18 days" scar,

_get timeout stays. Validated by the existing `test_the_cheap_subset_is_actually_CHEAP` (timing, by
its own design "pin the law not the membership") and `test_a_check_moved_to_SLOW_is_still_RUN_somewhere`
(the moved check still runs in the periodic tick) — both green. No new guard: the timing gate is the
law and it was red-proven in its own history (it caught `sweep would find` at 16,585 ms).

### REG-2201 - A FUTURE CHRONICLE TIMESTAMP READ AS FRESH, NOT UNKNOWN (2026-10-14, #99)

`_age_state` (roster_publish.py) and `_ago` scored `now_ms - as_of`, so a reading stamped AHEAD of
now (clock skew between PCs) went negative and read "current" / "under 1 min ago" instead of being
owned as unknown. A future clock beyond a minute of skew is now `unknown`; minor skew stays current;
stale and fresh are unchanged. [[stale-reading]] Law:
`test_a_roster_publish_stays_off_the_presence_beacon::test_a_future_timestamp_is_unknown_not_fresh`
(red-proof drops the future check, seen RED). The rest of #99 (stale-after-2h, _ROSTER_FAIL read

defects.

### REG-2200 - NO PC EVER PUBLISHED ITS CHRONICLE (2026-10-14, #94)

`roster_publish.chronicle_read` required `tally.get("ok") is True`, but a banked board_tally.json
(written by board_tally_merge, read via board_tally_load) carries the owner's sets/uniques/runewords
as `{have,total}` at the TOP LEVEL with no `ok` key — so chronicle_read returned None for every PC
and no chronicle count ever reached the roster. [[the-unjoined-end]] The gate now only REFUSES an
explicit `ok:False` (a failed read, which has no counts anyway); a tally with real counts and no
`ok` publishes. Verified: the real board_tally now yields sets/uniques/runewords, `{ok:False}` still
None, `{ok:True}` still works. Law: `test_a_banked_board_tally_without_ok_still_publishes`
(red-proof reverts to `ok is not True`, seen RED).

### REG-2199 - POST /api/roster-book HAD NO ORIGIN CHECK (2026-10-14, #116, security)

do_POST parses the body as JSON whatever the Content-Type, and `/api/roster-book` took it with no
origin gate while its d2jsp neighbours all call `console_may_post`. So a no-cors text/plain POST
from any tab in his browser could replace roster_book.json and publish his builds + stash cells
(mule names, x/y) under his name — and the roster Basic credential (app:DeanDiablo) sits in this
PUBLIC repo. The route now passes the SAME console_may_post gate (Origin / Host / Sec-Fetch-Site)
and 403s a cross-site request BEFORE `_roster_book_take`. Law:
`test_a_roster_publish_stays_off_the_presence_beacon` (test_the_roster_book_door_is_origin_gated +
a red-proof that drops the gate, seen RED).

### REG-2198 - THE SUNDER-TEXT LAW WAS BLIND ON ~9% OF bible.html (2026-10-14, #90)

`test_no_sunder_text_says_what_its_own_source_refutes` stripped tags with `re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ")`
over the WHOLE file, so every JS less-than swallowed to the next `>` — 436+ spans, 1.32M of
8.38M chars, incl. multi-line code like `< _probe.length; _i++) {`. A Sunder-refuting sentence
inside a swallowed span would never be matched, so the sweep went blind on ~9% of the page and
read clean regardless. The strip is now NAME-LED (`</?[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*\b[^<>]*>`): a tag holds
no `<`/`>`, so an inline tag like `<strong>` is still removed (a split phrase reads as text) while
`a < b` and `i<len` survive (572K stripped, no JS prose eaten). No hidden phrase was exposed — the
Sunder text is genuinely clean, it was just under-read. Law: the same law + a new guard
`test_the_sunder_tag_strip_is_name_led_not_whole_file` and a red-proof reverting the regex (RED).

### REG-2197 - THE SECOND-EYE DRAIN SWALLOWED A LOOK'S BODY INTO ITS model FIELD, SO 11 ROWS HAD NO FAMILY (2026-10-14, #182)

The #231 drain's `parse_comment` captured each `field: value` up to the next KNOWN field, DOTALL.
A monitor look writes `range:` and its body under `model:`, and `range` is not a known field, so
`model` swallowed the whole look — `grok-4.7\nrange: …\nCo-authored by Claude. …`. `family_of`
then saw a sentence naming TWO families (grok in the body, claude in the by-line) and returned
None by the anti-laundering rule, so 11 drained #231 rows carried `family: None` and `agreement()`
could not tell a cross-family corroboration from the same eye asked twice (the #182 hole). It was
ALREADY RED untampered in the prove sandbox and refused the v3720 push; hidden until now because
the Grok week shipped v3638→v3718 with `--no-verify`. Fix: single-VALUE fields
(version/sha/verdict/model) take ONE line, and a model id drops a trailing `(cross-family …)` note;

### REG-1550 - THE CHILD SUPERVISOR WOULD HAVE ENDED THE CONSOLE'S OWN LIVE WORKERS, AND FOUR MORE ROADS TO A KILL IT COULD NOT PROVE WAS OURS (2026-09-30)

**Found** verifying #83 (REG-1515) before it landed, by driving `child_guard.classify_unrecorded` - pure, it kills
nothing - over the REAL process table of his live Mac from the console's own point of view: the KAI closer's OCR
worker (`ocr_mac --worker`, a child of the console) and the console's warm chronicle reader (tv_diablo's pool runs
inside the console for chronicle/vault reads) both came back TO_END as 'unrecorded child of ours'. Both are
legitimately outside the door, and the same rule would have ended a reader the agent spawned 40 ms before a tick, its
ledger write not yet landed - at tick 3 (~30 s after boot) and every 5 min after. Four more roads, each driven: (1)
the table's births came from `ps -o lstart` / CIM CreationDate (local clocks) while the records hold sysctl /
GetProcessTimes - measured, `Sun Oct 25 01:30:00 2026` -> mktime 1792881000 against sysctl 1792884600 for a process
born in the repeated hour, so a live agent's recorded reader read as unrecorded and the agent as 'born after its
child', and both roads end in a kill; (2) a live parent whose birth could not be read NOW read as gone and its
children were ended; (3) a dead parent's child was ended on a birth match alone (Windows re-hands a pid within
seconds of a crash at start) and no kill re-asked the birth after a table read that takes seconds under D2R load;
(4) the OCR signature `--worker` is a substring of `--workers=3`; and `_stop_capture` still ran taskkill /T on a pid
read from the lease FILE with nothing showing it was a capture - a reused pid there is a stranger's tree.

**Fix (tv/child_guard.py, tv/control_app.py):** a LIVE parent's child is never the watchdog's to end - ours ->
`bypass` (said, counted by the census against that parent's ceiling, named on the doctor row), a stranger's ->
counted; the table's births are re-read through the records' own reader (`_same_reader`); a parent whose birth cannot
be read is UNKNOWN and reads as alive (`_parent_verdict`); a dead parent's child is ended only when the table shows
that pid running a known role's command carrying this checkout's path, born as recorded, and not now a live parent's
- an UNKNOWN table judges none of them and keeps the file; every kill re-asks the birth the instant before it fires
(`_verified_kill`: UNKNOWN or changed = kept and said); the OCR signature names the worker (`ocr_mac --worker` |
`ocr_win.ps1`, any-of elements); the stop kills a lease pid only when `_capture_rows` shows it as a capture of this
checkout (UNKNOWN kills nothing, says so, counts no survivor - the lease withdrawal still makes a real capture leave
by itself within ~2 s). The v2352 law in test_control follows the unified stop routine to its new address
(`_stop_worker_process` -> `child_guard.end` -> `_reap_later`), the v3427 way.

**Law:** `tv/test_child_guard_one_tree_per_role.py` +14 cases - `ALiveParentsChildIsNeverEnded` (the shape measured
on his Mac, through the real `_one_of_each_check`), `TheWatchdogNeverEndsOnAGuess` (7), the lease cases (4) - and
the builder's watchdog fixture re-aimed to the stronger standard (every endable pid has a readable birth and a table
row); 12 new red-proofs + 1 re-aimed, 41/41 PROVEN through heart2; `test_one_capture_per_console` 2 proofs
re-anchored, 19/19 PROVEN; swallow ratchet held at 69.

### REG-1551 - THE CENSUS GRADED CONSOLE + AGENT READERS AGAINST ONE CEILING, THE RECEIPT OWED PAID DEBTS, THE LEDGER WAS WALKED OUTSIDE ITS LOCK, AND AN IN-PLACE RELAUNCH FORGOT ITS OWN CHILDREN (2026-09-30)

**Found** verifying #83: (1) `census()` summed a family across every live parent against ONE ceiling - on his Mac the

agent warms its pool from reader threads) - a 'dictionary changed size during iteration' swallowed into a stale

### REG-1557 - A TOMBSTONE IS A RELEASE EVENT, NOT A GRAVE: THE RECORD TOOK THE FIRST ROW AND THE FILM HID THE PASSES (2026-09-30)

**Found** by the w26 skeptic driving the merged REG-1541 record over his real stores, read-only: **3 of the 29 reels
on his shelf carry tombstones - 14 rows between them, and every one of those rows carries a `kept` list** (the
frame-level drain releases frames and leaves the evidence stills in the folder); one reel alone carried **four** rows -
65, 14, 14, 14 stills before each pass, 13 kept every time - and **six** an hour later, the drain re-tombstoning it
on every pass. (The skeptic's own first write-up said "14 of 29 reels": the count was rows, not reels - the count is
the tell, and it was re-measured before it was written down here.) `ledger3._tombstone_of` returned the FIRST matching row and dropped the rest, and `_film`,
finding the folder still on the shelf, said "13 film still(s) on the shelf" as if nothing had ever been taken - the
release history he asked the ledger to keep (*"so when they get pruned they continue to exist on record"*) was in
the store and not in the record. reel_custody (REG-1544, the day before) had already carved the rule for this store:
*the LAST row wins the lookup (it is the latest act), and the count of rows per reel is kept beside it so a second
removal is never folded into the first* - two readers of one file with two rules is the drift copy-drift names.
**Fix** (`tv/ledger3.py`): `_tombstones_of` keeps every row in file order; `tombstone` is the latest act with
`releases {n, lastTs, released, kept}` beside it (`released` = Σ frames − len(kept) per pass, from
`reel_retention._tombstone`'s own meaning of `frames`: what the folder held before that pass); the film on the shelf
says "N release pass(es) took M frame(s); the drain kept K", a folder that is gone reads the last pass with the pass
count, and a pass whose frames nobody counted leaves `released` UNKNOWN - never a partial sum dressed as a total.
**Law:** `tv/test_a_session_says_what_it_yielded.py::TheRecordOverFixtureStores::test_a_reel_released_in_passes_keeps_every_pass_and_the_latest_act_wins`
- two passes with `kept` over the shelf reel, the same two over a released one, an uncounted pass, and no tombstone at
all. **Red-proofs, each seen RED by heart2 --prove:** the first row wins again · the shelf film hides the passes · an
uncounted pass is skipped and the rest summed.

### REG-1560 - THE TOOLTIP COMPOSITION HAD NO RUNTIME JOINT: THEIR PLANNER'S ROWS WERE COMPARED ONLY AT PUSH (2026-09-30)

**Found** by the #41 heart audit (rank 16, verified): the character builder's tooltip composition had no runtime
invariant and no doctor row. Its one independent engine - their planner's in-game tooltip, measured once on headless
Chrome and frozen as text (`tv/the_tooltip_oracle.json`: 203 rows over 6 runewords) - was compared only by
`test_the_tooltip_is_the_games_tooltip`, in node, at push time. A console could ship a composition that stopped being
theirs and nothing on the eagle would say so until the next push; `corroborate.BUILDERS` had no builder entry at all.

**Fix (tv/tooltip_oracle_lane.py + control_app, console_doctor, corroborate, auto_scope, loop_corroborate,
store_owners):** a roster lane **`tvd-tooltip-oracle`** (`_tooltip_oracle_loop`: a first look 60 s after boot, then
every 15 min; stamps its beat, leaves its lane trace, declares its scope - forbids delete - and is corroborated by
loop_corroborate) runs the SHIPPED composition (node over the bible.html on disk, through cb_node_harness) over every
oracle row and writes a **PER-ROW receipt**: `{runeword, base, agree, why, kinds}` for each row, the bible.html it
measured (`{id, size, mtimeNs, sha1}`), the node, the oracle's limit, and LIFETIME counters (runs, runsMeasured,
firstTs; an unreadable previous receipt carries them as None with `countersWhy`, never restarted at zero silently).
It re-measures only when bible.html's bytes moved or the receipt is 6 h old - one 0.3 s node run per ship, measured.
The doctor row **'their tooltip rows'** (CHECKS, WATCHES `_tooltip_oracle_loop`, MINE, COVERED_BY) reads the receipt,
never node: OK names the build, the age and the limit; MISSING names the row that is not theirs, or the row never
judged; UNKNOWN - never 0, never OK - for no receipt, `node absent` (a PC without node: the Windows box's node is
UNKNOWN today), a receipt whose sha1 is not the page on disk (stale-reading), a summary in place of rows, an oracle it
cannot read now. The corroborate joint **'their-tooltip-rows-are-ours'** (BUILDERS): left = their oracle rows counted
off the fixture file (never through the lane's reader, so a reader that drops a row cannot move both sides), right =
rows the FRESH receipt measured as ours, relation `==`; None on either side is UNKNOWN. The lane's contract speaks
on / worked / lastTs / owed (owed None when unknown). The gate `test_the_tooltip_is_the_games_tooltip` now drives the
same `measure()` / `judge()`, so the gate and the lane share one composition run. Measured on this Mac: 203 of 203
rows theirs on build v3525; the joint 203 == 203 AGREE and `prove_each` proven; the lane's first tick reads OK.

**THE LIMIT, said in every verdict:** their planner's 203 rows over SIX runewords (Breath of the Dying, Call to Arms,
Grief, Heart of the Oak, Insight, Spirit), one class, one level, measured once on 2026-09-26. A green here vouches for
those rows and nothing beyond them.

**Law:** `tv/test_their_tooltip_rows_are_ours.py` - 17 cases: 3 driving node over the real oracle (every row a verdict,

bridges (`_writeGrailFarm`, `_writeSetFarm`). `findRate` (runs/h x per-RUN chance) is the only rate a run sums;

find one"), with its assumptions on hover (runs/h, ~kills per run - estimates, printed, not hidden). The Sets hero

### REG-2192 - A BACKGROUND HEART PROOF STARVED A 0%-STUCK CHRONICLE SWEEP (2026-10-13, console)

**Found** on his live console: the chronicle sweep sat at 0% for 3:20+ ("river stuck · locks shut" on every
fleet row). NOT lock-blocked - it held a fresh .sweep.lock and the OCR worker was at 80%, so the reader was
WORKING but starved. `_self_prove_tick` had auto-started `heart2 --prove` (census stale, not playing - REG-1905's
"prove anyway under sustained busy"), and that proof's test workers pinned 95% CPU × 3 for 35 minutes while the
sweep waited for an idle window that never came. The self-prove is designed to run "below everything he does" and
yields to his GAME in 10 s (REG-1624), but a SWEEP - work he started and is watching - was not one of the things
it stood aside for.

**Fix (tv/control_app.py):** `_a_sweep_is_reading()` reads the LIVE `chronicle_sweep_state().get("running")`,
never the .sweep.lock file (a stale lock must not wedge the prover off, [[unknown-stays-unknown]]; a read that
raises reads as NOT sweeping, so a failure can only let the proof run). `_sp_yield_here()` is the play judge
widened: True when he is PLAYING or a sweep is READING. Both the self-prove tick (start gate) and the 10 s guard
now pass it, so a new proof does not start while a sweep reads and a running one yields within 10 s - the same
game-yield path, now covering the sweep. REG-1905's start-anyway under genuine non-sweep busy is untouched: a
sweep only DELAYS the proof; between sweeps it still proves. Status names the real reason, not "playing".

**Law:** `tv/test_control.py::TheSelfProveYieldsToASweep` (5) - a running sweep makes the judge yield; idle lets
it run; his game still yields; an unreadable sweep state never wedges the prover; both call sites pass the
widened judge. Seen RED two ways: neuter the sweep check → the sweep case fails; revert a call site → the
two-site count drops to 1. Takes effect on RELAUNCH (the console runs control_app from the working tree); does
not fix an already-stuck sweep - for that, drop baseline CPU (close the stray grok TTY, quit Battle.net).

### REG-2193 - A MAGIC/RARE VAULT CELL DREW A FLAT 2x1, IGNORING THE ITEM'S REAL FOOTPRINT (2026-10-13, #264)

### REG-2191 - A CURLY APOSTROPHE DREW GHEED’S FORTUNE NOWHERE WHILE FIND SAID IT STAYS WITH MAIN (2026-10-13, #264)

**Found** sweeping the mule / keeper logic for #264. The catalogue stores the name with a CURLY apostrophe -
`Gheed’s Fortune` (U+2019) - but `KEEP_IN_INVENTORY = /^(…|Gheed's Fortune)$/i` used a STRAIGHT quote, so it
matched its own canonical name NOWHERE: `_vaultKeeps` returned false, the item fell out of `ownedPool`, and it
was drawn on no mule and in no keep advisory - while `suggestMule`'s router (which also tested the raw name)
answered `__keep`, so FIND still said it “stays with your MAIN” about an item the vault drew nowhere. The two
keeper deciders disagreed by apostrophe variant - [[the-unjoined-end]], a keeper split in two - and a bare
`Gheeds` (the spelling in v3718's build note) failed the same way.

**Fix (bible.html):** one simple regex `/^(Annihilus|Hellfire Torch|Gheed'?s Fortune)$/i` (apostrophe optional)
and one `_keepName(n)` helper beside it that folds every apostrophe variant (U+2018/2019/02BC/00B4/0060) to a
straight `'` and trims. BOTH keeper deciders - the `suggestMule` router and `_vaultKeeps` - now test
`KEEP_IN_INVENTORY.test(_keepName(name))`, so a curly, a left-curly, a straight, a bare `Gheeds` and a padded
form answer the SAME at both sites, and a near-miss (`Gheed’s Fortuna`) still does not.

**Law:** `tv/test_a_hand_added_item_stays_his.py::test_a_curly_or_apostropheless_keeper_still_draws` - drives
`_vaultKeeps` in node over seven spellings, plus a source guard that BOTH deciders fold via `_keepName`
(count == 2). Seen RED two ways: strip the fold -> the curly case fails; un-join the router -> the two-site
count drops to 1. KEEP_A and the stale `.test(n)` assertion in the existing keeper law were updated to the
folded spelling (a new call breaks every harness that cut the caller).

### REG-2190 - SCRATCH CHROMES HELD HIS D2JSP SESSION AFTER A CRASHED CONSOLE (2026-10-13, security hygiene)

Each d2jsp read/post mkdtemps a d2jsp-quote-* / d2jsp-post-* profile and launches a headless Chrome
with his decrypted d2jsp cookies in it, cleaning both in the op's `finally`. A console killed mid-op
(kill -9, a relaunch, the stuck-sweep restart) never reaches that finally, so the Chrome keeps
running with his session and the profile stays in $TMPDIR, and nothing came back for them — up to a
few orphaned Chromes per crash, each holding his cookies and a DevTools port. Found by the
cross-family review of v3693-v3712. Each op now calls _sweep_stale_scratch() first: it removes any
d2jsp scratch profile older than 5 min (an in-flight one, seconds old, is never touched) and SIGKILLs
a Chrome still holding one — matched by its exact --user-data-dir, never by a name pattern, so his
real Chrome can never be a target (process-port-discipline). Law: a stale profile is swept and a
fresh one is kept, seen RED with the age gate removed.
Law: `test_the_d2jsp_desk_reads_a_price_before_it_posts` (test_the_cookie_header_is_only_the_d2jsp_host).

### REG-2189 - THE PRE-FLIGHT NEVER RAN THE LAWS THAT SCAN A CHANGED FILE (2026-10-13)

changed_gates() (heart2 --changed) returned gates_for_tests() alone — the laws whose own file is a
changed tv/test_*.py. laws_that_read(), written for exactly this, names the laws whose source SCANS
a changed file like bible.html or control_app.py, and nothing ever called it: run_gates mentioned
it only in a comment. So a push that changed only bible.html got an EMPTY pre-flight and every law
that scans the page ran for the first time on CI — the very thing REG-2148 said it had fixed, left
unjoined. Found by the cross-family review of v3638-v3653. changed_gates now returns
_gates_for_changed(all_changed), which merges gates_for_tests(changed tests) with
laws_that_read(changed non-tests). Measured: a bible.html change now pre-flights 216 scanning laws
(was 0). The law tested the function's output, never the pre-flight; it now also asserts
_gates_for_changed([bible.html]) carries every reader-law, seen RED with the merge removed.
Law: `test_a_law_that_reads_a_changed_file_is_in_the_preflight`.

### REG-2188 - A NO-ORIGIN GET REACHED THE D2JSP ROUTES ON HOST ALONE (2026-10-13, security)

console_may_post trusted a request with no Origin header as long as its Host was the console's.
A browser sends NO Origin on a cross-site <img>, iframe or window.open GET, but it DOES send the
target's Host — so any page he visited (always in Safari; in Chrome unless its local-network prompt
intervenes) could reach GET /api/d2jsp_login and /api/d2jsp_quote and make the console read the
Chrome Safe Storage keychain secret, copy and decrypt his cookies, start a scratch Chrome, and once
per process pull his real Chrome to the d2jsp login page. It could not read the reply, so nothing
leaked out, but every side effect fired. Found by the cross-family review of v3693-v3712. The fix
reads Sec-Fetch-Site, which the browser sets and the page cannot forge: a no-Origin request that is
explicitly cross-site or same-site is refused, while same-origin, none or an absent header still
passes, so the console's own request is never broken. POST was already safe (browsers always send
Origin on POST). The law pinned the old no-Origin-is-fine behaviour as correct; it now also asserts
a cross-site no-Origin request is refused, seen RED with the check removed.
Law: `test_the_d2jsp_desk_reads_a_price_before_it_posts` (test_the_cookie_header_is_only_the_d2jsp_host).

### REG-2187 - THE TENTH HEADER DOOR WRAPPED THE TAB STRIP (2026-10-13, console)

v3694 added the D2JSP door, making TEN header doors. Console-demos J10 had never run
across the Grok week (every push used --no-verify), so it went unseen: ten icon+word
tabs need ~1606px and wrapped to a second row at 1120 and 1200, and to three at 900.
v1614's ruling forbids the usual narrow-width fix — "the WORD is the tab, the picture is
the ornament ... No label is ever hidden at any width" — so the icons cannot be the ones
to stay while the word goes. Measured on an isolated console: the ornament now yields at
1280 instead of 1100, so ten WORD tabs (~604px) hold ONE row from 1000 up — the widths he
opens the console at. Below 1000 ten words no longer fit ~546px, and the strip wraps to a
SECOND row rather than hide a word (the v2093 safety net). J10 moves with the product: one
row required at >=1000, a second row allowed below, a third still a defect, and clip /
silent-scroll / offscreen forbidden at every width so a door can never vanish. The icon
yield assertion moves to >1280 to match. Verified: J10 red on the broken strip, green on
the fix; header looked at 1120 (one clean row) and 900 (two rows, every word present).
Gate: `tv/demo_console.mjs` J10 HEADER GEOMETRY.

### REG-2186 - A SHADOW VISIT WROTE INTO HIS OWN STORE (2026-10-13, #323)

Visiting another PC's console is meant to write nothing back into this PC. The
veil caught only ledger keys, while the board's own timers kept running and
wrote every other key straight into his real store. Every 45 s kaiChronicleSync
read the other PC's vault and trimmed his d2r_chronicleInbox, so a find he had
not ticked was gone for good. And _chronAutoAdopt stamped d2r_chronAdopted for
real while its foundLog went into the shadow copy that Leave throws away, so a
sweep that landed during a visit was marked done and never applied. Found by the
cross-family review of v3678 and reproduced in node. All three writers go
through window.LSR, so the fix is at that one door: while a visit is on, every
write and removal goes into the shadow map, whatever the key. Reads of a key
written during the visit come back from that map; a key it never wrote still
reads his own value. The old guard only grepped the veil's text and pinned a
count of 3, and stayed green with every write leaking. It is now a behavioral
law that runs the shipped veil in node and checks his store after Leave.
Law: `test_a_roster_publish_stays_off_the_presence_beacon` (AShadowVisitWritesNothingIntoThisPC, 4 cases, 2 red-proofs).

### REG-2185 - A PLANNER PICK WROTE OVER A RECORD HE ALREADY HAD (2026-10-13, #264)

Two writes in the Vault planner replaced a record that existed before the pick.
A magic, rare or crafted pick on a name already in Magic & Rare set the record
to { q, base, mods }, wiping its reel receipt (frameId, sessionId, at, shotFile),
its checker verdict and score, and his mods - a second "Small Charm of Vita" has
the same name, so it was easy to hit. And d2r_plannerMade holds one record per
name, so a second Grief on a Berserker Axe wrote over the first Grief's Phase
Blade, IAS and sockets. The reel intake refuses and the checker reconciles; only
the planner overwrote. Found by the cross-family review of v3683/v3685 and
reproduced in node. The older planner case picked the same item twice with the
same token (a re-roll of its own fresh pick) so it never met a pre-existing
record and stayed green over both. Now only a record this same pick made (he is
re-rolling it) is replaced; an existing record keeps everything and only gains a
field it lacks. A clear cannot reach it: a pick over an existing record is never
fresh, so _vpDrop leaves it alone. Storing every copy apart is still owed (art
and tooltips read by name).
Law: `test_a_hand_added_item_stays_his` (APlannerPickNeverOverwritesWhatHeHas, 2 cases, 2 red-proofs).

### REG-2184 - THE INTEGRITY FIX DELETED THE WRONG COPY OF A DOUBLE-FILED ITEM (2026-10-13, #264)

The vault audit's Fix for a "double-filed" row kept the mule filing and deleted
the Magic & Rare record (keep beats magic). For a magic, rare or crafted item
that record is its one home since v3716 and the only copy holding its base,
mods and checker verdict. The next audit then unfiled the leftover mule copy
as a guessed home and the next load dropped it from owned, so the item was
drawn nowhere. One "Fix all" did this to all nine of his double-filed rows.
Found by the cross-family review of v3713-v3718 and reproduced in node with the
shipped _vaultAudit and _vaultAuditApply. The fix decides by what the item is:
a catalogue item (unique or set piece) keeps its mule filing and the stray
Magic & Rare copy goes; a magic/rare/crafted item keeps its Magic & Rare
record and the mule filing goes through vaultUnassign, the door that refuses
a HARDENED row.
Law: `test_furniture_filed_in_a_mule_is_an_integrity_finding` (3 cases, 3 red-proofs).

### REG-2183 - THE WINDOWS INSTALLER COULD NEVER MOVE A CHANGED TREE (2026-10-13, #164)

Dean's PC sat on v3577, 1,063 behind, and the ALT on v3668, 105 behind, both
refused as "local tracked edits". The installer copies the update's
launcher_pull.py into %TEMP% and runs it there, and the rule asks self_prove
whether a changed file is the console's own record. From %TEMP% that import
failed, so every changed tree answered exit 1 "could not tell" and the
installer could never update it. Measured on the ALT over SSH. The installer
now extracts the update's self_prove.py into the same temp folder. When a
tree really has leftover edits (exit 2) - the ALT's was a draft of v3668 that
shipped later in another form - the installer lists them, saves every file
plus a patch and the old HEAD to ~/d2r_update_backups/<time>, asks Y/n, then
puts the copy on the update. Exit 1 still resets nothing. Gitignored stores
are never touched. Proven on the ALT: v3668 to v3718, 11 files saved, clean.
Law: `test_a_landed_update_is_not_an_edit` (TheInstallerRunsTheRuleBesideSelfProve).

call `_runSpanSay` or `_playSay`.

### REG-2150 - A LAW WROTE HIS VAULT LANE MEMORY (2026-10-10, #303)

`_vault_lane_note_outcome` saves the lane store at the end of every one-reel sweep.

### REG-2115 - THE UPDATE BAR'S WAIT LABEL WAS THE FIRST THING TO GIVE, AND THE RENDER GATE CALLED A 0px LABEL CLEAN (2026-10-09, #315)

His screenshot 2026-10-08 23:43: "not now - a read is in flight · waiting for it to fi…". Measured in headless Chrome at 1120:
the label "waiting for it to finish" needs 235px and was laid out at 0px, beside a 66px meter - and render_check's update-wait
target said "clipped 0/11" at all six widths, because its clip scan only judges a box that HAS a clientWidth; a label crushed
to nothing has none. Two layout causes: the reason beside it had flex-basis = its whole sentence, so the row's shrink fell on
the meter in proportion to that; and inside the meter Chrome sized it with the bar at its 54px floor but laid the bar out at
its 70px basis, taking the difference from the words (235 needed, 222.5 given, even when nothing shrank). Now the reason has
basis 0 (it takes what is left and wraps, with a 200px floor above 760px), the meter keeps its content width, the bar's basis
is its floor, and the label carries its text as a title like the reason does. Measured after: whole at 1440, 1120 and 800;
yields with an ellipsis (and a title) at 901, where the reason keeps its floor; RELAUNCH NOW on screen at every width.
Gate: a new render target update-wait-say makes the LABEL the subject at 1440 and 1120 with no title to excuse a cut - red on
the old CSS ("never matched a painted element": the 0px label), green after. Both update targets now hold the bar visible
against the page's own version check, which under load hid it mid-measure at 5 of 6 widths. OPEN, filed apart: the clip scan
still cannot see ANY text child crushed to zero width in any other target (#318).

### REG-2123 - A GATE'S PRIVATE CONSOLE SHARED HIS AGENT PORT AND CUT HIS ON AIR SESSIONS TEN TIMES IN ONE NIGHT (2026-10-09)

Found because the v3631 push refused twice on test_button_matrix "already red untampered" (STOP -> dark). Reproduced alone in a
sandbox, then narrowed: the law failed only under the prover's lane ports - it pinged a literal :17771 while the private
control_app it boots runs its agent on TV_PORT. Reading on showed the worse half: _boot_control made only the CONTROL port
private, so with no lane ports the private app's agent port fell through to :17771 - HIS live agent. Its OFF sent his agent
/shutdown ("closing session (off)") and its STOP SIGTERMed the port's listener ("signal:SIGTERM"). And inside a prover sandbox
copied from the main checkout, tv/control_agent.pid named his agent's pid, so the private app's STOP SIGTERMed it by pid even
on a lane port. His agent log, 2026-10-09: restarts at 02:04, 02:05 (gate shards; 02:00:19 was the console's own clock-hour rotation, like 01:00:19 and 03:00:19), 02:16, 02:20, 02:26 (the two push
pre-proves), 02:32-02:37 (four of my own reproduction runs - Claude's) - each a cut ON AIR session.
FIXED: the private app gets its own agent port (TV_PORT = a free port, like render_check / the headless law / roundtrip_sim
already did - the matrix was the one outlier of the four that boot control_app); the law pings the agentPort its app reports;
safe_copy never copies a .pid file (a file that names a live process on this machine is not source). Laws: the new
test_a_private_console_never_shares_his_ports calls the shipped _boot_control with Popen replaced and requires private ports
(a law that RAN the matrix could only fail by touching his agent); test_safe_copy's pid case; the matrix's own REG-2123 proof
(red in a prover lane). Proved after the fix: test_button_matrix[0] and [1] PROVEN in a lane, his agent restarted 0 times.
REG-2122 (doubling the matrix's waits under lanes) is WITHDRAWN and reverted - it was a timing diagnosis the measurement refuted.

### REG-2039 - A CHRONICLE SWEEP HELD A WAITING BUILD FOR HOURS (2026-10-08, #239)

MEASURED 2026-10-07 on his Mac's fleet row: "may false - a chronicle sweep is reading footage", the sweep at "5 of 293
frames - about 804 min left" (Grok reads timing out at 140 s) - every new build waited up to ~13 h, because the sweep
lock is released only when the run ends. Now the drift loop, with a build waiting and the relaunch blocked by a chronicle
sweep in this process, asks it to stop (a status read never does): at its next page the sweep banks that page and every
page since its last checkpoint, records the frames it read per reel with the prompt version (chron_autoread.json
"resume", through the one writer), seals nothing and ends - the finally releases the lock and the relaunch follows. The
reel's next pass is handed those frames and does not pay for them (chronicle_retro counts them as resumedFrames); the
seal counts them, so a resumed reel never seals as 0 pages; a record from another prompt version is ignored. For 30 min
after a stop no new sweep starts, so the next one cannot hold the relaunch again. NOT DONE: why Grok reads time out
(3546 errors on the Mac, 484 on the ALT) - still on #239.
Law: test_a_waiting_build_stops_the_sweep_at_a_banked_page (4 red-proofs).

### REG-2026 - TWO MORE EDGES OF THE EXCERPT CUTTER (2026-10-08, the #231 eye on v3615)

The v3615 look named two more ways `excerpt_blocks` cut the wrong Python lines. Both reproduced as failing cases before any code changed. (1) An INDENTED line of a module-level statement (`    limit=5,` inside `SETTINGS = dict(`, `    1,` inside `CONST = (`, the body of `if __name__ == "__main__":`, a blank line between two statements) was glued to the def above it, because REG-2018's module-level test looked only at the changed line's own column. The upward walk ran to the previous def, so the eye got that function's body (`'return 1' unexpectedly found in '--- lines 1-9 ---'`). Now an indented, blank or closing-bracket line is classed by its statement's first line (the nearest column-0 line of code above it), and a module-level line gets its whole statement plus the window, still bounded by the 400-line block cut. (2) A decorator written over several lines (`@app.route(\n    "/x",\n)`) with its hunk on the `@` line was excerpted alone (`'def f():' not found in '--- lines 4-6 ---'`), because the step past decorators skipped only lines that start with `@`. The cutter now steps through to the def/class line and past it, and the walk up crosses multi-line decorators. Measured old vs new on the real tree, one changed line at a time: module-level lines glued to a def went from 172 to 0 in console_doctor.py (every line), 106 to 0 in second_eye_run.py (every line) and 78 to 0 in control_app.py (every third line, 15,703 checked), and no line inside a def changed its excerpt in control_app.py. ### REG-2015 - WITH NO BUILD WAITING, REG-2014 ALSO SKIPPED THE CLEAR (2026-10-07, the #231 eye on v3612)

REG-2014 stopped the in-use clock unless a build waits by skipping every write to the hold - including the writes that END a streak. So if the drift flag read not-True for a poll while a hold was running (it reads None before its first measurement and after a failed one), the old `since` kept ageing, and the next waiting build met the ceiling at once and replaced the window under him. Now: no build waiting means no hold running, so the clock and the latch are CLEARED on that poll (the verdict still says he would be waited for); a still window clears them on any poll; only a waiting build starts the clock. Law `test_a_relaunch_waits_while_he_uses_the_window` (+1 case, +1 RED_PROOF, 9/9 PROVEN).

### REG-2012 - THREE HOLES THE #231 EYE FOUND IN REG-2010 (2026-10-07, the look on v3609)

1. **The 20-minute ceiling was not sticky.** Reaching it cleared the hold's start, so the next poll began a fresh 20 minutes - and the fleet beacon's `_relaunch_report` asks `drift_may_relaunch` too, so the beacon could consume the ceiling moment before the drift loop ever saw it. The ceiling now latches (`capped`) until his streak ends (the window still for 60 s, hidden, or its age unknown).

### REG-1993 - THE RENDER GATE'S FIXED 353 s STARVED EVERY PUSH MADE WHILE HE PLAYED (2026-10-07, his "raise the limit why not?")

The first v3603 push was refused at minute 6: the render did not finish in 353 s at load 8.0, because he was ON AIR over GeForceNOW and the console's OCR worker was at 69%. Every completed target was clean; it simply ran out of time. A fixed higher ceiling would be an absent hang detector on every quiet push. So the load measured when the render starts now scales all three coupled numbers by one factor (`tv/render_bound.py`): the hook's kill, render_check's `_CLEAN_RUN_COST` and its `_RUN_REPORT_BY`. The factor is load / 5 (5 being the daytime load the 317 / 333 / 353 numbers were measured at), never below 1 and capped at 2.5. At load 8 that is 565 / 507 / 533 s. The hook's literal stays the measured base, so the laws that read it are unchanged. `gate_run` widens by a caller-set `GATE_SCALE`, which the render call site exports with `TV_RENDER_SCALE` and unsets after. A render that really hangs is still killed, at a bound proportional to how busy the machine was. Law: test_the_render_bound_moves_with_the_load (5 cases incl. the hook's own gate_run widening run in bash; 5 RED_PROOFs, PROVEN). The cost he accepts by asking: a push made while he plays loads the machine his game streams on.

### REG-1992 - A LAW ALREADY RED UNTAMPERED WAS FOUND ONLY WHEN ITS TURN CAME, SO TWO PUSHES DIED LATE (2026-10-07, his "optimize the pushes")

The v3601 push was refused at minute 39 and the v3602 push at minute 80. Both times the law was already red untampered (v3602: a red that only showed on his Mac, REG-1953). That is the cheapest verdict the prover makes, one run per gate, but it was scheduled gate by gate among the expensive tampered runs. With more gates than lanes, the push now runs a CLEAN WAVE first: every gate's untampered run, across the lanes, exactly as its first proof in run order would ask it (same widths). A red stops the run before any tamper and refuses the push. The main pass reuses each green; `_prove_one` seeds it, bound to that pass's own sandbox, so the closing run asks it again there. A gate whose every proof the verdict cache would serve is not asked. With as many lanes as gates the wave is skipped, because each first clean run already starts at the first second. Law: test_a_red_law_refuses_before_any_tamper, which runs the real _prove_push with a red gate queued last and gets 0 tampered runs before the refusal. A green wave costs 2 clean runs per gate, the same as REG-1988 alone (3 RED_PROOFs, PROVEN; the first draft of [2] was an inert sabotage, because the lanes already refuse work once the wave has stopped, and it was replaced). test_a_proof_remembers_where_it_went_red[3] was re-anchored.

On his live data the same minute: 10,155 ms CPU, the reference at x1.81, so a budget of 16,330 ms; about 5,600 ms of fast-core work. ### REG-1989 - AT PUSH TIME A LANE PARKED BEHIND THE ONE BROWSER WHILE OTHER WORK WAITED (2026-10-07, measured on the v3602 push)

The v3602 push proved 131 gates in 4 lanes. 11 of them reach a browser through their imports and are proved one at a time under one lock (#42, after four Chrome lanes drove his Mac to load 100). ### REG-1933 - THE THEATRE OPENED A REEL BY ITS PLACE, AND THE DELETE DID TOO (2026-10-07, #223 / GrokBot tick 371-372)

GrokBot read three counts of "one" session that disagreed: S46's dossier FILM FRAMES 49 against the theatre's "film 64" opened from it, S74's card FILM FRAMES 0 against a theatre with "film 11 . 3 AI reads", the same on S30 and S48. What differs is which reel: `/api/session?n=` is a position in a newest-first list re-split from the journal on every call, and `replay.split_sessions` orders reels by their NEWEST row - so a session started between the shelf's fetch and the click, or a retro lane (kai, intake) writing a row onto an older reel, moves reels and `?n=46` answers with another one; nothing checked the sessionId that came back. (The Mac's own list has a Sep-8 reel at n=2 because 850 kai rows were appended to it later.) ⚠ GrokBot's theatre header showed S46's own date and span, but that header is drawn from the CARD's metadata, not the payload, so it cannot tell which reel actually loaded. `/api/session/delete` took the same `{n}`, so the same shift deleted the journal rows and frames of the reel below his. The page now sends the reel's id (`&sid=`, and `sid` in the delete), the server finds the reel by id in the journal as it is now, an id it no longer holds is refused (the delete says "nothing was deleted"), and a reel that comes back under another id is never painted. The mechanism on GrokBot's console is inferred from the code and the Mac measurement, not measured there - GrokBot re-checks after the ship. And because the other way two counts of one reel part is an index listing frames the disk no longer holds (the dossier counts the directory, the theatre counted the index), the theatre's film is now the indexed frames that are ON DISK, one listing per request, and `stats.indexMissing` counts what fell out. ⚠⚠ AND THE LIKELIEST CAUSE OF S46'S 49 WAS NEITHER: GrokBot's next two ticks (377, 378) watched dossier numbers CLIMB on finished reels - S41 0 -> 6 -> 8 (its card says 8), S175 60 -> 63 -> 61, S53 105 / 106, S74 0/0/0/0 then 3/11/1. The dossier's D20 count-up wrote every in-between value on requestAnimationFrame ('the truth is never altered' - only the last frame was true), and on his busy machine those frames sat on screen for seconds, so 49 was most likely a tile part-way to 64. The number is now written once and only its opacity moves (prefers-reduced-motion: no motion); swept to its one twin, the TV.D READS meter, which eased between counts the same way and now snaps and bumps. Law `test_a_reel_opens_by_its_id` (13 cases, 8 RED_PROOFs, all PROVEN).

### REG-1892 - AN ORDER LAW ON str.find() PASSED WITH ITS SUBJECT GONE (10 sites, swept) (2026-10-07, #184)

REG-1827 closed 2 sites; the class was wider. assertLess(a, b) / assertGreater(b, a) on find() results passes VACUOUSLY when the smaller side's needle is absent, because find() returns -1 and -1 is less than every index. A census of tv/test_*.py on 873e591b found 150 candidates; every one was read. 140 were already safe (a presence check on the same index, count == N, an assertIn on the needle, a chained order, a refusal written as `b < a`, a hi-search from the missing index that also returns -1). 10 were real and are fixed by asserting the smaller side present first: test_a_landed_update_is_not_an_edit (Mac launcher + fleet_pull + _pull_once record HEAD), test_control (board script defines _n), test_frames_respect_evidence_holds (frame_verdict slice; its assertNotIn passed on ""), test_quit_leaves_the_shadow_reader_running (_WINDOW_ONLY), test_the_engine_room_lives_on_tvd (.rail-secondary, 2 orders), test_the_fleet_card_says_how_each_pc_films_and_drains (</details>), test_the_gate_never_adopts_a_browser_it_did_not_start (export TV_RENDER_PORT), test_the_verdict_reaches_the_card (var _lvRows). Proven by sabotage in a safe_copy tree: 9 cases in 8 files, each needle deleted - the pre-fix law PASSED, the fixed law FAILS. Sibling shapes (tuple-unpacked finds, self.attr finds, find()+k, sorted()-order, find vs a constant/.index()) were scanned too: 16 hits, all safe. Test code only; pushed as ci/find-order-sweep through the ci/* lane (REG-1841).

Law `TheTwoPublicScrubsAgree` (test_a_landed_update_is_not_an_edit) feeds both the same cases and requires equal output with no name left; seen RED by narrowing the Python drive regex to backslash only.

### REG-1831 - THE PAGE-NEWER BANNER NAMED A DIRECTION IT NEVER ORDERED (2026-10-06, #231 look at v3579)

`_pageNewerSay` said "this window is newer than the console behind it" for ANY difference between the running stamp and the stamp on disk, so a console process AHEAD of its page got the same sentence as a page ahead of its process. It now orders the two versions numerically (v9 below v10): console behind disk keeps the banner, console ahead says it is ahead, an unparseable stamp says UNKNOWN, equal says nothing. Law `test_a_window_that_fails_says_why`.

### REG-1830 - A QUIT'S KEEP-SERVICE FLAG LET A LATER WINDOW'S X DESTROY THE VIEW (2026-10-06, #231 look at v3579)

`_quit_window_keeps_service` sets `_QUIT_KEEPS_SERVICE` and rightly leaves it set after a successful destroy, because the park loop and the background mode read it. `_on_console_window_closing` answered True whenever that flag was set and no exit was asked, before `close_means_background`. So a window the park loop reopened in the same process had its X destroy the view instead of hiding it. The quit now records the window it destroyed (`_QUIT_KEEPS_WINDOW`). The close is let through on the flag only while no other window is up. A window that is not the quit's goes the normal ✕ route. Law `test_a_later_close_of_a_new_window_still_hides`.

### REG-1710 - PUSHES WENT FROM 17 MINUTES TO 100+: EVERY test_control SABOTAGE RE-RAN ALL 2,259 CASES (#42, 2026-10-02)

His question: "all these pushs are so long taking hours each ... we had pushes that were 17 minutes average. now they
are each an hour plus the last couple days. is it because they are big?" **Measured from the push log:** not the size.
The 17-20 minute pushes (04518e05, bcfc1328) proved in 5-9 minutes and never touched tv/test_control.py; every v3550+
batch did, and a changed law must prove each sabotage - test_control's 6, plus a clean run, each a FULL run of 2,259
cases (8-14 min), not cacheable (it lists a directory at run time). 99-101 minutes of proofs per push, then serial lanes
(#144) and four refusals each re-paid it. **Built - the red memory:** at push time, a tampered run that goes red writes
down which cases failed (tv/.heart2_red.json, per machine, gitignored); the next push asks only those cases - untampered
first (must be green), tampered second (must be red). Only that pair is PROVEN; any other outcome (a renamed case, a
subset that stays green, a run that cannot finish) falls back to the full proof unchanged, so the memory can only save

### REG-1677 - A REUSED CLEAN RUN COULD BANK A FALSE BLIND (the v3543 cross-family eye, 2026-10-01)

**Found by** the Grok seat on v3543 (third ask; two `cannot-tell` before it). **Was:** REG-1669 let a gate's later proofs
reuse the first proof's green clean run. If an earlier proof's run left the sandbox changed, a later proof judged on the
cached green could miss its anchor (INVALID) or stay green tampered (BLIND) where its own fresh clean run would have gone
red first (UNPROVABLE). The closing clean run only downgraded PROVEN, and was skipped altogether when nothing was PROVEN
- so a drifted sandbox could bank BLIND/INVALID, which the census files as blind, and one blind record shuts every lock
on that PC (the river). And the closing run sat outside the per-proof handler: a raise there wrote the whole gate BLIND
and unmeasured. **Now** the closing run is asked whenever a reused verdict could be banked (PROVEN, BLIND or INVALID); a
red, unknown or raising closing run makes PROVEN and every REUSED BLIND/INVALID UNPROVABLE, while a first proof's BLIND
- judged on its own fresh clean run - stands. Law: `tv/test_one_clean_run_serves_a_gates_proofs.py`
(AReusedCleanRunNeverBanksAFalseBlind, the finding's scenarios driven through the real `_prove_gate`); 3 new red-proofs,
one re-anchored; all 6 PROVEN.

### REG-1656 - A RE-TICK'S REDO PUT BACK PART OF WHAT IT TOOK AND SAID NOTHING ABOUT THE REST (#125, the #231 seat, 2026-10-01)

**Was:** REG-1638's redo (`_tickRedoRestore`) returned what it put back - and its one caller, `toggleOwned`, threw the
result away. So when the vault part could not be undone ("another removal came after the un-tick - put it back from
the vault removal list") nobody ever read the sentence: the date came back, the vault entry did not, and the board
looked whole. A door missing from the page read exactly like a refusal - with no vault door the redo even said
"another removal came after the un-tick", a reason nothing had measured. And the game-date door merges with the OLD
value winning, so a redo would have written its date over one a later read stored inside the window (the evidence
door already refused to; the two disagreed).

**Now:** the redo lists every owed part that did not come back with its OWN reason - its door is not on this page /
its store would not parse / a later read wrote one - kept / its store refused it / another removal came after the
un-tick - and never writes over a game date a later read wrote. The caller keeps the result and notes it on the
last-tick marker of THAT item only (a full redo clears it); the last-found bar - where he looks after a tick, since the
toast is motion-gated - says "re-ticked inside the misclick window - not put back: ..." until the next tick replaces
the marker. Law: `tv/test_an_untick_then_a_retick_is_one_misclick.py` - the redo, the note and the bar's helper driven
in node on the page code; the handler's join (restore, then note) and the bar's join read from their code in order.

### REG-1658 - TWO RETIREMENTS JUDGED BY A BLIND INSTRUMENT WOULD NEVER BE LOOKED AT AGAIN (#126, 2026-10-01)

**Was:** his two retired reels (…66296, …82142) said "no attempt left a reason, so WHY is UNKNOWN": both were judged
before a sweep could tell the lane why it did not seal (REG-1649), on frames where the cross-check could not see a
grid (REG-1648). Nothing revisits a retirement except the boot re-entry, and that only re-admits a reel still holding
UNEXTRACTED panels - so a retirement made by a broken instrument stood for ever.

**Now:** `vault_reentry_sweep` re-judges a retirement made blind (`lastWhy` None and "no attempt left a reason") ONCE:
it leaves the retired list with `tries = MAX - 1`, exactly one attempt. A failure retires again WITH its reason
(REG-1649 writes one on every exit path), so it is never blind again and never re-judged again; a success seals. At
most `_VAULT_REJUDGE_PER_BOOT` (3) per boot - the ALT's count could not be read (SSH timed out), so one relaunch must
not buy a backlog. A retirement that carries its reason stays retired. The boot prints "[vault] re-judging N
retirement(s) made without a reason - one attempt each: ...". Cost, stated: one sweep per re-judged reel, once (the
last ones ran ~30 panel reads each). Law: `tv/test_the_durable_set_is_loaded_before_it_is_asked.py` gains the cases
(blind -> one attempt; reasoned -> kept; five blind -> three). 3 new red-proofs RED.

### REG-1657 - A STASH READ WAS CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST THE BAG BESIDE IT (#126, 2026-10-01)

**Was:** the vault's free cross-check compares the names a read returned with the occupied cells the lattice
counted - and the lattice counts the INVENTORY, while the vault reads stash panels. MEASURED 2026-10-01 across every surveyed
reel on his Mac, panel kinds read: stash 2002 · shared 407 · personal 121 · materials 41 · runes 12 · gems 4 ·
inventory 0. Every comparison was between two panels. With the lattice working again (REG-1648), reel …82142 - an
EMPTY bag beside a stash tooltip naming one real item - would have filed "the read named 1 item(s) but only 0
square(s) are filled, so at least one name did not come from this picture": a fabrication claim about a correct read.

**Now:** `cross_panel_verdict` - an over-read on any panel but the inventory (or one nobody can tell) is
"other-panel": never filed as an over-read, said in its own words ("N frame(s) named items on a panel the pixel layer
does not count (stash) - the cross-check cannot speak for them"), and never settled - `vault_seal_is_definitive`
admits only under-read and agree, so no seal loosens and the footage stays readable. An inventory over-read stays an
over-read. The sweep asks it once, after `reconcile_verdict` and before the over-read list.
**NOT fixed, stated:** agree and under-read on a stash read still compare against the bag's count. They cannot accuse
(the read named no more than the bag holds), but they are not a cross-check of the stash either, and they can settle
a session that grounded no rows. A real one needs the stash's own grid counted - a design question, not made here.
Law: `tv/test_a_stash_read_is_never_called_a_fabrication.py`. 4 red-proofs RED.

### REG-1641 - ASKING HIS CONSOLE FOR ITS STACKS KILLED IT (2026-10-01)

handler restores the signal's PREVIOUS action and re-raises it, and SIGUSR1's previous action is the default one,
which TERMINATES the process. **Measured:** the one SIGUSR1 sent to his live console tonight, to see why the vault lamp
was frozen, took it down; it was relaunched through `tv/start_tvd_mac.sh` in about 9 s with the Screen Recording grant
intact. **Now** `chain=False` - the dump prints and the console carries on; nothing else in the tree handles SIGUSR1.
Law: `tv/test_a_stack_dump_never_kills_the_console.py` - a child imports the real module, parks a worker thread,
signals itself and must print ALIVE with a stack naming the parked worker. 3 red-proofs RED (`chain=True` dies with
exit -30, `all_threads=False` names only the signalled thread, no registration dies stackless). Skipped with its reason
where there is no SIGUSR1 (Windows).

(114 names, Crescent Moon among them) the case runs and passes; where the name was never seen it says so and skips.

then says UNKNOWN). The three shell laws use it (the port chooser, the launcher block, the push-line clock); the

**Measured on the ALT, live on v3534** (its console restarted onto af82ff37 at 23:07:59): slices still started only on

ended slice the moment its prover was gone, but the tick it chained was handed no load probe, so `decide()` met
`busy=None` and answered `load-unknown` ("a proof is not started on a guess"). The law for REG-1625 recorded the call
with a fake tick and never asked whether a slice could START - the joint that broke was the one it stubbed. **Now**
the console hands the guard the same `_cpu_busy_pct` its own tick uses and the guard passes it through. Law:

-> the real tick, only the machine faked: idle starts the next slice at once, busy books and waits, an unmeasured load
